v1.0.16 · GitHub ↗ · MIT

bdo-toolkit

A Python library that passively decodes live or recorded Black Desert traffic into structured results. It never sends anything to the game.

v1.0.16Python ≥ 3.14NA/EU validated

Install

python -m pip install bdo-toolkit

Windows live capture needs Npcap 1.88 or later; offline replay doesn’t. See Installation & setup for the full checklist.

Workflows

Each is independent — pick by the result you need.

Item eventsDrops, gathering, receipts and storage moves as they happen.LiveCaptureSession→ BDOEvent stream Inventory & storageBetaWhat the game sent during a login or switch, summarised once.CharacterLoadSession→ ItemStateSnapshot Arena of SolareBetaOne leaderboard load, reused for ranks and player stats.capture_solare_snapshot()→ SolareCaptureResult Grind trackingExperimentalMob drops with optional Agris and solo XP, from one capture.GrindSession→ GrindEvent stream Raw server messagesExperimentalEvery server message, opcode-free and undecoded, for protocol research.replay_raw()→ RawMessage stream

Results describe only what appeared while capture ran. Captures can contain endpoints, storage contents and player names — read Capture privacy before sharing them.

Start

Installation & setup

Install the package and prepare the computer for passive live capture, for item, calibration and Arena of Solare workflows.

Install

python -m pip install bdo-toolkit

Installs the bdo_toolkit package, the bdo-toolkit command and the required dependencies.

Live-capture prerequisites

Before any live example

Without a compatible capture backend and permission to observe traffic, live examples, calibration, character-load and Solare capture can’t start.

Passive

Live capture only observes inbound server traffic. It never sends, injects, modifies, delays or automates game traffic.

  • Windows: install Npcap 1.88 or later. Domain-specific requirements live with each live API.
  • Other platforms: use the packet-capture backend available to Scapy. Physical live capture is unverified outside the Windows baseline below.
  • Permissions: run with permission to capture traffic. Elevate only when the driver or local security policy requires it.
  • Timing: start capture before the game action: before collecting or moving an item, logging in or switching characters, or opening the Solare Leaderboard for the first time after a restart.

Network settings: PacketCaptureOptions. No game traffic: find and test capture settings.

Choose live or replay

SourceNeedsUse
Live captureA compatible capture backend, permission to capture and an active game sessionContinuing item activity; inventory at a login or character switch; town storage at the first world load after a fresh launch; live calibration; the first Solare Leaderboard load after a restart
PCAP or PCAPNG replayNo capture driver, adapter or elevated shellRepeatable development, tests, support diagnosis and post-patch verification

Most applications start live. Replay helps when a representative recording already exists, or the same evidence must be analyzed again.

Supported live-capture environment

Opened isn’t visible

Startup means an adapter opened, not that it sees BDO traffic. Drivers, virtual adapters, VPN routing, loss or an encrypted tunnel can leave a run incomplete or silent.

The toolkit reads inbound, unfragmented IPv4/TCP packets.

Validated Windows baseline

Windows live capture requires Npcap 1.88 or later; older versions are unsupported. As of September 3, 2026, maintainer validation covers Windows 11 25H2, Python 3.14.0, Npcap 1.88, Scapy 2.7.0 and a wired Ethernet adapter. Later Npcap releases meet the version floor but aren’t independently validated.

This is a documentation support boundary. The validated machine had WinPcap API-compatible mode on; the toolkit doesn’t know whether that mode is required and never inspects the installed Npcap version. Other operating systems and Npcap modes aren’t part of maintainer validation. Replay uses no Npcap or adapter, but the recording must still contain supported BDO traffic.

Hardware, network card and driver

The live path runs through the physical or virtual adapter, its driver and offload behavior, operating-system routing, the capture backend (Npcap on Windows), Scapy, then the toolkit. Each layer can present the same connection differently, so one known-good network card isn’t a compatibility list for every card or driver.

Choose the options object

One model

LiveCaptureOptions inherits PacketCaptureOptions. Use the parameter name and type the live API documents.

Live APIs build default options internally. Pass an options object only when this computer needs a different adapter, destination IPv4, server-port set, filtering mode or item-event queue size.

WorkflowArgumentTakes
Continuing item eventslive_options=LiveCaptureOptions: every shared packet setting, plus the packet and event queues
Item state, calibration or Arena of Solarecapture_options=PacketCaptureOptions: the shared adapter and packet-selection rules
PCAP or PCAPNG replayneitherReplay opens no adapter. Pass its own ports= only when the recording used a non-default server port

Interfaces and VPN routing

See also

Find settings on Windows · manual adapter settings

An interface is the physical or virtual adapter the capture backend observes. Automatic selection follows the computer’s default IPv4 route with the default BDO server ports; it doesn’t inspect BDO’s own connections. Several adapters, a VPN or a local proxy can need a different interface, local IP or port set.

With a VPN, readable BDO traffic may appear on a virtual adapter. A local proxy such as ExitLag can expose the connection on loopback with a session-specific port. The toolkit can’t decode an encrypted tunnel, or traffic the capture backend can’t see.

Diagnose capture when automatic selection fails

Before you begin

Complete the prerequisites, connect your VPN or routing service and enter a game server. Keep that connection up while you discover and test.

Use this Windows walkthrough when capture starts but receives no game traffic, or after you change adapters, VPNs or routing services. It proposes settings from BDO’s current connections; it doesn’t apply them or prove that packets decode.

Inspect current connections

python -m bdo_toolkit.cli diagnose-capture

It lists grouped settings proposals: interface, local IPv4, server or proxy ports, and the underlying connections. Compatible game connections appear together, for example ports: 8884,8885,8889. Use the values from your own output; proxy ports can change after a reconnect.

Add --json for structured output. If Windows connection inspection times out, retry with --timeout 30; adapter enumeration isn’t covered by the timeout.

Review the proposals

  • game_port: BDO connections on its default server ports. Keep the grouped ports together.
  • local_proxy: BDO connects to a local peer. Check the peer name, then use the reported loopback interface, local IP and proxy ports.
  • other_tcp: other ports, often including 443, which may carry web or authentication traffic. Don’t merge them into a game-port proposal just because the adapter and local IP match.

Several proposals can be valid observations: compare their BDO process ID, adapter, kind and connections before you pick one. A proposal with (no matching adapter) can’t be applied; check Npcap and adapter availability first.

  • no_game: start BDO and retry.
  • no_connections: enter a game server and retry. IPv6-only connections aren’t supported.
  • unavailable: follow the reported inspection error. Discovery supports Windows only.

Apply one proposal

If your application has capture settings, copy the proposal’s interface, local IPv4 and complete port list into them, then restart its capture session. Use the adapter identifier from the output, not a guessed display name. local_ip restricts the inbound destination; it doesn’t select an adapter.

For a Python item listener, save this as capture_with_proposal.py next to a current opcodes.local and run it. It discovers settings again, asks for a proposal and listens for item activity until Ctrl+C.

from bdo_toolkit import capture_live, diagnose_capture

result = diagnose_capture()
for message in result.messages:
    print(message)
if not result.proposals:
    raise SystemExit("No settings proposals. Resolve the diagnostic above and retry.")

for number, proposal in enumerate(result.proposals, 1):
    print(number, proposal.kind, proposal.interface,
          proposal.local_ip, proposal.ports)

try:
    number = int(input("Proposal number: "))
    if not 1 <= number <= len(result.proposals):
        raise ValueError("Proposal number is out of range")
    options = result.proposals[number - 1].to_live_options()
except ValueError as error:
    raise SystemExit(str(error)) from error

try:
    for event in capture_live(
        opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
        live_options=options,
    ):
        print(event)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    pass

For item state, calibration or Solare, build PacketCaptureOptions from the proposal’s interface, local_ip and ports and pass it as capture_options. APIs: diagnose_capture() · CaptureSettingsProposal.

Verify the selected settings

Selected isn’t seen

The endpoint reports what was selected, not whether BDO was visible there. Clean health doesn’t prove the right adapter saw the game.

  1. Start a new capture session with the selected settings, with the VPN and game connection as they were during discovery.
  2. Where the API allows, use an explicit session and read its CaptureEndpoint after startup.
  3. Perform one known in-game action once capture is ready, then check the workflow’s output and, where exposed, its final capture health or acquisition counters.
  4. No packets: follow the acquisition checks. Packets but no item events after a known action: check filters and profile compatibility. Discovery alone can’t tell these apart.

Start

Opcode profile setup

Install the local file that lets item-event and item-state workflows recognize the current patch’s traffic. It’s a decoder profile, not a character or account profile; Arena of Solare doesn’t use one.

Get a profile

Replaces the file

The command can replace opcodes.local; a timestamped backup is kept by default. Use one writer for this path.

The channel can lag

Stable doesn’t update itself and can trail a weekly patch until a maintainer promotes a current profile. Keep manual calibration as your patch-day fallback.

Latest maintained NA/EU profile

For current NA/EU traffic, fetch the latest profile that maintainers captured, verified and promoted:

bdo-toolkit profile fetch https://ychwu.github.io/bdo-toolkit-profiles/channels/na-eu/stable.json --output opcodes.local

It downloads and verifies once; capture never updates the profile in the background. A locally calibrated profile stays on your computer and is never uploaded.

Other sources

→

Calibrate locally Recommended

Rebuild a profile from controlled in-game item transfers when the maintained one is unavailable or stops decoding.

 →

Use a historical profile

Keep the matching profile beside an older PCAP so it replays with its original patch layout.

Use it

Keep it with its data

Live traffic needs a current profile. An older PCAP needs the profile from its own patch.

Pass the path as opcode_profile= whenever an item workflow starts. Quickstart uses the same opcodes.local.

Verify it in game

Loads isn’t current

A file can load cleanly and still be stale after a patch.

Run Quickstart, then gather an item, collect a mob drop or withdraw something from town storage. Check that the printed item ID, quantity and source match what happened.

If a known action prints nothing, fetch the maintained profile again. If the channel isn’t current yet, follow manual calibration.

Quickstart

Run one small Python program, perform an item action in game, and print the first item event the toolkit sees.

Capture one item event

Setup first

Install the package and live-capture support (Installation & setup), then create opcodes.local (Opcode profile setup).

No output?

Zero-event troubleshooting

from bdo_toolkit import LiveCaptureSession

with LiveCaptureSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    print("Listening for item activity...")
    for event in session.events():
        print(event.format_human())
        break
from contextlib import closing

from bdo_toolkit import replay_pcap

with closing(replay_pcap(
    "path/to/session.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
)) as events:
    for event in events:
        print(event.format_human())
        break

Live: run python quickstart.py, then gather an item, collect a mob drop or withdraw something from town storage. Replay: point both paths at a recording and the profile from its patch.

Example outputthe first event
[23:06:01.245] ITEM_RECEIVED source='Gathering' item_id=7003 quantity=6 item_instance=0x6f105b8a3d7294c1

ITEM_RECEIVED means an item entered inventory, and Gathering is the in-game source; then come the raw item ID, quantity and observed instance. Other actions produce other event types and source labels.

Guides

Item events

Listen for item changes as they happen: one BDOEvent per decoded record, filtered down to what your application keeps.

From a game action to Python

Before you begin

Complete Installation & setup and Opcode profile setup.

Lesson files

Clone the repository ↗ and run lessons from its root; pip doesn’t install examples/.

Item activity is a stream of changes observed after the listener starts: gathering, a monster drop, a storage withdrawal or a deposit. It doesn’t reconstruct what inventory or storage already held; for that, see Inventory & town storage.

game action→capture_live()→BDOEvent→EventFilter→your code or writer
item_receivedlive
An item receipt or inventory update decoded. source can be Gathering, Mob Drop, Storage or another known receipt context.
storage_deltalive
A live addition to town storage was proven. source names a proven origin such as Player Inventory or Worker Production, and storage_id names the destination. Withdrawals are item_received from Storage.
loot_previewlive · optional
An item was shown in a preview before collection. Not proof of receipt; needs separately calibrated preview support.

Most applications start with event_type, source, item_id and quantity. Time, enhancement, storage identity, formatting and serialization are on the same object. The toolkit returns raw game IDs; item names and market data are yours to supply.

Pick the capture control you need

Quiet isn’t empty

After a weekly patch, a stale profile can load normally and decode nothing. Check diagnostics and health and zero-event troubleshooting before treating silence as game state.

ApplicationStart withYou get
A blocking scriptcapture_live()A continuing iterator of BDOEvent values
A UI, service or worker threadLiveCaptureSession.events()The same stream, with explicit start, stop, polling and health
An asyncio applicationAsyncLiveCaptureSession.events()The same events as an async iterator

EventFilter decides delivery once an event is decoded and any storage source is classified. Event writers turn a delivered event into a console line or a JSONL record; they don’t capture traffic.

Guides/Item events

Watch live item activity

Run a continuing listener, make a few known item changes in game, and match each delivered BDOEvent to what you did.

Run the finished example

Needs

A current opcodes.local in the repo root. Source on GitHub ↗

python examples/live_transfer_log.py

Wait for Listening for confirmed item activity, keep the terminal open and return to the game:

  1. Gather an item or collect a monster drop.
  2. Withdraw one item from town storage.
  3. Optionally deposit an item, or wait for worker production to reach storage.
  4. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal when you’re done.

Read the result

No output?

Zero-event troubleshooting

Reference

BDOEvent · event types & sources

stdoutrepresentative · application fields only
[09:35:41.102] ITEM_RECEIVED source='Gathering' item_id=7003 quantity=6
[09:35:48.417] ITEM_RECEIVED source='Storage' item_id=15156 quantity=1
[09:36:02.884] STORAGE_DELTA source='Player Inventory' destination='Velia' storage_id=0x00000005 item_id=7003 quantity=5
[09:36:18.513] STORAGE_DELTA source='Worker Production' destination='Heidel' storage_id=0x00000020 item_id=4003 quantity=20
[09:36:24.190] STORAGE_DELTA destination='Heidel' storage_id=0x00000020 item_id=7307 quantity=8

The last line has no source: the live addition was proven, but its origin wasn’t resolved.

MemberTells you
event_typeWhich change decoded, such as item_received or storage_delta
sourceThe known origin, producing system or context. Storage additions use Player Inventory, Worker Production, or None when unresolved
storage_id · storage_nameThe numeric destination, and its optional town name, on storage events
item_idThe exact raw game item ID. Enhanced variants can have distinct encoded IDs
quantityThe amount in this change, not the resulting inventory or storage total

The same object has timestamp_text and timestamp_iso, enhancement fields such as base_item_id and enhancement_level, format_human() for display and to_dict() for structured output.

Build it yourself

When it stops

The loop runs until Ctrl+C, a capture failure, or a capture_seconds deadline.

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

confirmed_activity = EventFilter(
    event_types={"item_received", "storage_delta"},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=confirmed_activity,
):
    fields = [event.event_type]
    if event.source is not None:
        fields.append(event.source)
    if event.storage_id is not None:
        destination = event.storage_name or (
            f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{event.storage_id:08x})"
        )
        fields.extend((destination, f"0x{event.storage_id:08x}"))
    fields.extend((event.item_id, event.quantity))
    print(*fields)
  1. EventFilter keeps the two confirmed activity types. Character-load records, unresolved neutral records and loot_preview stay out.
  2. capture_live() starts passive capture and blocks while it waits for traffic.
  3. Each pass receives one BDOEvent; your loop decides whether to print, count, store or forward it.

Guides/Item events

Track mob drops

Keep confirmed items collected from defeated monsters and total each raw item ID for the current run.

Run the finished example

Needs

A current opcodes.local in the repo root. Source on GitHub ↗

python examples/live_mob_drops.py
  1. Leave the counter running and return to the game.
  2. Defeat monsters and collect their drops.
  3. Press Ctrl+C when you’re done.

Read the result

Current contents

For what the character holds now, use Inventory & town storage.

stdoutrepresentative · totals reset on restart
Collect mob drops in game. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
item_id=1000707 quantity=1 total_this_run=1
item_id=1000707 quantity=2 total_this_run=3
item_id=44195 quantity=1 total_this_run=1

quantity is the amount in one observed receipt. total_this_run adds those receipts for this process run; it isn’t the character’s inventory quantity.

Build it yourself

Matching

Criteria combine with AND; values inside one criterion are alternatives. Strings match exactly, case included. Rules.

from collections import Counter

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

totals: Counter[int] = Counter()
mob_drops = EventFilter(
    event_types={"item_received"},
    sources={"Mob Drop"},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=mob_drops,
):
    totals[event.item_id] += event.quantity
    print(event.item_id, event.quantity, totals[event.item_id])

An event passes only if it is an item_received and its source is Mob Drop. The Counter is your application’s state; the toolkit keeps delivering ordinary BDOEvent values.

Extend it

  • Show more per drop: timestamp_text, base_item_id, enhancement_level and enhancement.
  • Keep only selected drops by adding item_ids to the filter.
  • Keep the run by passing each event to JsonlEventWriter.

python examples/live_worker_productions.py
  1. In the worker window, pick an active task whose output you recognize and note its destination town.
  2. Start the listener before the task finishes, then keep playing.
  3. Once the production reaches town storage, read the terminal line and press Ctrl+C.

Read the result

Fails closed

If the captured messages don’t prove worker origin, the addition doesn’t pass this filter. Silence doesn’t prove that no production finished.

See also

Source labels · storage locations · origin evidence

stdoutrepresentative · one confirmed addition
Waiting for worker production to reach town storage. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
source='Worker Production' destination='Heidel' storage_id=0x00000020 item_id=4003 quantity=20

Read cause and destination separately:

  • source names the inferred producing system. It’s classifier output, not a raw context-byte label.
  • storage_id names the destination; storage_name is optional display text. An unregistered key keeps its number with storage_name=None, so you can show UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x…) without inventing a name.
  • quantity is the amount added, not the storage total. Multi-record productions can also carry record_index and record_count.

The event carries no worker identity, production node, task name or facility.

Build it yourself

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

worker_productions = EventFilter(
    event_types={"storage_delta"},
    sources={"Worker Production"},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=worker_productions,
):
    destination = event.storage_name or (
        f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{event.storage_id:08x})"
        if event.storage_id is not None
        else "unknown"
    )
    print(
        event.source,
        destination,
        event.storage_id,
        event.item_id,
        event.quantity,
    )

storage_delta proves live storage activity. Requiring sources={"Worker Production"} then keeps the additions whose bounded classifier evidence points to worker production. Decoder problems still reach you through diagnostics.

Guides/Item events

Filter item activity

Choose which decoded BDOEvent values reach your application, from delivery presets to exact multi-field rules.

Choose the stream you want

None is the API’s default

Live APIs treat event_filter=None as activity(); replay treats it as everything. An explicit filter replaces either default.

Reference

EventFilter · event types & sources

Filtering happens after decoding and storage-origin classification. Pass one filter to the capture API, and only matching events enter your loop.

You needPass
Ordinary live item activitynothing, or EventFilter.activity()
One exact activity streamEventFilter(...) with every criterion you need
Every decoded eventEventFilter.all()
Low-level character-load recordsEventFilter.snapshot_records()

Use a preset or its explicit form

Both tabs build equal immutable filters. Use the preset when its meaning is what you want; use the constructor when you add or change criteria.

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter

activity = EventFilter.activity()
from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter

activity = EventFilter(
    event_types={"loot_preview", "item_received", "storage_delta"},
)

activity() leaves out character-load snapshot events and neutral inventory_record and storage_record values.

Combine exact criteria

Raw IDs

Enhanced items can have different raw IDs, and item_ids doesn’t match base_item_id.

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

heidel_worker_items = EventFilter(
    event_types={"storage_delta"},
    sources={"Worker Production"},
    storage_ids={0x0020},
    item_ids={4607, 7003},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=heidel_worker_items,
):
    print(event.item_id, event.quantity)

Values inside one criterion are alternatives: item 4607 or 7003. Criteria add up, so the event must also be a storage_delta to Heidel with worker-production evidence.

  • event_types matches exact event types.
  • sources matches the inferred origin or context, such as Worker Production.
  • storage_ids matches the numeric destination, such as Heidel’s 0x0020.
  • item_ids matches exact raw item IDs.

Helper methods

Besides the three presets, two helpers:

  • EventFilter.from_values(...) is a named constructor with the same inputs. It doesn’t combine or chain filters.
  • filter.allows(event) tests an event your code already holds. Capture and replay call it for you.
from bdo_toolkit import BDOEvent, EventFilter

potato_receipts = EventFilter.from_values(
    event_types={"item_received"},
    item_ids={7003},
)


def should_keep(event: BDOEvent) -> bool:
    return potato_receipts.allows(event)

Common mistakes

  • Wrap one value in a collection: storage_ids={0x0020}. A bare int, str or bytes raises TypeError.
  • None leaves a criterion unrestricted; an empty iterable rejects every event.
  • sources matches origin or context labels such as Worker Production and Player Inventory. For a town, use storage_ids.
  • An explicit filter doesn’t inherit the activity preset: a source-only or storage-only filter can match non-activity records. Add event_types to stay activity-only.
  • Filters are immutable. Build a new one when the policy changes.

Exact constructor and validation: EventFilter. The full delivery pipeline: Item-event internals.

Guides/Item events

Item-event internals

How captured TCP becomes a delivered BDOEvent: framing, fail-closed storage classification, delivery order and bounded live capture.

From captured TCP to your code

Public contracts

Capture functions · LiveCaptureSession · diagnostics and health · BDOEvent

captured TCP→per-flow reassembly→message framing→profile decode→storage classification→EventFilter→BDOEvent

TCP packets are only transport: one packet can hold several BDO messages, and one message can span several packets. The toolkit reassembles each server-to-client flow before it looks for complete length-framed messages. The selected profile then supplies the opcode and byte geometry to decode item records from a message.

TermHere it means
PacketOne captured TCP segment; never an event boundary
MessageOne complete reassembled BDO wire unit, with its own length and opcode
RecordOne item entry decoded from a message; a repeated message can hold several
EventThe immutable BDOEvent delivered after classification and filtering

Each event keeps its message’s timestamp, length, opcode and record position, plus a provisional per-flow stream position when available. None of that makes the stream a complete inventory ledger.

Framing and profile selection fail closed

Valid isn’t current

A profile can be valid JSON and still stale for the patch. Static validation proves its shape; only traffic proves its opcodes and geometry still match.

Recovery

Opcode profile setup · calibration · DecoderHealth

Capture that attaches midstream starts unsynchronized. A generic message boundary needs framing evidence: a known opcode, an exact standalone frame or consecutive plausible lengths. Retransmission and out-of-order delivery are resolved per directional flow; bytes the capture missed can’t be rebuilt.

One explicit, immutable profile compiles into runtime layouts, and a candidate must satisfy its layout’s message length and item geometry. Receipts, loot previews and storage records need an independent top-level boundary; a nested signature alone can’t produce an event. Inventory hydration can also recover from two fully decoded, exactly adjacent wrappers on the same TCP flow generation, even across a sequence-number wrap. A differently segmented retransmission can’t give already-framed payload new boundaries.

Overlapping same-opcode loot-preview layouts and contradictory storage geometry are rejected. Where an inventory-transfer layout supports structural validation, a failed marker, instance or repeated-record check is final: those bytes aren’t retried through weaker stride decoding.

Storage records take a classification detour

See also

Event types · source labels · origin evidence

Most events go straight to delivery. Storage records first pass two stateful classifiers, because the decoded item fields alone don’t prove a live addition versus existing character-load state.

decoded storage record→worker or manual origin evidence→hydration-cohort evidence→final event type→EventFilter
EvidenceBecomes
A confirmed worker companion chainstorage_delta, source="Worker Production". Worker evidence beats a nearby manual signal
No worker chain, but a calibrated matching source decrementstorage_delta, source="Player Inventory"
Live activity proven without worker or manual evidencestorage_delta, source=None
A multi-destination character-load cohortstorage_snapshot, source=None
No independent live or hydration proofneutral storage_record, source=None

The origin classifier goes first, so real deposits don’t inherit a nearby hydration epoch. Hydration then groups still-neutral records by TCP flow generation, opcode, timing and destination diversity. Neither stage infers cause from a town name or a single context byte.

EventFilter runs after both stages: an activity filter sees an evidence-promoted storage_delta, and sources sees the final label. Decoder diagnostics stay out of band and bypass the filter.

Wire time and delivery order can differ

Order by timestamp

Iteration order isn’t global wire order. Correlate by timestamp and keep the original when you buffer or sort.

Origin and hydration decisions use bounded lookahead. While a storage event waits for evidence, a later non-storage event can be delivered first; the storage event keeps its earlier timestamp.

Equal timestamps and separate TCP flows still have no universal total order. extra["stream_sequence"] is provisional per-flow metadata, not a cross-flow ordering key.

Current bounds and backpressure

Not promises

Current safeguards, not compatibility guarantees. Queue sizes are configurable through LiveCaptureOptions; classifier and flow limits stay internal.

StateCurrent boundWhy it matters
Raw-packet handoff4,096 packets by default; the native callback never blocksOverflow records CaptureIntegrityError and shuts capture down fail-closed
Decoded-event delivery1,024 events by default; a full queue applies backpressureA slow consumer can eventually fill the raw queue. Hand expensive work to your own queue
TCP flow state64 active flows, 300-second idle timeoutEvictions show in flow_state_evictions
Idle TCP gap serviceThe packet worker advances the clock at drained queue boundariesBytes already accepted for decoding are processed before an idle timeout abandons their gap
Worker-origin correlation32 following complete messages or 2 seconds; at most 64 pending operations per flow, 4,096 in totalUnconfirmed or contested evidence fails neutral instead of growing without limit
Manual-origin correlationThe two most recent earlier complete messages on the same flowA calibrated decrement must match; a coincidental quantity can’t override instance-aware geometry
Hydration classification30-second inventory-anchored epoch; storage bursts split after a 0.5-second gap or 1 second in total8 destinations prove an anchored cohort. The storage-only fallback needs 17 destinations and at least 8 records
Pending hydration records10,000 eventsAn oversized unproven cohort flushes as neutral records instead of taking unbounded memory

Filtering doesn’t save capture work: candidate traffic is still framed and decoded before values are matched. The runtime can skip the origin-correlation graph when the filter can’t deliver storage events and no origin_observer is set.

Consumption, deadlines and finalization

Retry the same owner

If cleanup_incomplete is true, the original session still owns native or worker resources. Retry its stop(); a new session doesn’t finish the first cleanup.

Exact rules

Sync session · async session · Asyncio integration

APIWork beginsFailures surface
replay_pcap(), capture_live()Arguments bind at the call; profile loading, capture and decoding begin with iterationOn the first or a later iteration. Buffered events can drain before a retained background failure is re-raised
LiveCaptureSessionThe constructor validates inputs; start() opens capture and the worker pipelineLifecycle and consumption methods re-raise the first retained failure on their documented timing
AsyncLiveCaptureSessionThe same session boundaries, run on a private workerCancellation and awaited methods keep the synchronous failure and cleanup contract

A live capture_seconds deadline belongs to the session and keeps running while your code pauses after a yielded event. On stop, capture joins, every accepted packet ahead of the worker sentinel is decoded, TCP reassembly finishes, and pending origin and hydration decisions finalize. Shutdown-finalized events stay drainable before a retained error is raised.

Read the right reliability signal

capture_live()

It exposes diagnostics but not its session’s health. For integrity decisions, own a LiveCaptureSession or its async form.

See also

No item activity appears · safety & privacy

SignalAnswers
session.endpointWhich adapter, local address and capture filter were selected?
session.healthDid local capture or TCP report packet loss, queue overflow, a gap reset or flow eviction?
session.decoder_healthDid observed storage traffic validate against the profile?
on_diagnostic=Which deduplicated storage-decoder warning explains incompatibility or an unresolved destination?

The signals are independent: a locally clean capture can still use a stale profile, and storage_status="not_observed" proves nothing either way. Values read mid-capture are observations; use the final post-stop values when completeness matters.

Guides

Inventory & town storage

Capture one character load and query a finite snapshot of the inventory and town storage the game sent. Any login or switch gives inventory; the first world load after a fresh launch also gives storage.

From character load to one snapshot

Before you begin

Complete Installation & setup and Opcode profile setup.

Timing

Storage needs the first world load. As of the September 3, 2026 NA/EU patch, full town storage arrives only when the first character enters the world after launch. Later switches resend inventory only.

Lesson files

Clone the repository ↗ and run lessons from its root; pip doesn’t install examples/.

CharacterLoadSession passively captures whatever records the game sends, and stop() assembles them into one immutable ItemStateSnapshot. It doesn’t update after capture ends.

CharacterLoadSession.stop()→ItemStateSnapshot→inventory or storages→your query
Object pathWhat it holdsReference
snapshot.inventoryOrdinary stacks, known balances and provisional container viewsInventorySnapshotSummary
snapshot.storagesEvery observed destination; current contents only for towns in the latest sweepStorageContents → StorageSnapshotSummary

Selection is conservative: only the latest inventory generation and storage sweep become current state. A validated empty inventory still counts as observed, so an earlier character’s items are never carried forward. The rules: Item-state internals.

Capture a character load

Start capture before the right load and stop once the world settles. Any login or switch gives inventory; the first world load after a fresh launch also gives town storage.

Run the finished example

Timing

Pick the load for the data. A switch is enough for inventory. For town storage on NA/EU, restart the game and start capture before the first world load; later switches don’t resend storage.

Needs

A current opcodes.local in the repo root. Source on GitHub ↗

python examples/live_character_load_snapshot.py
  1. Wait until the terminal says capture started.
  2. Log in or switch characters for inventory, or make the first world load after a fresh launch for storage.
  3. Once the character is playable and the world has settled, press Enter.

The example checks the profile path, handles Ctrl+C and prints format_item_state() for troubleshooting.

Read the result

Private output

The formatter prints profile paths, balances, towns and storage counts. Review it before sharing.

stdoutcounts vary by load
CHARACTER LOAD SNAPSHOT DIAGNOSTIC
Storage decoder: compatible (... observed wrappers decoded)
Hydration packets detected; trigger is unclassified (initial login vs character switch).
INVENTORY SNAPSHOT
  183 serialized records: 179 occupied item stacks + 4 currency balances
STORAGE SNAPSHOT
  27/34 known destinations observed
  642 unique occupied item stacks from ... decoded snapshot records

The trigger is never classified: a login and a switch look the same on the wire. Registered towns missing from the capture are reported, not assumed empty.

Build it yourself

Types used

CharacterLoadSessionItemStateSnapshotformat_item_state()

Limitations

coverage, identity_complete and warnings say what the snapshot can’t prove.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import CharacterLoadSession

with CharacterLoadSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    input(
        "Capture started. For storage, enter the world for the first time "
        "after a fresh game launch; a later character switch captures "
        "inventory only. Press Enter after the world has settled: "
    )
    snapshot = session.stop()

print(f"Hydration detected: {snapshot.hydration_detected}")
print(f"Inventory observed: {snapshot.inventory.hydration_observed}")
print(f"Storage decoder: {snapshot.decoder_health.storage_status}")
  1. Construction loads and pins the profile for this one session.
  2. Entering the block calls start(), which returns once passive capture is ready.
  3. You make the load. No marker ends it, so pressing Enter is your stop decision.
  4. stop() drains capture, assembles state and returns the snapshot. Context exit only cleans up.

The three prints separate any item-state evidence (hydration_detected), inventory hydration (inventory.hydration_observed) and storage-profile compatibility (decoder_health.storage_status). Application data lives in snapshot.inventory and snapshot.storages.

Build it yourself

Types used

CharacterLoadSessionInventorySnapshotSummarySnapshotItem

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import CharacterLoadSession

with CharacterLoadSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    input("Log in or switch characters, then press Enter when settled: ")
    snapshot = session.stop()

inventory = snapshot.inventory
if not inventory.hydration_observed:
    raise RuntimeError("No character inventory was observed")
if not inventory.items:
    print("No occupied inventory stacks were observed")
for item in inventory.items:
    label = item.container_name or "Unclassified"
    print(item.item_id, item.quantity, label)

stop() returns an ItemStateSnapshot; its inventory is an InventorySnapshotSummary, and inventory.items holds one SnapshotItem per retained ordinary stack.

Pick the right query

Reference

Every field and helper: Inventory contents.

You needUse
Every ordinary stackitems
Stacks of one item IDrecords_for(item_id)
The total of one item IDquantity_for(item_id)
Known wallet balancescurrency(), currency_balances
Provisional groupscontainers, container(), container_named()
  • occupied_stacks counts records; it doesn’t sum quantities.
  • hydration_observed=True with empty items means the latest generation was observed empty.
  • Tuple order isn’t slot order, and known balances aren’t part of items.
  • container_name is provisional; persist container_code when identity matters.
  • Records without instance identity are left out, not guessed. You get item IDs, not names.

Read the result

This prints real storage contents. Review the terminal before sharing.

Not capacity

occupied_stacks counts retained records. Storage capacity isn’t decoded.

stdoutids redacted
HEIDEL CONTENTS
183 observed occupied stacks
item_id=<redacted> quantity=<redacted>
item_id=<redacted> quantity=<redacted>
… 178 more stacks …
item_id=<redacted> quantity=<redacted>

An empty items tuple alone doesn’t prove the town is empty. There are three distinct outcomes:

Missing

storage is None

Not returned by this capture.

Stale

current_state_observed is False

Seen only in an earlier inferred sweep.

Empty

current_empty is True

Current state proved it empty.

Use named() for a user-facing name (case-insensitive) and by_id() when persisting — numeric storage_id is authoritative.

Build it yourself

Types used

CharacterLoadSessionStorageContentsStorageSnapshotSummary

Cross-town

find_item(), total_quantity(), locations_for()

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import CharacterLoadSession

town_name = "Heidel"

with CharacterLoadSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    input("Enter the world for the first time, then press Enter: ")
    snapshot = session.stop()

if snapshot.decoder_health.storage_status != "compatible":
    raise RuntimeError("Town-storage decoding is unavailable")

storage = snapshot.storages.named(town_name)
if storage is None:
    raise LookupError(f"{town_name} was not returned by this snapshot")
if not storage.current_state_observed:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{town_name} has no selected current state")

if storage.current_empty:
    print(f"{town_name}: explicitly observed empty")
else:
    for item in storage.items:
        print(item.item_id, item.quantity)

The observed total isn’t an account total. A zero means no retained match in that source, and missing coverage, unavailable storage decoding or identity-unresolved records can lower it. The example reports an unavailable source and prints the combined total only when both sources were observed.

Build it yourself

Records, not totals

For individual stacks use inventory records_for() or storage find_item().

Gaps

ItemStateCoverage · item-state internals

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import CharacterLoadSession

item_id = 7003

with CharacterLoadSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    input("Enter the world for the first time, then press Enter when settled: ")
    snapshot = session.stop()

if not snapshot.hydration_detected:
    raise RuntimeError("No character-load item state was detected")

inventory_total = None
if snapshot.inventory.hydration_observed:
    inventory_total = snapshot.inventory.quantity_for(item_id)
    print(f"Character inventory: {inventory_total}")
else:
    print("Character inventory: unavailable")

storage_total = None
if snapshot.decoder_health.storage_status == "compatible":
    storage_total = snapshot.storages.total_quantity(item_id)
    print(f"Town storage: {storage_total}")
    for storage in snapshot.storages.locations_for(item_id):
        label = storage.name or f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{storage.storage_id:08x})"
        print(f"  {label}: {storage.quantity_for(item_id)}")
else:
    print("Town storage: unavailable")

if inventory_total is not None and storage_total is not None:
    print(f"Observed total: {inventory_total + storage_total}")

inventory.quantity_for() totals the ID across ordinary inventory stacks. storages.total_quantity() totals it across selected current town storage, and locations_for() returns the destinations that hold it.

Guides/Inventory & town storage

Item-state internals

How character-load traffic becomes one observational ItemStateSnapshot: atomic decoding, generation and sweep selection, identity merging and fail-closed limits.

From traffic to one snapshot

Public contracts

CharacterLoadSession · ItemStateSnapshot · inventory and storage contents

Shared pipeline

Item-event internals · event types

captured TCP→framed messages→snapshot records and empty envelopes→generation and sweep selection→instance merge→ItemStateSnapshot

Character-load decoding reuses the item-event engine for TCP reassembly, framing, profile validation and low-level records. Inventory hydration becomes inventory_snapshot. Storage passes through neutral classification and becomes storage_snapshot only when hydration evidence is strong enough.

The assembler also reads selected raw envelopes. A valid count-zero wrapper holds no item record, so its envelope is the only evidence that an inventory group or a town is explicitly empty.

Assembly runs once, at stop() or at end of file. The result is immutable and never applies later item events.

Inventory batches are validated atomically

The profile supplies the opcode, the one-record base length and the item, quantity, context and instance geometry. For a multi-record wrapper, runtime finds a plausible declared count in the prefix and derives the stride from message length, base length and count. The division must be exact, every offset must line up, and every item ID, quantity and instance must validate.

One failing record rejects the whole wrapper. There is no valid-looking prefix and no marker-scan fallback.

Container and slot metadata are a weaker, separate inference: first a record-tail window, then a wrapper-header column, both over complete sibling groups and recognized raw codes. An ambiguous layout or unknown code withholds container metadata for that opcode but keeps valid records in unclassified_records. A known balance needs both the container code and the item ID.

Storage uses stronger finite-capture evidence

See also

Storage classification · storage locations

Wrapper geometry is profile-driven: the calibrated destination and count fields must agree with message length and full record validation. The numeric destination is kept even without a registry name; no other field is ever substituted.

The live item-event stream leaves an unproven storage group neutral. The item-state assembler has more evidence — a selected inventory boundary, retained count-zero envelopes and the surrounding sweep — so it can prove sparse hydration from an inventory-anchored cohort, or fold timing-split neutral groups into an already proven sweep.

That reconciliation never crosses a confirmed live storage mutation, and stays within one TCP flow generation, storage opcode, bounded inventory epoch and inferred sweep. Live item events keep their fail-neutral behavior.

How current state is selected

StageCurrent inferenceSelected result
Inventory generationA new TCP flow generation, or more than one second between record-bearing or count-zero inventory wrappers, starts another generationOnly the latest is assembled. An empty latest generation clears earlier items and still anchors its storage epoch.
Storage destination blockA change of destination, flow/opcode or empty state, or a gap over one second, closes the blockTightly timed chunks for one destination stay one block
Storage sweepThe first previously closed destination seen again starts another sweepThe latest sweep becomes current state

A selected count-zero block clears earlier items for that destination. A destination seen only in an earlier sweep stays for provenance with current_state_observed=False, and its old items are withheld — safer than carrying stale contents into a sweep that may itself be partial.

With neither an inventory record nor a count-zero inventory wrapper there is no inventory boundary. The assembler then keeps all storage diagnostics, uses only the latest sweep for contents, records generation_selection="all_observed_storage_no_inventory_boundary" and warns that the evidence may span several loads.

Instance identity controls merging

Order

Tuples are sorted for deterministic output. That isn’t inventory-slot or storage-slot order.

Inventory is keyed by the decoded item instance, storage by the storage instance within one selected destination block. Repeats of the same opaque identity collapse to the latest record; diagnostics keep the raw and duplicate counts.

A record without its calibrated eight-byte instance never gets a synthetic key. It shows up in missing-identity diagnostics but is left out of stacks, counts, totals, balance interpretation and duplicate inference, so a damaged layout can’t invent state.

Completion stays observational

No end marker

No completion marker is decoded, nor login versus switch, nor trustworthy capacity. Treat a snapshot as observed evidence, not an account database.

SignalProvesDoesn’t prove
hydration_detectedInventory hydration was observed, storage records decoded, or a storage summary retainedThat the load finished
identity_completeNo retained record lacked an observed instanceThat every expected record or destination arrived
decoder_healthObserved storage traffic matched the profile and registryThat storage was fully captured; not_observed is inconclusive
coverageSpecific missing-identity, registry and sweep gapsAccount-wide completeness or a protocol end marker

Current bounds and inference thresholds Optional referenceShow detailsHide details

Implementation safeguards and inference thresholds, not protocol promises.

MechanismCurrent value or rule
Inventory-generation splitNew TCP flow generation, or more than 1 second between consecutive inventory messages
Storage destination-block splitDestination, flow/opcode or empty state changes, or more than 1 second between groups
Inventory-anchored storage epoch30 seconds; sparse finite proof needs at least 8 distinct destinations and at least one validated empty envelope
Storage hydration burstSplit after a 0.5-second gap between groups, or 1 second in total
Relevant framed evidence10,000 retained frames by default
Snapshot records50,000 retained records by default
Relevant raw bytes64 MiB retained by default

The accumulator checks before retaining an over-limit frame or record and raises ItemStateCaptureLimitError — never a silently truncated snapshot. Defaults and exception fields: capture limits.

Patch-recovery boundary

See also

Calibration boundary · item state is incomplete

Calibration can update opcodes, base lengths, record spacing and the item, quantity, instance, destination and count positions. Runtime then derives the multi-record stride, the inventory count and container metadata from them.

A redesigned record, a new count encoding, a changed destination meaning or a changed hydration relationship needs decoder work. Ambiguity fails closed — rejected frames, missing metadata, neutral records, incompatible decoder health or no snapshot — never a guessed state.

Guides

Calibration

Keep item decoding current after a patch: install a maintained profile when one exists, or calibrate your own from controlled in-game actions.

Why calibration exists

Before you begin

For live calibration, complete Installation & setup. For the maintained option, see the latest NA/EU profile.

Lesson files

Clone the repository ↗ and run lessons from its root; pip doesn’t install examples/.

Item decoding uses an explicit local profile that says where current-patch messages carry item IDs, quantities, instances, storage destinations and repeated records. A weekly patch can move those layouts, and the old file can still load normally while a listener quietly produces nothing.

Calibration watches a known item while you perform controlled game actions, then derives message specs from that evidence. Capture and analysis work without a usable old profile and write nothing; saving the result is a separate decision.

Choose how to recover after a patch

Verify every patch

Every weekly patch needs verification, not necessarily calibration. A running listener pins its profile, so start a fresh one to check a new file.

A maintained profile isn’t generated automatically: a maintainer captures current traffic, verifies it and promotes it. Right after maintenance, the stable channel can be missing or still point at the previous patch.

→

Calibrate locally No downtime

Rebuild the profile as soon as you can do the controlled storage actions, without waiting for anyone to publish.

 →

Use the maintained profile

Fetch it once a current profile has been promoted.

Either way, start a fresh live item-activity logger afterward and perform one known item action.

From evidence to a working profile

One call

calibrate_and_update() does both steps and applies the same three-family readiness gate before touching the profile.

CalibrationSession.stop()→CalibrationResult→update_profile()→ProfileUpdate→fresh listener

stop() analyzes the retained frames and returns a read-only CalibrationResult. There’s no global ok flag, because success is judged per profile family: events_found names the promoted families and specs holds their layouts.

update_profile() is the separate write step. Its ProfileUpdate reports written, added, replaced_events and backup_path. A successful write still needs a fresh runtime check.

The walkthroughs use the two-step API so you can inspect the recovered families before deciding to write.

Know the workflow boundary

Passive

Calibration never moves items or touches the game. In these walkthroughs only update_profile() changes the local file.

Reference

Calibration functions · CalibrationSession · profile updates

WorkflowEvidence you provideProfile scope
Storage transfersControlled deposits and a withdrawal of one known unstackable itemTransfer, destination and manual-deposit evidence; default action="auto"
Loot previewOne known item shown in a preview windowOptional LOOT_PREVIEW; explicit action="loot-preview"
Arena of SolareA Leaderboard loadA separate structural classifier; doesn’t use the item profile

Default writes keep unrelated families and back up an existing file before an eligible change. Calibration can recover moved opcodes and record positions, but not a fundamentally redesigned item record, count encoding, destination identity or evidence relationship.

Guides/Calibration

Manual calibration after a patch

Rebuild the item profile yourself with three controlled storage moves, then verify both transfer directions in a fresh listener.

Calibrate in three moves

Needs

A repository checkout; run from its root so calibration and verification share opcodes.local. Source on GitHub ↗

Prepare five unstackable items

Why quantity 1

Each serialized record is one unstackable item, even when four or five move together.

This guide uses five Magic Crystal of Infinity - Skill, raw item ID 15156: cheap, widely available and unstackable. Another unstackable item works too; set ITEM_ID to its raw ID.

  • Use five matching copies of the item.
  • Put all five in character inventory and none in the chosen storage.
  • Pick one unambiguous registered town, such as Velia, Heidel, Calpheon City or Olvia.
  • Don’t use Muzgar, Velandir, Yukjo Street, Godu Village or Bukpo.

Run the example and make the moves

Writes opcodes.local

Only after the required transfer evidence passes. Unrelated families are kept and an existing file is backed up; an incomplete result writes nothing.

python examples/live_calibrate_profile.py

Wait for the prompt before touching storage:

stdoutthe opening prompt
Listening in the background.
Perform the following in-game actions yourself while capture remains open.
Use one unambiguous town such as Velia, Heidel, Calpheon City, or Olvia.
Do not use Muzgar, Velandir, Yukjo Street, Godu Village, or Bukpo.
Using unstackable item 15156 (per-record quantity 1):
deposit one item, then deposit the remaining four,
then withdraw all five matching items in one action.
Press Enter when all three moves are done...

Make each move while the prompt waits

Move only these five crystals. The example keeps listening while the terminal waits for Enter.

Read the result

Progress isn’t proof

session.frames_collected is live progress, not a completeness counter.

stdouta successful run · abridged; frame count and backup name vary
collected 1439 frames
scanned 1439 frames
...
detected direction(s): inventory->storage, storage->inventory
...
wrote opcodes.local
backup at opcodes_backups\opcodes.local.bak.20260823014827341818
...

This confirms both transfer directions and the local write. The backup line appears only when opcodes.local already existed. An incomplete run exits earlier with incomplete transfer profile; missing ... and writes nothing.

  • The analysis result: events_found is the readiness check used here; specs holds the promoted layouts, ignored explains rejections, detected_directions() lists proven directions and retention.truncated flags a cut-off evidence window.
  • The write result: written, path, added, replaced_events and backup_path.
  • result.summary() and update.summary() are readable reports; neither replaces the family check.

What the sequence proves

Stackables won’t do

A stack of five is usually one record with quantity five, so it can’t supply the multi-record evidence.

Depositing one crystal, then four, produces two distinct repeated-record counts; together they prove the storage destination and record-count fields. Withdrawing all five proves the reverse direction. quantity=1 describes each serialized record, not the batch size.

What runtime uses

The transfer runtime needs all three families: INVENTORY_TRANSFER (the withdrawal and receipt path), STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA (destination-storage records) and SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT (manual-deposit evidence). Missing any one makes the calibration incomplete, and the example refuses to write it. SOURCE_CONTAINER_DECREMENT and SOURCE_ITEM_REFERENCE can also appear as audit evidence, but runtime ignores their saved entries. Full contract.

These uppercase names are profile families, not lowercase BDOEvent.event_type values.

Build it yourself

stop() inside the block

Context exit alone only cleans up and discards the unfinished calibration.

from pathlib import Path

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import CalibrationSession, update_profile


profile = Path("opcodes.local")
required = {
    "INVENTORY_TRANSFER",
    "SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT",
    "STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA",
}

with CalibrationSession(item_id=15156, quantity=1) as session:
    input("Deposit 1, deposit 4, withdraw all 5; then press Enter: ")
    result = session.stop()

missing = required - result.events_found
if missing:
    raise RuntimeError(f"incomplete calibration: {sorted(missing)}")

update = update_profile(result, profile)
print(result.summary())
print(update.summary())
  1. The constructor declares the known per-record value; action="auto" is the default and analyzes both directions.
  2. Entering the context starts capture; stop() returns the result.
  3. The code checks events_found, because nonempty specs doesn’t prove every required family was recovered.
  4. update_profile() does the separate file write and returns a ProfileUpdate.

Verify both directions

Still quiet?

Fix an incomplete calibration. Async version: async_calibrate_profile.py ↗

From the repository root, start a new process so it loads the updated file:

python examples/live_transfer_log.py
  1. Wait until the logger says it’s listening.
  2. Deposit one calibration crystal into the same allowed town.
  3. Withdraw it again.
stdoutrepresentative · a fresh capture with the rebuilt profile
[09:42:11.038] STORAGE_DELTA source='Player Inventory' destination='Velia' storage_id=0x00000005 item_id=15156 quantity=1
[09:42:14.721] ITEM_RECEIVED source='Storage' item_id=15156 quantity=1

Both lines together verify the practical storage-addition and withdrawal paths.

Guides/Calibration

Add loot-preview support

Optionally teach the item profile to recognize what a gathering or manual-loot window offers, before anything is collected.

What it detects

A preview isn’t a receipt

The window can close without anything being collected. For proof an item entered inventory, use item_received.

The game can show an Item List before collection, for example after gathering or when you manually loot a defeated mob. Loot-preview support recognizes the traffic that fills that window and delivers a loot_preview event when it appears. It reports the offered item, not whether the window is open.

It’s optional and doesn’t affect detecting items entering inventory, which uses the separate item_received path. Skip this page unless your application needs to know what the preview showed.

Choose a known preview

The example targets Potato, raw item ID 7003. Use a repeatable preview you know shows Potato, or set ITEM_ID and ITEM_NAME to the exact item your preview shows.

The displayed amount varies, so the example uses quantity=None and anchors on the item ID. No town storage or five-crystal sequence is involved.

Run the finished example

Writes opcodes.local

Only the loot-preview scope is replaced; transfer families are kept and an existing file is backed up. A missing preview writes nothing.

Needs

Run from the repository root. Source on GitHub ↗

python examples/live_calibrate_loot_preview.py
  1. Wait until the terminal says it’s listening.
  2. Gather a wild potato and wait for the Potato Item List.
  3. Once the window has fully appeared, return to the terminal and press Enter.

Read the result

A successful run writes the loot-preview scope to opcodes.local. If the script says loot preview was not calibrated, no update was attempted.

  • The analysis: events_found is the check used here; specs and specs_by_event() show the promoted layouts, ignored explains rejections, and retention.truncated tells you when only a retained tail was scored.
  • The write: written, added and backup_path.
  • result.summary() and update.summary() format both stages for people.

Build it yourself

Explicit action

action="loot-preview" is required: the default "auto" covers transfer directions only.

from pathlib import Path

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import CalibrationSession, update_profile


profile = Path("opcodes.local")

with CalibrationSession(
    item_id=7003,
    quantity=None,
    action="loot-preview",
) as session:
    input("Gather a wild potato; after the Item List appears, press Enter: ")
    result = session.stop()

if "LOOT_PREVIEW" not in result.events_found:
    raise RuntimeError(result.summary())

update = update_profile(result, profile, action="loot-preview")
print(result.summary())
print(update.summary())
  1. item_id=7003 anchors the known Potato record.
  2. quantity=None means “don’t constrain the watched quantity”, not that the message has no quantity field.
  3. events_found uses the uppercase family LOOT_PREVIEW; delivered events use lowercase loot_preview.

Verify the delivered event

Wrong tool

live_transfer_log.py filters previews out, so it can’t verify this.

No result?

Fix an incomplete calibration

Start a fresh process so the decoder loads the changed profile, and request preview events explicitly:

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live


preview_only = EventFilter(event_types={"loot_preview"})

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=preview_only,
):
    print(event.source, event.item_id, event.quantity)

Open the same preview again; each appearance should print one line.

Guides/Calibration

Fix an incomplete calibration

Match the terminal message to one controlled retry, and verify the result before changing any opcode, offset or profile field by hand.

Locate the failure stage

Different evidence

A quiet verification listener isn’t automatically an analysis failure, and a nonempty result isn’t automatically a usable transfer profile.

StageEvidence
CaptureThe script never reaches the listening prompt, or the capture backend fails
AnalysisA CalibrationResult comes back with missing families, or scoring raises before a result exists
Persistenceupdate_profile() refuses, or fails before or during the write
Runtime verificationThe file was written, but a new listener doesn’t deliver the expected event

Inspect a returned result

No result at all?

CalibrationAuthorityError: destination or count authority wasn’t proven. DirectionMismatchError occurs only with an explicit single direction.

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import CalibrationResult


def inspect_result(result: CalibrationResult) -> None:
    print(result.summary())
    print("families:", sorted(result.events_found))
    print("directions:", sorted(result.detected_directions()))

    for reason in result.ignored:
        print("ignored:", reason)

    if result.retention.truncated:
        print("Retry with a shorter, cleaner capture.")

Call inspect_result(result) right after result = session.stop() when a two-step calibration comes back incomplete.

  • ignored lists why candidate layouts were rejected; it holds no application events.
  • retention.truncated=True means only the newest retained tail was scored.
  • Empty or partial events_found means incomplete, for any workflow whose required family is missing.

Match the message you saw

You seeNext
Capture never reaches Listening in the backgroundRecheck the live-capture prerequisites: permission and adapter selection
It listens, but frames_observed stays zeroDo the shared adapter, VPN, local-IP and filter checks, then repeat the sequence
incomplete transfer profile; missing ...Confirm item ID 15156, keep QUANTITY = 1, use an allowed town, and repeat the whole deposit 1, deposit 4, withdraw 5 sequence
loot preview was not calibrated ...Check the raw item ID, start capture before the preview, let the window load, and retry one clean preview
destination-fieldMove to an allowed town and repeat the full transfer workflow
record-count-fieldKeep deposit 1 and deposit 4 separate, both finished before the withdrawal
live retention truncatedRepeat a shorter clean run and press Enter right after the final action

Make the retry unambiguous

Don’t copy values

Never reuse an opcode, byte offset or stride from another patch. Calibration refuses ambiguous evidence so a clean capture can establish them safely.

Lessons

Transfers ↗ · loot preview ↗

  • Start capture before the first storage move or before opening the preview.
  • For transfers, use five matching unstackables in one allowed town, and do nothing else with items until capture stops.
  • For a preview, show the exact item ID configured in the script and avoid other item windows.
  • Press Enter only after the final move, or once the preview has fully loaded.

The profile updates, but verification is quiet

Private captures

For a maintainer investigation, record one short private reproduction with Wireshark or another external tool on the same adapter. Never post the PCAP publicly.

Still no events?

Zero-event troubleshooting

After transfer calibration:

  1. Stop any logger that was running when the profile changed.
  2. From the repository root, start python examples/live_transfer_log.py again and check the printed profile path.
  3. Wait for the listening message, then repeat one deposit and one withdrawal.
  4. Read any decoder diagnostic printed separately.

After loot-preview calibration: start a fresh listener with the explicit loot_preview filter from Verify the delivered event and reopen the same preview. The transfer logger deliberately excludes previews.

If storage decoding stays incompatible after another clean calibration, keep the terminal diagnostic for the report.

Guides/Calibration

Calibration internals

How controlled item traffic becomes fail-closed profile geometry: direction signals, record counts and runtime validation.

From captured traffic to a profile

See also

Manual calibration · result types

captured messages→known-item candidates→direction and geometry proof→CalibrationResult→update_profile()→runtime validation

Calibration collects complete inbound messages around the known item action. Analysis finds plausible item records, classifies their transfer direction, and proves the offsets and repeated-record shape each profile family needs. Only an unambiguous candidate becomes a MessageSpec.

The CalibrationResult is read-only. Saving is a separate update_profile() step, and a fresh decoder validates the new file again when it loads. Specs store normalized one-record geometry; the observed action totals are evidence, not runtime constants.

Transfer families and runtime use

Not a readiness flag

events_found can include the two evidence-only families, so a nonempty set doesn’t prove runtime readiness.

The transfer runtime needs INVENTORY_TRANSFER, STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA and SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT. Without any one of them, transfer calibration is incomplete.

INVENTORY_TRANSFERrequired
Storage withdrawals, item_received, and inventory hydration and state.
STORAGE_ITEM_DELTArequired
Storage deposits, destination-town identity, and storage hydration and state.
SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENTrequired
Reliably promotes a manual deposit to storage_delta with source="Player Inventory".
SOURCE_CONTAINER_DECREMENTnot used at runtime
Kept only as calibration and audit evidence. A context-after-quantity layout is allowed only when an exact receipt-instance anchor proves the companion.
SOURCE_ITEM_REFERENCEnot used at runtime
Kept only as calibration and audit evidence.

LOOT_PREVIEW is a separate, optional event-producing family. Automatic transfer calibration doesn’t look for it; the loot-preview walkthrough uses an explicit action and keeps the transfer families.

How transfer direction is classified

Explicit direction

Single-direction modes are stricter declarations for advanced recovery. A candidate proving the opposite direction raises DirectionMismatchError.

The default action="auto" evaluates both transfer recipes and records every candidate’s decision in DirectionEvidence. Direction comes from structural signals, not an opcode table.

Observed signalMeans
A high-entropy source-context label before the item recordThe item is entering inventory
A validated storage context before the item recordThe item is entering storage
A small preceding same-flow message carrying the watched item IDFallback evidence of entering storage, used only when no intrinsic signal fired
Both intrinsic signals, or no usable signal in automatic modeThe candidate is withheld; calibration doesn’t guess

How storage-wrapper geometry is proven

Excluded towns

Muzgar (0x055F), Velandir (0x0566), Yukjo Street (0x058C), Godu Village (0x0590) and Bukpo (0x05A4) each hold Velia’s key 0x0005 one byte later in the wrapper, so a capture there can’t prove which column is real.

See also

MessageSpec fields · DecoderHealth

Before promoting STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA, calibration must uniquely identify both the destination field and the declared record-count field. Across the captured deposits it intersects registered-destination candidates with two-byte count candidates whose values fit the observed record geometry. It needs at least two distinct validated deposit counts; the one-record and four-record deposits provide that cross-check.

The excluded-town restriction applies only while learning the offset. A profile calibrated in an unambiguous town handles those destinations normally.

If either column stays ambiguous, CalibrationAuthorityError is raised before any result or write. Once both are proven, calibration records the one-record base length, context_offset and record_count_offset. Runtime derives each wrapper’s stride from its declared count, actual length and that base, and validates every declared record before emitting any neutral storage record.

How source-decrement geometry is proven

Trust contract

Origin evidence

SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT supplies the inventory-side evidence that identifies a manual storage deposit. Quantity and instance field order aren’t treated as patch constants: calibration anchors the exact source instance when available, tests non-overlapping quantity phases and measures the repeated-record period.

For a repeated decrement, only one longest field-valid shape matching the storage record count is promoted. Ambiguous phases, overlapping fields and stride aliases that skip records are withheld without discarding independently proven families. At runtime, an instance-aware spec never falls back to a coincidental quantity when its instance field is empty or invalid.

Storage-source classification is a separate runtime stage. A confirmed worker companion chain wins and assigns source="Worker Production"; otherwise calibrated decrement evidence can assign source="Player Inventory". With neither signal, proven live activity gets source=None, and a record lacking independent live or hydration proof stays storage_record.

Evidence retention and scope

Retry, don’t raise

A shorter clean retry is usually stronger than raising the limits.

Live calibration keeps the newest contiguous evidence tail under two default bounds: 50,000 frames and 64 MiB of payload. Analysis scores that retained tail, not every frame observed; CalibrationRetention reports the observed, retained, discarded and truncated counts.

A truncated result covers only the newest tail. Offline calibrate_pcap() analyzes a finite recording without the live bounds.

Patch-recovery boundary

Fails closed

Calibration withholds ambiguous specs, loading rejects incomplete runtime geometry, and the decoder reports incompatible storage structure instead of guessing.

Calibration can relearnNeeds decoder work
Message opcodes and normalized one-record lengthsA redesigned shared item-record structure
Item, quantity, instance, context and count positionsA new count encoding or a changed destination-ID meaning
Repeated-record spacing within current invariantsChanged origin-evidence or hydration-cohort relationships

Guides

Arena of Solare

Capture one Arena of Solare Leaderboard load, save it, and reuse the recording for overall rankings, class tables and player lookups.

From one leaderboard load to reusable data

One shot

After its first load the client caches the Leaderboard for an unknown time, and live decoding is sensitive to host timing. Save that load, then analyze the file with replay_solare(). Missed it? Restart the game first.

Before you begin

Complete Installation & setup. Solare needs no item opcode profile or calibration.

The leaderboard updates daily on the game’s schedule; players can’t refresh it. Start capture before the Leaderboard tab’s first load after restarting the game. The toolkit passively observes the two responses and returns one SolareCaptureResult. It emits no BDOEvent objects and never controls the game.

start capture→open Leaderboard once→save PCAPNG→SolareCaptureResult→replay and query

Always branch on result.complete. A complete result carries one immutable SolareLeaderboardSnapshot in result.snapshot. A non-complete one keeps status, message and evidence with snapshot=None: partial rows are never shown as leaderboard state.

overall_top_100SolareOverallEntry rows
The authoritative overall ranks 1–100.
playersSolarePlayer rows
The class top-20 tables, flattened. Not a global top 620.

The two responses decode independently. A name can appear in either or both, and optional values are never copied between row types. Check overall_capabilities or class_table_capabilities before relying on Elo or performance fields.

Capture once, replay as often as needed

Current geometry

A complete snapshot needs 31 supported class tables of exactly 20 rows plus the overall top 100. Agent isn’t in that roster yet: Agent rows, or any class with under 20 ranked players early in a season, stay non-complete until new-season traffic is captured, reviewed and supported.
