Guides/Arena of Solare

Capture a leaderboard load

Start passive capture before the first Leaderboard load after a game restart, then keep both the checked result and a reusable PCAPNG.

Run the finished example

Keep the packets

Live analysis can be unstable; a recording isn’t. Save the load with --save-pcap, save_pcap= or Wireshark, and analyze it with replay_solare().

Lesson

solare_live_snapshot.py ↗

From the repository root, before the first Leaderboard load of this game session:

python examples/solare_live_snapshot.py --save-pcap solare-leaderboard.pcapng
  1. If the Leaderboard was already opened this game session, restart Black Desert.
  2. Wait for the capture-ready message before touching Arena of Solare.
  3. Open the Leaderboard tab once. The broader Arena menu isn’t enough.
  4. Leave the tab visible while both leaderboard responses arrive.
  5. The script stops on confirmation or after its 120-second default deadline. Ctrl+C ends it earlier.

Recording never overwrites a file, so use a new path for each attempt. Without --save-pcap, the script captures and reports the same way but writes nothing.

Private

The PCAPNG holds private capture data. Keep it local and review it before sharing.

Example outputrepresentative, abridged · paths and milestones vary
[capture-ready] passive Solare capture is ready ..., recording ...\solare-leaderboard.pcapng; open the Leaderboard tab for its first load after restarting the game
[snapshot-confirmed] opcode-agnostic Arena of Solare leaderboard confirmed
[capture-finished] stop reason: complete-snapshot
[saved-capture] ...\solare-leaderboard.pcapng

Once one complete load is saved, reuse that file for the query walkthroughs instead of reopening the game.

Build the capture yourself

Reference

capture_solare_snapshot() · SolareCaptureResult

from pathlib import Path

from bdo_toolkit.solare import capture_solare_snapshot

capture_path = Path("solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
print("Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.")
result = capture_solare_snapshot(save_pcap=capture_path)

if not result.complete:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
assert snapshot is not None
print("complete: leaderboard snapshot ready")
print(f"saved capture: {capture_path}")
print(f"overall rows={len(snapshot.overall_top_100)}")
print(f"class-table rows={len(snapshot.players)}")
Example outputa representative complete result
Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.
complete: leaderboard snapshot ready
saved capture: solare-leaderboard.pcapng
overall rows=100
class-table rows=620
  • capture_solare_snapshot() owns one bounded live run and returns one result.
  • save_pcap records the accepted packets and refuses an existing destination.
  • complete is the safe branch; arriving traffic alone proves nothing.
  • snapshot exists only on a complete result and roots every leaderboard query.

Show progress in an application advanced

See also

Async updates() · SolareUpdate fields

The finished example polls manually because it owns a deadline and heartbeats. When the toolkit’s milestones are enough, LiveSolareSession.updates() is simpler:

from pathlib import Path

from bdo_toolkit.solare import LiveSolareSession

with LiveSolareSession(
    save_pcap=Path("solare-leaderboard.pcapng"),
) as session:
    print("Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.")

    for update in session.updates():
        print(f"[{update.kind.value}] {update.message}")

result = session.result
if result is None or not result.complete:
    raise RuntimeError("leaderboard capture did not complete")
Example outputrepresentative, abridged · middle milestones vary or coalesce
Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.
[capture-ready] passive Solare capture is ready ...
[ranked-progress] 500 unique ranked players recovered; waiting for class balance and the top-100 cross-check
[snapshot-confirmed] opcode-agnostic Arena of Solare leaderboard confirmed
[finished] Solare capture finished with status complete

updates() waits internally, yields through the terminal finished update, then ends. snapshot-confirmed is a milestone, not the end; the final update carries update.result, also kept as session.result.

Use wait() when progress doesn’t matter, poll() for your own deadlines or heartbeats, and stop() for manual shutdown. Breaking out of updates() doesn’t stop capture; exit the context or stop it yourself.

Use the terminal result

Next

Read the overall top 100 from the saved capture. No complete result? Troubleshoot it.

On success, continue through snapshot.overall_top_100, snapshot.players or the snapshot lookups. Otherwise print status.value and message, and read evidence only when you must tell incomplete structure from capture loss.

The same function can change its deadline, report progress through on_update or keep opaque extension bytes. None of that changes the rule: only a complete result publishes a snapshot.

Build the ranking loop yourself

Elo is optional

Rankings can stay structurally valid after a patch changes deeper fields. Check overall_capabilities first; missing means unavailable, not zero.

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare("solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete or result.snapshot is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
has_elo = "elo" in snapshot.overall_capabilities

for entry in snapshot.overall_top_100:
    elo = entry.elo if has_elo else "unavailable"
    print(entry.global_rank, entry.name, elo)
Example outputsynthetic · first rows
1 ExamplePlayer01 3045
2 ExamplePlayer02 3012
3 ExamplePlayer03 2988

On a toolkit-built complete result, snapshot.overall_top_100 is a tuple of 100 SolareOverallEntry rows. The loop prints global_rank, name and elo.

Use the row beyond rank and name

Not top_100

Don’t substitute snapshot.top_100: it projects class-table rows ranked 1–100 and can be shorter than the overall table.

Next

Read a class top 20 · read player statistics

The same row can expose direct aggregate total_wins, total_draws and total_losses; derived total_matches and total_win_rate; and its own classes_played. Read player statistics checks the capability set before using them.

Build the class query yourself

Roster fails closed

An unsupported new class code never gets a familiar name. Use the canonical class codes.

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare("solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete or result.snapshot is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

class_leaderboard(11) filters the class-table players by primary class and returns SolarePlayer rows in global-rank order. It never derives a class table from overall_top_100.

Read a class-table row

Next

Find one player · SolarePlayer fields

Each SolarePlayer owns name, global_rank, primary_class, optional elo and per-class classes_played. class_table_capabilities says which optional fields exist.

global_rank stays the global rank; the tuple position is the order within the class. Under the supported geometry, a complete snapshot returns 20 rows for every supported class.

This is a valid result: a place in the overall top 100 doesn’t require a place in any class top 20.

Build both lookups yourself

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

name = "ExamplePlayer"  # Replace with an exact name from your capture.
result = replay_solare("solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete or result.snapshot is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
overall_entry = snapshot.get_overall_entry(name)
class_entry = snapshot.get_player(name)

print(f"overall={overall_entry is not None}")
print(f"class-table={class_entry is not None}")
Example outputsynthetic · an overall-only player
overall=True
class-table=False

get_overall_entry(name) searches only overall_top_100 and returns a SolareOverallEntry or None. get_player(name) searches only the class-table players and returns a SolarePlayer or None.

Keep the two results separate

No player ID

The model exposes no stable player UID. A name is lookup text, not a durable identity key.

Next

Read player statistics · lookup reference

  • Name matching is exact and case-sensitive.
  • Either lookup can return None on its own.
  • When both succeed, they’re independently decoded objects. Never copy missing Elo, classes or performance from one into the other.

Check overall_capabilities before reading optional fields from overall_entry, and class_table_capabilities before reading them from class_entry.

Build the statistics view yourself

Three field groups

The capability check authorizes elo, the direct aggregate outcomes and the per-class records separately, before any is used.

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

name = "ExamplePlayer"  # Replace with an exact overall name from your capture.
result = replay_solare("solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete or result.snapshot is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
entry = snapshot.get_overall_entry(name)
if entry is None:
    raise LookupError(f"{name!r} is not in the overall top 100")

required = {"elo", "aggregate_performance", "performance"}
missing = required - snapshot.overall_capabilities
if missing:
    raise RuntimeError(f"overall details unavailable: {sorted(missing)}")

print(entry.elo, entry.total_matches, entry.total_win_rate)
for record in entry.classes_played:
    class_name = record.player_class.name or record.player_class.code
    specialization = record.specialization
    specialization_name = (
        "unavailable"
        if specialization is None
        else (specialization.name or specialization.branch)
    )
    print(
        class_name,
        specialization_name,
        record.matches,
        record.wins,
        record.draws,
        record.losses,
        record.win_rate,
    )
Example outputsynthetic · the same row
2874 100 58.0
Lahn Awakening 40 24 1 15 60.0
Ranger Succession 30 18 0 12 60.0
Sorceress Succession 16 10 1 5 62.5

get_overall_entry() returns one SolareOverallEntry; each value in its classes_played is a SolareClassPerformance.

Separate aggregate and per-class outcomes

Not a sum of slots

The aggregate can cover more matches than the one to three visible slots. Keep it separate; missing optional values mean unavailable, never zero.

See also

Player statistics reference · internals

entry.elooverall row
Elo decoded from this overall row.
total_wins · total_draws · total_lossesdirect
The row’s own aggregate outcome tuple.
total_matches · total_win_ratederived
Computed from the complete aggregate tuple.
classes_playedper class
Zero to three detailed records from the same overall response: player_class, specialization, matches, W/D/L and win_rate.

Starting from a class-table SolarePlayer instead? Check class_table_capabilities and read that row’s elo, primary_class and classes_played. It has no overall total_* fields.

Guides/Arena of Solare

Solare internals

How generic BDO traffic becomes a fail-closed Arena of Solare snapshot: opcode-agnostic table proof, source-local detail inference and capability publication.

From captured traffic to a snapshot

See also

Normal workflow · evidence and health · snapshot

live capture or PCAP→TCP reassembly→generic BDO framing→structural proof→clean-health gate→detail decoding→capability publication→SolareCaptureResult

The Solare route shares passive packet acquisition, TCP reassembly and generic message framing with the rest of the toolkit, then builds only the Solare classifier and result. It doesn’t run the item-event decoder, load an item opcode profile or emit BDOEvent values.

A snapshot needs structural confirmation and clean acquisition first. Optional detail decoding reads only the exact class-table and overall windows that discovery already selected, so it can’t promote menu-only, partial, ambiguous, gapped or dropped traffic.

What the runtime discovers and what it assumes

Opcode is only a label

It keeps unrelated repeated families apart as an opaque equality label. Discovery never compares it with a known Solare value, and no detail selection includes it.

AuthorityExamplesLifetime
Discovered from every captureObserved opcode labels, message lengths, record stride, name, rank and class positions, response boundaries and the winning table windowsCurrent result only
Reviewed structural invariantsGeneric BDO framing; zero flags; two records per candidate message; the supported name/rank encoding; the validated 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class-table geometry; an independent 100-row overall table; the cross-table relationshipPackage code, until deliberately extended
Registered detail knowledgeReviewed geometry fingerprints and source-specific deep-field offsets; opcode is excluded from every fingerprintPackage decoder fast path
Ephemerally inferred detailsUnique full-table solutions for Elo, class slots, performance, aggregate outcomes, recent history and requested raw boundaries on an unregistered geometryDiscarded after the result is built
Deliberately withheldUID or account identity, meanings of individual recent-result codes, parsed gear or skill-addon semanticsNo capability or serialized field

How leaderboard identity is proven

Not a data source

The cross-check proves both responses describe the same snapshot. Neither response supplies data for the other.

The scanner works per reassembled directional TCP flow, starts a new generation when a four-tuple reopens, and can synchronize after attaching midstream. Candidate families are keyed by:

(TCP four-tuple, connection generation, observed opcode, message length)
    → repeated candidate family
StageRequired proof
Generic framingA little-endian total length, zero flags and a bounded 8–32 KiB message. Synchronization prefers two equal large-family headers, and otherwise needs three plausible generic headers
Class table (rich in evidence)Two fixed UTF-16LE name columns, one increasing rank column starting with exact ranks 1–20, and a reviewed 31- or 32-class roster appearing 20 times each: 310 or 320 messages × 2 records = 620 or 640 rows. If ordinary discovery is incomplete, a separate fallback accepts the reviewed terminated short-response envelope, including a single-record tail, with the full known roster, 1–20 entries per class, at least 400 total rows and a complete overall cross-check. Missing boundaries or stream bytes reject the fallback
Overall tableA separate later family in the same flow generation, within a 1 MiB stream distance, holding 50 messages × 2 records with unique names and exact ranks 1–100
Cross-table confirmationAt least 20 exact (rank, name) pairs and no contradiction either way: a shared rank keeps its name, and a shared name keeps its rank
Menu contextThe observed 24-message, five-name-slot family explains menu or history traffic, but can’t establish either leaderboard response

No player among global ranks 1–20 can have 20 same-class players ahead under the per-class cap, so those first 20 must appear in the class-table union. Rank 21 and later may legitimately be missing from every class top 20.

Response windows, retries and exact-50 ambiguity Optional backgroundShow detailsHide details

A recording can start inside a stale response, hold a complete retry and end inside another refresh. Discovery deduplicates by flow generation, stream sequence, length and message digest; finds boundaries from the ten-message rank-reset prefix 1/2 through 19/20; and evaluates only reset-aligned windows. Partial, complete and partial traffic therefore can’t be spliced into a false snapshot.

When several windows are complete, the first to complete in observation order wins. Live capture permanently latches that window and its confirmation health. Replay feeds the same incremental tracker, so saved files use the same selection.

The first 50 messages of a class response also hold ranks 1–100, because both families carry two records per message. Repeated class codes or a following rank 101/102 prove a class-table prefix; a same-family reset to ranks 1/2 closes the prior candidate. Unrelated traffic isn’t a boundary.

An overall response ending at exactly 50 messages closes live only after the decode queue drains and 1.5 seconds pass without another zero-flag, candidate-sized message. The clock is per candidate, so small unrelated traffic doesn’t reset it. Finalized replay closes the trailing window at once.

How optional details are recovered

Same-geometry drift fails closed

If a patch keeps a registered outer fingerprint but moves deeper fields, optional capabilities can disappear while rankings stay complete. A damaged capture is never reinterpreted as a new layout.

Not calibration

Solare has no calibration command, user profile, persisted learned layout or promotion step. Item calibration can’t repair a Solare result.

complete source window→registered geometry?→reviewed fast path or bounded inference→all-row validation→source capability set
Geometry pathBehaviorPersistence
Registered outer geometryThe reviewed source-specific decoder runs and validates its complete owning-table groupsDecoder-owned package code; no user profile
Unregistered outer geometryThe learner searches the selected records for one unambiguous full-table solution per group, publishing valid groups and withholding ambiguous onesOffsets live only while this result is built, and are relearned next run
Registered geometry, failing deep fieldsThe registered decoder’s fail-closed result stands; the learner never reinterprets the same geometryKeep the recording for decoder review

Each value is reread from its own response. Shared-player agreement can prove or disambiguate an offset, but no overall field is filled from a class row, and no class-table field from the overall response.

Ephemeral detail-learning gates Optional referenceShow detailsHide details

The learner reads only the exact selected class records and 100 overall records, rereads every structural identity, and refuses a learned record window over 32 KiB.

The short-board fallback may preserve recent-history codes that disagree with cumulative counters only when independent overall-table joins establish the counter labels. Full-board validation is unchanged; malformed histories and unbalanced counters still reject details.

Candidate groupAcceptance rule
Class and specialization slotsClass position is already structural on the class table; overall needs one unique three-slot class column. One to three unique occupied known classes must precede explicit empty sentinels, and specialization needs one unique compatible three-slot column
Per-class performanceArithmetic candidates are checked against history and independent companion evidence before requiring a unique layout. A uniquely established companion counter layout can corroborate numerical values without assigning outcome labels; history must independently establish those labels. The match-counter triple and three distinct, non-overlapping outcome triples must satisfy wins + draws + losses == matches for every occupied slot, with zeroes in empty slots. A zero-only outcome needs one bounded 12–15-byte region between independently validated fields. If the whole region is zero, equivalent addresses remain in the inference proof. Otherwise exactly one 12-byte placement must be zero in every row, including unused slots; adjacent bytes are left uninterpreted. Other unassigned gaps may be shorter than a complete 12-byte counter array and need not be interpreted. Competing full-size gaps or conflicting regions remain unavailable
Recent historyOne region must decode across all slots. Equal binary pairs count as wins, unequal binary pairs as losses, and the observed (-1,0) pair as a draw. Complete short histories require exact W/D/L counts; longer windows bound each lifetime component. Low-match players are optional. Signed histories require complete observed pairs; other signed variants remain unsupported. Individual tokens have no public outcome meaning
EloOne unique zero-extended 32-bit column pair: positive, bounded, non-increasing by rank, diverse enough, and equal for shared names across both independently read responses. A learned table can instead anchor to a validated registered companion
Overall aggregate W/D/LLearned only after overall per-class performance. Totals equal exposed matches below the three-slot cap, never undercount capped rows, show a nontrivial capped-row excess, and have one strongly supported orientation. Candidate counters cannot overlap independently identified name or rank fields
Opaque raw regionsOnly when requested. Gear boundaries validate all 14 equipment tuples in every occupied block; addon candidates need the proven bounded numeric-CSV shape and slot periodicity; both responses must validate boundaries, and at least 20 shared name/class slots must agree byte for byte. Public bytes are still sliced from each response separately
Candidate fan-outMore than eight full match candidates, 4,096 active outcome candidates, 64 validated outcome columns, 64 arithmetic layouts, 256 aggregate vectors, or more than one complete solution withholds that group instead of choosing heuristically

Learned IDs look like solare-rich-ephemeral-v1-… or solare-overall-ephemeral-v1-…. The digest covers role, geometry and inferred offsets, not opcode, player content, identifier-like bytes or raw content, so raw-enabled decoding can yield a more specific ID. The owning capability set, never the ID, authorizes optional fields.

Capability publication and source independence

Measured, not promised

On the development machine, unknown-layout learning took about 0.85–1.02 s, and raw-enabled replay of the validation captures about 1.6–1.9 s end to end.

PathPublication boundary
Registered class tableElo, performance and requested raw extensions form one strict full-table bundle. Any deep invariant failure leaves class rows at rankings only
Registered overall tableElo, aggregate performance and per-class performance are independent all-100 groups. Raw extensions depend on valid overall performance
Learned tablesElo and performance are independent table-wide groups. Aggregate depends on valid learned overall performance; raw depends on valid performance and raw-boundary agreement in both tables

class_table_capabilities and overall_capabilities are authoritative for their own responses, and capabilities is their intersection. Missing optional data means unavailable: never zero, a slot sum or a value copied from the other table.

Structural confirmation can be announced before optional-field finalization completes. Registered geometries stay on the fast path.

Capture integrity and bounded resources advanced

Conservative health

Gap counters cover selected inbound flows and drop counters the whole capture handle, so damage on unrelated selected traffic can withhold a valid leaderboard.

See also

SolareCaptureHealth · LiveSolareSession

A leaderboard load can deliver more than 5 MiB in under a second. Windows live capture therefore requests a 64 MiB Npcap buffer, keeps packet callbacks minimal, and moves writing and decoding to a worker. Timeout recovery waits for capture finalization, so callback latency, native batching or worker backlog can’t make the decoder skip a prefix that’s still arriving.

BoundaryCurrent limitEffect
Live packet handoff4,096 packetsOverflow makes health unclean and requests a resource-limit stop
TCP reorder pressure2,048 pending segments or 8 MiB per flowAn anchored flow past either limit can reset at retained data. Timeout recovery waits for live finalization; any reset before confirmation blocks publication
Active reassembly64 flowsA flow-state eviction makes health unclean
Discovery ownership768 candidate messages or 16 MiBThe retained window is evaluated before an older batch is released. Rollover alone is diagnostic, not packet loss
Progress delivery64 updatesIntermediate milestones can coalesce; the queue isn’t an audit log

With stop_on_complete=False, live capture latches the clean health of its first confirmed snapshot; replay reports health across the whole recording.

Snapshot semantic identity Optional backgroundShow detailsHide details

snapshot_id is a deterministic semantic SHA-256 identifier for idempotent imports, not a wire UID. Its normalized envelope excludes observation time, evidence, health, identifier-like source bytes and opaque raw blobs, and missing optional values aren’t contradictions.

The compact class-table identity is kept only when every overall row has a class-table counterpart and every comparable non-raw value agrees. Otherwise both collections contribute, so an overall-only row or a legitimate source-local difference changes the identity. The private envelope version is independent of public serialization schema version 2.

Patch-recovery boundary

After a patch

Run the ordinary live example first, and save one clean private PCAP for review. Decoder work comes only after that result.

Patch or season changeExpected result
Opcode onlyStructural confirmation and registered details survive: neither the classifier nor a detail fingerprint trusts opcode
Outer geometry (message length, stride, name or rank position) changes while the table relations surviverankings survives; the unregistered path attempts bounded inference for each optional group
An unknown detail group is ambiguous or invalidThe snapshot can stay complete, publishing only the independently validated capabilities
Deep fields move while outer geometry exactly matches a registered profileThe affected registered group or strict class bundle is withheld; that geometry never enters the learner
A class is added or removed, or a supported class returns fewer than 20 rowsThe exact 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era proof can’t confirm a complete snapshot until the roster, geometry and regression evidence are deliberately extended
Truncated burst, TCP gap, backend drop, queue overflow or flow eviction before confirmationA non-complete result with evidence and health; no snapshot
Two-record framing, flags, compression, name/rank encoding or the cross-family relation changesPartial or inconclusive until the classifier proof itself is extended

A complete result with the expected capabilities proves the classifier and detail path still work. A complete rankings-only result localizes the change to optional details; a partial result points to acquisition or structural assumptions instead.

Historical layout evidence Optional referenceShow detailsHide details

Observed regression evidence, not configuration or classifier input. Each message holds two records; offsets are relative to the owning record, while decoding keeps the original five-byte-header message.

Several validated tail fields extend past the nominal stride but stay inside the complete second-record message, so bounds are checked against the original message. This much movement across generations is exactly why offsets are never caller configuration.

Across 400 registered-layout overall rows, aggregate matches never fell below the exposed slot sum. All 192 one-slot rows and all 111 two-slot rows matched it exactly; 52 of 97 three-slot rows had a positive gap, up to 125 matches in June and 108 in July. The aggregate is authoritative, but the gap doesn’t identify a hidden fourth class.

Confidence and research boundary

Private evidence

Saved PCAPs and serialized results can hold names, rankings, Elo, outcomes and identifier-like bytes. Keep captures local, opt into raw only when needed, and share the smallest support report first.

See also

SolareRawSection · capture privacy

  • Synthetic tests rewrite opcodes arbitrarily while preserving structure, and cover the exact overlap threshold, rank/name contradictions, stale prefixes, multiple refreshes, capture gaps, retention rollover and exact-50 closure.
  • Six complete private captures replay across several opcode and geometry shifts. Five registered-layout captures forced through the learner reproduce every public field and opted-in raw byte, and a genuinely unregistered July 30 geometry succeeds through the ordinary ephemeral path.
  • Adversarial tests corrupt or duplicate Elo, performance, aggregate, history and raw candidates one at a time, and verify that only the affected group is withheld under its path’s dependency rules.

All six real captures place every overall top-100 player somewhere in the class-table union, so the legitimate overall-only case is proven synthetically, including its directly decoded aggregate, until a divergent real capture is observed.

No public player identifier is exposed. Several nonzero cross-table eight-byte candidates look convincing, older generations use different representations, and the strongest remaining candidate still doesn’t prove account, family, character, lifetime or future stability. Identifier-like bytes stay outside learning, capabilities, serialization and snapshot identity.

Likewise, recent-result regions keep literal wire text without naming individual codes, and gear and addon regions stay opaque. Aggregate W/D/L has strong whole-table and cross-generation evidence; its exact in-client wording stays conservative until a controlled UI comparison settles it.

← Read player statisticsNext: Asyncio integration →

Guides

Asyncio integration

Use the async session facades when an application already owns an asyncio event loop. Ordinary scripts should use the synchronous APIs.

What asyncio integration changes

Same contracts

Each facade wraps the synchronous capture, decoding, buffering, result and failure contracts, moving blocking lifecycle work onto its own worker threads. There’s no second decoder or event model.

WorkflowAsync facadeApplication receives
Item activityAsyncLiveCaptureSessionAn async stream of the same BDOEvent objects
Item calibrationAsyncCalibrationSessionOne CalibrationResult from await session.stop()
Arena of SolareAsyncLiveSolareSessionAn async SolareUpdate stream and one SolareCaptureResult
Agris balancesAsyncLiveAgrisSessionAn async stream of AgrisBalance observations

There’s no package-wide async mode. PCAP replay, CharacterLoadSession, GrindSession, LiveXPSession, LiveRawSession, profile loading and updates, formatting and serialization stay synchronous. To run one of them from asyncio, move the whole call onto a worker thread yourself.

Application-controlled item capture

One consumer

A session has one event consumer. When several components need the events, fan them out from that task through your own queue.

Stopping

Breaking out of async for doesn’t stop capture. Stop from your shutdown path; async with exit also cleans up.

A long-running application consumes events in one task, while a UI action or shutdown signal decides when capture stops:

import asyncio

from bdo_toolkit import AsyncLiveCaptureSession


async def consume(session: AsyncLiveCaptureSession) -> None:
    async for event in session.events():
        print(event.format_human())


async def main() -> None:
    stop_requested = asyncio.Event()

    async with AsyncLiveCaptureSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
        consumer = asyncio.create_task(consume(session))
        try:
            # Your Stop button or shutdown path sets this.
            await stop_requested.wait()
        finally:
            await session.stop()
            await consumer


asyncio.run(main())

events() ends once capture stops and buffered events drain, so stopping first, then awaiting the consumer, delivers every finalized event.

Where await belongs

Callbacks stay synchronous

on_diagnostic, Solare on_update and the others run synchronously. Keep them short, and call only request_stop() there; never block or consume.

awaitlifecycle · one-shot polls
session.start(), session.stop() and session.poll() can wait on capture or cleanup.
async forstreams
session.events() and Solare session.updates() are async iterators: consume them, don’t await them.
plain readsstate · models
session.running, session.result and event.to_dict() are ordinary synchronous reads.
asyncio.to_thread()blocking work
For a synchronous call too slow for the event loop, such as update_profile() after await session.stop() returns a calibration result.

Cancellation and cleanup

Exact rules

Item capture · calibration · Solare · Agris

Cancelling an async lifecycle or consumption call is a shutdown request, not permission to abandon the capture. The facade finishes bounded cleanup for work already started before asyncio.CancelledError escapes.

  • Each facade is single-use; create a new one for each capture or calibration run.
  • Item capture and Agris allow one consumer. Solare allows one progress consumer plus one completion waiter.
  • If cleanup_incomplete is true, retry await stop() on the same facade instead of replacing it.
  • An exception already leaving an async with body stays primary while cleanup runs.

Guides

Troubleshooting

Start with the outcome your application received, then prove acquisition before changing filters, profiles or classifier settings.

Identify the outcome first

Empty isn’t an error

A healthy capture can still deliver nothing. Never read an exception as an empty result, or silence as zero.

You receivedIt meansNext
An exceptionAn operation, lifecycle stage, callback, writer or cleanup step failedThe owning API’s Raises section
No item eventsThe adapter, filter, profile or action yielded nothing deliverable, even if capture is healthyProve acquisition, then check delivery and the profile
An item-state snapshot with gapsOnly the hydration evidence seen during that capture is reportedRoot checks, coverage, warnings and decoder health
A non-complete Solare resultThe leaderboard wasn’t proven complete under the current structural contractStatus, evidence and health
A GrindFeatureError or invalid statusAn XP or Agris reader stopped, or the whole capture lost authorityThe reader status and final health

Choose a problem

→

Live capture sees no game traffic

Check the adapter, local IPv4 restriction, Npcap, permissions and VPN route, for every live workflow.

 →

No item activity appears

Once acquisition is proven, check delivery filters, profile compatibility and storage classification.

 →

Item state is incomplete

Read the snapshot’s checks and coverage before retrying a character load.

 →

Solare result is incomplete

Match the status to the captured action, health counters and supported geometry.

 →

Calibration is incomplete

Use the calibration retry workflow and its controlled in-game sequence.

 →

Prepare a support report

Collect structured diagnostics first; share a raw capture only when it’s needed.

If an exception was raised

Generic exceptions

TypeError, ValueError and the like are documented by the function or class that raises them.

ProfileErrorprofiles
A profile failed to parse, validate, load or fetch.
CaptureIntegrityErrorcapture
Known acquisition loss: packet drops, gaps or a full queue.
CalibrationAuthorityErrorcalibration
Calibration found the target but couldn’t prove a safe decoder profile.
DirectionMismatchErrorcalibration
The capture contradicts an explicitly declared transfer direction.
XPTrackingError · AgrisDetectionErrorgrind tracking
A standalone XP or Agris reader lost authority; in GrindSession these arrive as events instead.

How the pipelines decide

When the outcome doesn’t match what you expected, the internals guides explain each decision: item events (pipeline, classification, ordering and capture bounds), calibration (evidence and runtime geometry) and Arena of Solare (structural discovery, detail inference and capture integrity).

← Asyncio integrationNext: Live capture sees no game traffic →

Guides/Troubleshooting

Live capture sees no game traffic

No traffic or no packets: check the adapter, local IPv4 restriction, capture backend and VPN route before you look at filters, profiles or decoders.

Confirm it’s an acquisition problem

On Windows

First follow Diagnose capture when automatic selection fails: inspect BDO connections, pick a settings proposal and test it.

Stage only

A nonzero signal proves only that its stage saw traffic, not that a profile, filter, action or classifier should produce a result.

Find out what candidate traffic, if any, reached the workflow. Each API reports a signal at a different stage:

WorkflowSignalZero means
Continuing item eventspackets_acceptedNo packet matched the selected adapter, server ports and optional local IPv4
Calibrationframes_observedNo complete generic BDO frame reached calibration
Character-load item stateframes_seen or the final diagnosticsNo complete generic BDO frame reached the character-load collector
Arena of Solareno-traffic status and result healthNo usable inbound game-server traffic reached classification

Once acquisition is established, continue with the owning workflow.

Inspect the selected interface and filters

Clean isn’t correct

Health reports known loss on the selected path. A wrong adapter can stay perfectly clean while seeing no BDO packets.

See also

Interfaces and VPNs · PacketCaptureOptions

  1. Where the session exposes it, read session.endpoint after startup: its interface, local_ip and bpf_filter are fixed for the run.
  2. If the interface is missing or unexpected, run scapy.all.show_interfaces() and copy the exact physical or virtual adapter name into interface=.
  3. While diagnosing a pinned interface, leave local_ip=None so a wrong destination address can’t hide matching traffic.
  4. Start a fresh session, wait until it’s ready, and perform one known in-game action.

Account for VPN routing

  1. Stop the session, set up the VPN state and routing your application will use, then start a new session.
  2. For a full tunnel, test the VPN’s virtual adapter that exposes decrypted IPv4/TCP, not the physical adapter carrying encrypted tunnel packets.
  3. For split or per-application routing, check the physical adapter too: BDO can take a different route from the computer’s default.
  4. If no adapter visible to the capture backend (Npcap on Windows) exposes decrypted BDO traffic, live decoding isn’t possible with that VPN setup. Offline replay works only if a compatible recording can be made.

Check the capture backend, permissions and filtering

IPv4 only

Capture reads inbound, unfragmented IPv4/TCP. Native IPv6 BDO traffic and fragmented IPv4 aren’t supported, and use_bpf doesn’t change that.

You seeDo
The adapter fails to openConfirm the capture backend is installed and usable (Npcap 1.88 or later on Windows), the adapter still exists and the process may capture
It opens, but every signal stays zeroRecheck the interface, VPN route, local_ip and server ports, and that the game action happened after readiness
Traffic appears only with use_bpf=FalseKeep that comparison as evidence that the BPF path suppressed matching traffic, and report the adapter, driver, Scapy and Npcap versions. Python-side filtering admits more traffic and adds capture pressure, so it isn’t a general fix
Health reports drops, queue overflow, gap resets or flow evictionTreat the run as incomplete, reduce capture pressure where you can, and retry before suspecting the decoder

Retry, then continue with the workflow

Once acquisition works and the workflow’s integrity or diagnostic signal shows no known loss, continue with the symptom:

→

No item activity appears

Event delivery, current-patch profile compatibility and storage classification.

 →

Item state is incomplete

The character-load window, observational coverage and decoder health.

 →

Calibration is incomplete

The controlled action sequence, evidence and retention.

 →

Solare result is incomplete

The one-shot load, terminal status, structural evidence and health.
← TroubleshootingNext: No item activity appears →

Guides/Troubleshooting

No item activity appears

Check the live path in order: acquisition first, then delivery policy, then profile compatibility.

Establish acquisition first

Accepted isn’t decoded

A nonzero packet count shows candidate acquisition, not successful BDO framing or decoding.

See also

No game traffic · diagnostics & health

Use an explicit LiveCaptureSession and confirm that packets matching its capture filter reach the raw queue before you read anything into decoder silence.

If session.health.packets_accepted stays zero, or the selected endpoint is uncertain, finish the shared adapter, VPN, backend and filter checks first.

Ask for every event, briefly

Pass EventFilter.all() to separate capture or decoding problems from the ordinary activity preset. If records appear only then, acquisition works, and classification or your earlier filter excluded them.

inventory_record and storage_record are neutral decoded records, not confirmed activity. Their fields and decoder_health show whether calibration geometry or evidence-based promotion is missing.

Check the profile against the current patch

Valid but stale

A valid file can still be stale. Quiet decoding after a weekly patch doesn’t have to raise an exception.

  1. Confirm the selected file exists, is active, and has the profile families the tested action needs.
  2. Perform one known action after capture is ready, and compare it with the same action from verification.
  3. If traffic is healthy and all() stays quiet, fetch the maintained profile again or follow Calibration.

Storage-specific checks

You seeIt provesInspect
storage_deltaThe record was promoted to proven live activitysource, the numeric storage_id, optional storage_name and quantity
storage_recordThe wrapper decoded, but neither origin nor hydration evidence claimed itThe calibrated count and destination fields, matching decrement evidence and decoder_health.storage_status
No storage event under EventFilter.all()The expected wrapper didn’t decode with this profileProfile family coverage, message geometry, diagnostics and current-patch calibration
← Live capture sees no game trafficNext: Item state is incomplete →

Guides/Troubleshooting

Item state is incomplete

Read every snapshot as observed evidence, then use its root checks and coverage to find what the load didn’t prove.

Start with the two root checks

No frames?

Check shared live acquisition first.

CheckMeansIf False
state.hydration_detectedAt least one inventory or town-storage hydration signal was decodedThe capture likely missed the load window, selected the wrong traffic or used incompatible profile geometry
state.identity_completeNo decoded record lacks its item-instance identityInspect the missing-instance counters in state.coverage; don’t merge uncertain records by item ID

Neither is a completion marker. True doesn’t prove every container or registered town appeared.

Read coverage as a reason, not a score

Reference

ItemStateCoverage · StorageContents

Coverage fieldQuestion it answers
inventory_records_missing_instanceDid an inventory record lack the identity a trustworthy stack needs?
storage_records_missing_instanceDid a storage record lack it, including outside the selected sweep?
selected_storage_records_missing_instanceDo the selected current storage summaries have incomplete identity?
registered_storage_ids_not_observedWhich registered destinations produced no evidence?
unregistered_storage_ids_observedWhich observed destination IDs have no built-in display metadata?
storage_locations_not_selectedHow many earlier destinations did the latest sweep not revisit?
storage_locations_with_incomplete_current_identityHow many selected town summaries have incomplete identity?

Retry the load, not the queries

After a patch

If the same gap repeats with healthy acquisition, verify or recalibrate the item profile before raising capture limits.

  1. For storage, restart Black Desert and start a fresh CharacterLoadSession before the first character enters the world. A later switch only rehydrates inventory.
  2. Let the world settle before stopping. Opening a town storage afterward doesn’t recreate the load window.
  3. Inspect state.warnings and state.decoder_health. Use state.diagnostics only when the ordinary checks don’t explain the gap.
  4. Keep the earlier result as evidence, but don’t combine snapshots as if they shared one completion boundary.
← No item activity appearsNext: Solare result is incomplete →

Guides/Troubleshooting

Solare result is incomplete

Use the terminal status to tell a missed Leaderboard load, incomplete acquisition and unsupported structural geometry apart.

Match the returned status

Restart first

The client caches the Leaderboard after its first load. Before any retry, restart the game, start capture, then open the tab once.

See also

Status meanings · evidence and health

no-traffic
No usable inbound game-server traffic. Next: verify the shared live-capture setup; if the Leaderboard was already opened, restart the game first.
menu-context
Solare menu or history-like traffic, but no complete Leaderboard response. Next: restart the game, start capture, then open the Leaderboard tab itself.
ranked-partial
Ranked structure found, but the class-balanced table and overall cross-check were incomplete. Next: save the evidence, then retry after a game restart.
rich-candidate
The class-balanced table was complete, but the independent overall top-100 cross-check wasn’t captured. Next: save the evidence, then retry after a game restart.
detected-incomplete
Relevant traffic recognized, but acquisition or structural checks didn’t prove a complete snapshot. Next: inspect TCP gaps, native drops, queue overflows and flow evictions, then retry after a game restart.
inconclusive
No supported complete interpretation won. Next: with clean health and a complete Leaderboard load, keep the capture and investigate patch-era layout drift.

Keep completion fail-closed

Don’t loosen gates

Never relax classifier gates or synthesize missing rows. Repeated clean failures after a complete Leaderboard load are evidence to keep for a layout update.

Patch behavior

Patch-recovery boundary

Completion currently needs the 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class-table geometry, an authoritative overall top 100 and exact overlap checks. Early in a season, an underfilled class can make a readable response incomplete, and a new class needs reviewed geometry support once populated traffic exists.

Restart the game and retry a clean capture first.

A complete snapshot can still lack optional details

Missing Elo, aggregate outcomes, performance or raw extensions don’t invalidate confirmed rankings. Check snapshot.overall_capabilities and snapshot.class_table_capabilities; unavailable stays distinct from zero.

← Item state is incompleteNext: Prepare a support report →

Guides/Troubleshooting

Prepare a support report

Share the smallest structured evidence that reproduces the problem, before considering a raw PCAP.

Start every report with the same context

Versions

The snippet prints the toolkit, Python and Scapy versions and the OS build.

import platform
import sys

import scapy

import bdo_toolkit

print(bdo_toolkit.__version__, sys.version.split()[0], scapy.VERSION, platform.platform())
Example outputone Windows machine
1.0.8 3.14.0 2.7.0 Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0
  • Whether the run was live or replayed, and whether the problem repeats in a fresh process and capture.
  • For live capture: the adapter name, whether it’s physical or virtual, and its model and driver version when available.
  • On Windows: the Npcap version, and whether WinPcap API-compatible mode is on.
  • With a VPN: full-tunnel or split routing, and whether its state changed after capture started.
  • The in-game action taken after capture was ready, and the outcome actually received.
  • Where the active opcode profile came from, and whether it was verified after the current weekly patch.

Add the workflow’s own diagnostics

Recorded elsewhere?

For a Wireshark or Dumpcap recording, include its version too.

Item events
The resolved session.endpoint, final session.health and session.decoder_health, diagnostic messages, and one redacted event.to_dict() if an unexpected event appeared.
Inventory & town storage
hydration_detected, identity_complete, coverage, warnings and decoder_health. Add capture diagnostics only if the ordinary schema-v5 result doesn’t explain the gap.
Calibration
The terminal message, ignored reasons, DirectionEvidence, action mode, controlled quantity and destination town; never just “calibration failed”.
Arena of Solare
Status and message, ranked, overall and cross-check counts, both capability sets, capture health and layout identifiers. The support report example prints them.
Grind tracking
Final status.to_dict() and health.to_dict(), any GrindFeatureError reasons, and which readers were enabled.

Escalate to raw data only when necessary

Don’t publish captures

PCAPs and serialized results can hold endpoints, item state, player names, rankings and identifier-like bytes. Read what outputs contain first.

A structured report usually tells setup, profile, acquisition and geometry problems apart without exposing the traffic. If a maintainer needs the PCAP, agree first on the smallest capture window and a private transfer method. Never include raw session identifiers or private packet contents in a public report.

← Solare result is incompleteNext: Safety & privacy →

Guides

Safety & privacy

Passive capture never controls the game, but the traffic and results it records can still hold private application and player data.

Passive and read-only boundary

Never

Send, inject, modify, delay or replay traffic to the game; automate gameplay; read process memory; or bypass anti-cheat.

The toolkit only observes local traffic. Calibration analyzes controlled traffic and writes nothing but an explicit local profile file. Optional PCAP, JSONL, item-state, Solare, raw-message and origin-candidate outputs are local writes your application asks for.

What saved outputs can contain

Overwrite protection

Refusing to overwrite protects an existing file; it doesn’t make a new capture safe to publish.

PCAP or PCAPNGevery save_pcap
Network endpoints, complete captured payloads, decoded and undecoded game data, and identifier-like bytes.
Item-event JSONL--jsonl · to_dict()
Timestamps, endpoints, event types, sources, item IDs, quantities, storage destinations and retained evidence.
Item-state JSONto_dict()
Observed inventory, balances, town-storage contents, warnings and decoder health. include_diagnostics=True adds capture diagnostics and the local capture_path.
Solare result JSONto_json() · CLI
Player names, rankings, Elo, aggregate outcomes, recent-result text and per-class performance. Raw sections need explicit retention and serialization.
XP and Agris readingsto_dict() · --jsonl
Your character’s level and XP, Agris balances and cap, timestamps and connection endpoints.
Raw message dumpsRawMessage.to_dict()
Every server-to-client payload byte from the selected ports, with endpoints and timestamps.
Origin-candidate JSONsave()
Structural observations, opaque IDs and short digests for review; raw shared tokens are never stored.

Share the minimum necessary

  1. Start with the structured fields in Prepare a support report.
  2. Read the exact file before sending it. Redact endpoints, local paths, names, item contents and identifiers the diagnosis doesn’t need.
  3. Keep include_diagnostics, retain_raw_extensions and include_raw off unless the recipient needs those fields.
  4. Use the shortest useful capture window, a private transfer channel, and an agreed retention and deletion plan.

functionsbdo_toolkit

Capture functions

Two iterators that decode BDOEvent values: replay_pcap() from a saved recording, capture_live() from live traffic.

status
stable
session
LiveCaptureSession
guide
Item events

replay_pcap()

Lazy start

Both functions are generators. Validation, profile loading and capture start on the first next(), not at the call.

Order

In both, a storage event can arrive after later events of other types while its source is classified. Timestamps are unchanged.

function
bdo_toolkit.replay_pcap( path: str | Path, *, opcode_profile: str | Path | OpcodeProfile, ports: tuple[int, ...] = (8884, 8885, 8889), event_filter: EventFilter | None = None, origin_observer: Callable[[CompanionObservation], object] | None = None, on_diagnostic: Callable[[DecoderDiagnostic], object] | None = None, ) -> Iterator[BDOEvent]
YieldsBDOEventeach decoded event that passes the filter · delivery order

Replays a .pcap or .pcapng file incrementally. With event_filter=None the stream is complete.

Example

Matching profile

Decode a recording with the profile from its patch era: matching-era profile.

from bdo_toolkit import replay_pcap

for event in replay_pcap(
    "path/to/session.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
):
    print(event.to_dict())
Example outputfirst event · abridged
{'event_type': 'item_received', 'timestamp': 1783663561.245, 'timestamp_iso': '2026-07-10T06:06:01.245Z', 'flow': {'source_ip': '203.0.113.20', 'source_port': 8889, 'destination_ip': '192.0.2.42', 'destination_port': 51824}, 'item_id': 7003, 'quantity': 6, 'source': 'Gathering', 'confidence': 'observed', ...}

capture_live()

Setup

Needs an opcode profile and the live-capture prerequisites.

Stop control

The iterator blocks between events. To stop from another thread, use LiveCaptureSession.

function
bdo_toolkit.capture_live(*, opcode_profile: str | Path | OpcodeProfile, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, event_filter: EventFilter | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = None, origin_observer: Callable[[CompanionObservation], object] | None = None, on_diagnostic: Callable[[DecoderDiagnostic], object] | None = None, ) -> Iterator[BDOEvent]
YieldsBDOEventeach decoded event that passes the filter · delivery order

A passive, blocking iterator for scripts and command-line tools. With event_filter=None it delivers EventFilter.activity(): no character-load snapshot or neutral records.

Example

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

potato_receipts = EventFilter(
    event_types={"item_received"},
    sources={"Gathering"},
    item_ids={7003},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=potato_receipts,
):
    print(event.event_type, event.source, event.item_id, event.quantity)
from bdo_toolkit import capture_live

for event in capture_live(opcode_profile="opcodes.local"):
    if (
        event.item_id == 7003
        and event.event_type == "item_received"
        and event.source == "Gathering"
    ):
        print(event.event_type, event.source, event.item_id, event.quantity)

The first tab filters delivery; the second checks the default activity stream in your code. For everything, pass EventFilter.all(). Matching rules.

classbdo_toolkit

LiveCaptureSession

Live capture with start and stop under your control. One consumer reads BDOEvent values through events() or poll().

status
stable
asyncio
AsyncLiveCaptureSession
scripts
capture_live()
guide
Item events
class
bdo_toolkit.LiveCaptureSession(*, opcode_profile: str | Path | OpcodeProfile, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, event_filter: EventFilter | None = None, origin_observer: Callable[[CompanionObservation], object] | None = None, on_diagnostic: Callable[[DecoderDiagnostic], object] | None = None, )
YieldsBDOEvent via events()one consumer · poll() is the timeout-aware alternative

Example

One consumer

events() and poll() share one queue, and overlapping consumers silently split events. Fan out from your single loop.

Setup

Needs an opcode profile and the live-capture prerequisites.

from threading import Thread

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, LiveCaptureSession

mob_drops = EventFilter(sources={"Mob Drop"})
session = LiveCaptureSession(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=mob_drops,
)
worker_errors = []


def consume_events():
    try:
        for event in session.events():
            print(event.event_type, event.source, event.item_id, event.quantity)
    except BaseException as exc:
        if not worker_errors:
            worker_errors.append(exc)


worker = Thread(target=consume_events, daemon=True)


def on_start():
    session.start()
    print("Capture started")
    worker.start()


def on_stop():
    session.stop()
    worker.join()
    if worker_errors:
        raise worker_errors[0]
    session.raise_if_failed()
    print("Capture stopped:", session.stop_reason)
from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, LiveCaptureSession

mob_drops = EventFilter(sources={"Mob Drop"})
session = LiveCaptureSession(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=mob_drops,
)

def on_start():
    session.start()
    print("Capture started")


def on_ui_timer():
    while (event := session.poll(timeout=0)) is not None:
        print(event.event_type, event.source, event.item_id, event.quantity)


def on_stop():
    session.stop()
    on_ui_timer()  # Display events finalized during shutdown.
    print("Capture stopped:", session.stop_reason)

The worker keeps the first consumer failure, stops on the control thread, joins, then re-raises. With the UI form, call on_ui_timer() periodically and once after stop().

Capture started
item_received Mob Drop 767248 8
item_received Mob Drop 11882 1
Capture stopped: requested

Methods

Inside callbacks

In origin_observer or on_diagnostic, only request_stop() is allowed. Blocking control or consumption there raises RuntimeError.

start()→ None
Opens the adapter and returns once capture is ready; decoding continues in the background. Success makes the session single-use. After a failed start, retry start() only if cleanup_incomplete is False; otherwise retry stop().
stop()→ None
Stops intake, waits for the decoder, finalizes pending storage classification and wakes the consumer. It doesn’t drain the queue or re-raise a retained failure: keep consuming, or call raise_if_failed(). Repeat calls are no-ops.
request_stop()→ None
Requests shutdown without waiting; the stop to use inside callbacks. Keep consuming, then call stop() from control code to finish.
events()→ Iterator[BDOEvent]
Blocking iterator for the one consumer, without busy-waiting. After stop() it drains queued and shutdown-finalized events, then ends or raises the retained failure. Breaking out doesn’t stop capture.
poll(timeout=None)→ BDOEvent | None
One event, for timer-driven loops. 0 checks without waiting; None waits for an event or stop. Returns None on timeout or after the final event (check stopped), and re-raises a retained failure once buffered events drain.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Re-raises the first retained failure now, in the calling thread.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter calls start(). Exit stops a started session that hasn’t stopped, without raise_if_failed(); the block’s exception stays primary.

Packet capture is active.

stoppedbool

Shutdown finalization completed.

requested, capture-ended or error, after stop.

errorBaseException | None

First retained failure: startup, capture, decoding, callback or cleanup.

cleanup_incompletebool

Release unverified — keep the session, retry stop(). Success clears it, not error. Internals.

endpointCaptureEndpoint | None

Resolved interface, local IPv4 and BPF filter, once startup is attempted.

healthLiveCaptureHealth

Immutable capture-integrity snapshot. Counter families may be sampled at adjacent instants.

decoder_healthDecoderHealth

Storage schema and destination compatibility, apart from capture integrity.

classbdo_toolkit

AsyncLiveCaptureSession

Awaitable live capture for asyncio applications. One task reads BDOEvent values through async for, events() or poll().

status
stable
sync
LiveCaptureSession
guide
Asyncio integration
class
bdo_toolkit.AsyncLiveCaptureSession(*, opcode_profile: str | Path | OpcodeProfile, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, event_filter: EventFilter | None = None, origin_observer: Callable[[CompanionObservation], object] | None = None, on_diagnostic: Callable[[DecoderDiagnostic], object] | None = None, )
YieldsBDOEvent via events()one consumer · async for uses events() · await poll() is timeout-aware

Example

One consumer

async for, events() and poll() share one queue; a second concurrent consumer raises RuntimeError. Fan out from one task.

Setup

Needs an opcode profile and the live-capture prerequisites.

import asyncio

from bdo_toolkit import AsyncLiveCaptureSession, EventFilter


async def consume(session: AsyncLiveCaptureSession) -> None:
    async for event in session:
        print(event.format_human())


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncLiveCaptureSession(
        opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
        event_filter=EventFilter(
            event_types={"item_received", "storage_delta"},
        ),
    ) as session:
        consumer = asyncio.create_task(consume(session))
        try:
            await asyncio.to_thread(
                input,
                "Capture started. Press Enter to stop.\n",
            )
        finally:
            await session.stop()
            await consumer


asyncio.run(main())

input() stands in for your app’s Stop control. Stopping first, then awaiting the consumer, keeps events finalized during shutdown.

Capture started. Press Enter to stop.

Methods

Inside callbacks

In origin_observer or on_diagnostic, only request_stop() is allowed. Blocking control or consumption there raises RuntimeError.

await start()→ None
Opens capture off the event loop and returns once the adapter is ready. One start attempt per session, even a failed or cancelled one; if cleanup is incomplete, keep the session and retry stop().
await stop()→ None
Finalizes without blocking the loop; concurrent callers share one shutdown. It doesn’t consume buffered events or re-raise a retained failure: keep consuming, or call raise_if_failed(). Repeat calls return.
request_stop()→ None
Requests shutdown without waiting; the stop to use inside callbacks. Keep consuming, then await stop().
events()→ AsyncIterator[BDOEvent]
Async iterator for the one consumer; waits without blocking the loop. After stop it drains queued and shutdown-finalized events, then ends or raises the retained failure. Breaking out doesn’t stop capture, and unread events stay available.
await poll(timeout=None)→ BDOEvent | None
One event, or None on timeout or after the final event. 0 checks at once. A retained failure is raised once buffered events drain. Cancelling a pending poll stops the session.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Re-raises the retained failure now, synchronously.
__aiter__async iteration
async for event in session uses events(); it isn’t a second consumer.
__aenter__ · __aexit__async context protocol
Enter awaits start(). Exit stops a session that hasn’t stopped, without raise_if_failed(); the block’s exception stays primary.

Cancellation stops

Cancelling a pending poll() or iterator-next stops the session, including through asyncio.wait_for(). For a wait that can time out, pass poll(timeout=…).

LiveCaptureOptions

Immutable live-capture settings: the shared packet settings plus bounded queues for raw packets and decoded events. Every accepting API builds LiveCaptureOptions() when you pass live_options=None.

dataclass
bdo_toolkit.LiveCaptureOptions( interface: str | None = None, local_ip: str | None = None, ports: tuple[int, ...] = (8884, 8885, 8889), use_bpf: bool = True, auto_local_ip: bool = True, event_queue_size: int = 1024, packet_queue_size: int = 4096, )

Example

Sizing

Watch session.health on an explicit LiveCaptureSession; capture_live() doesn’t expose its session.

Two filters

use_bpf reduces raw traffic entering Python. EventFilter selects finished events after source classification.

from bdo_toolkit import LiveCaptureOptions, capture_live

options = LiveCaptureOptions(
    event_queue_size=2048,
    packet_queue_size=8192,
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    live_options=options,
):
    print(event.format_human())

Keeps the packet defaults and doubles both queue bounds.

Parameters

Backlog, not reach

Larger queues absorb a briefly slow consumer or decoder, at the cost of memory. They can’t reveal traffic on another adapter, decrypt a VPN or recover interface drops.

interfacestr | None = None
Inherited adapter name.
local_ipstr | None = None
Inherited destination-IPv4 restriction.
portstuple[int, ...] = (8884, 8885, 8889)
Inherited server source ports.
use_bpfbool = True
Inherited backend or Python-side filtering.
auto_local_ipbool = True
Inherited default-route local-IP policy.
event_queue_sizeint = 1024
Decoded events waiting for the one consumer. When full, the decoder waits for space; shutdown-finalized events are kept separately.
packet_queue_sizeint = 4096
Captured packets waiting for decoding. The native callback never waits: an overflow is known loss, so capture stops and records CaptureIntegrityError.
native callback→packet queue→decoder worker→event queue→one consumer

A full event queue pauses decoding, so a consumer that stays slow eventually overflows the packet queue.

  • Grind tracking: GrindSession, LiveXPSession, LiveAgrisSession, AsyncLiveAgrisSession, calibrate_agris_live(), calibrate_agris_and_update()

Example

Selection isn’t proof

An adapter can open cleanly while another one carries the BDO connection. After startup, check the session’s endpoint, then perform one known action and look for its event.

No game traffic?

Troubleshoot shared acquisition.

When automatic selection picks the wrong adapter, list the interfaces and pass the exact Scapy name, not an IP address, as interface=.

from bdo_toolkit import PacketCaptureOptions
from scapy.all import show_interfaces

show_interfaces()
options = PacketCaptureOptions(
    interface="Ethernet",  # Replace with the displayed name
)

Parameters

interfacestr | None = None
Capture adapter name. None tries the generic default route, not BDO’s own route. Availability is checked at start.
local_ipstr | None = None
Destination IPv4 restriction, not an adapter selector; validated and normalized at construction. With an explicit interface, None leaves it unrestricted.
portstuple[int, ...] = (8884, 8885, 8889)
Server source ports treated as BDO traffic: at least one int from 1 to 65,535. Duplicates are dropped; first-seen order is kept.
use_bpfbool = True
Filters in the capture backend. False brings more traffic into Python and applies the same source-port and destination checks there; the adapter doesn’t change.
auto_local_ipbool = True
With interface and local_ip both omitted, also restricts capture to the default route’s local IPv4, if discovery finds one. False keeps the default-route adapter without that restriction.

How selection resolves

Construct vs start

Values are validated at construction. Adapter availability, permissions, driver and BPF support, and route discovery are checked when capture starts.

Automatic selection follows the computer’s generic default IPv4 route, not the route of one BDO connection. With several adapters or a VPN, pin the adapter.

typesbdo_toolkit

Diagnostics & health

Four checks on a capture: what it selected (endpoint), whether packets were lost locally (health), whether the profile still decodes storage (decoder_health), and why not (on_diagnostic=). Integrity and compatibility are independent: a clean capture can still use an incompatible post-patch profile.

status
stable
session
LiveCaptureSession
guide
No game traffic

Example

Final values

Read health after stopping and draining. Values read during capture are observational and can worsen later.

capture_live()

The script iterator hides its session’s health and endpoint, but still accepts on_diagnostic=.

import time

from bdo_toolkit import LiveCaptureSession

with LiveCaptureSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        session.poll(timeout=1.0)  # handle events here
    session.stop()
    while session.poll(timeout=0) is not None:
        pass  # drain events finalized during shutdown

health = session.health
decoder = session.decoder_health
print("filter:", session.endpoint.bpf_filter)
print("capture clean:", health.capture_is_clean)
print("storage decoder:", decoder.storage_status)
if not health.capture_is_clean:
    print(health.to_dict())
if decoder.storage_is_compatible is False:
    print(decoder.to_dict())
Example outputa minute that included one storage deposit
filter: tcp and (src port 8884 or src port 8885 or src port 8889) and dst host 192.0.2.42
capture clean: True
storage decoder: compatible
ResultMeansDo
capture_is_clean is TrueNo known local loss. Not proof that upstream delivery was completeAccept, subject to your own completeness rules
capture_is_clean is FalseAt least one loss indicator is nonzeroInspect to_dict(); discard, retry or mark the result incomplete
storage_status == "compatible"Observed storage traffic decoded with this profileUse storage results, subject to capture integrity
storage_status == "not_observed"No storage message decided it either wayInfer nothing from silence
storage_status == "incompatible"Required profile fields are missing, or storage evidence contradicted the profileRead the diagnostics; recalibrate or update the location registry as they direct

LiveCaptureHealth

Clean isn’t complete

capture_is_clean covers known local loss only. Counter families read mid-capture may be sampled at adjacent instants.

CaptureIntegrityError

Recovery

Capture bounds and backpressure

exception
bdo_toolkit.CaptureIntegrityError(RuntimeError)

Raised when the raw-packet queue overflows, which proves local loss. The session stops fail-closed: normal consumption delivers buffered events first, and raise_if_failed() reports it at once. Treat the run as incomplete.

Silence

not_observed is neither success nor failure: no storage message decided it.

Diagnostic codes

Fail-closed

Numeric storage IDs stay visible, health turns incompatible, and no town is ever guessed. Names never come from source.

storage_decoder_incompatible
Required storage fields are missing, or observed geometry contradicts the profile, including top-level messages shorter than every applicable layout. Compact count-zero envelopes stay neutral for snapshot validation.
storage_destination_unavailable
A storage wrapper decoded without a usable destination value.
storage_destination_unrecognized
The numeric destination is kept but isn’t in the location registry.
storage_destination_schema_mismatch
Cross-wrapper evidence contradicts the profile’s destination field. Existing events aren’t relabeled.

Recalibrate when destination geometry changed; otherwise inspect the observed IDs and the registry. Storage troubleshooting.

Receive decoder diagnostics

Fast and thread-safe

Replay calls it on the iterator thread; live capture may call it from several session threads. It’s never awaited.

Don’t block

Inside the callback, never call stop(), poll() or iterate. Use request_stop(), then finish from control code.

on_diagnostic= takes a synchronous Callable[[DecoderDiagnostic], object] on replay_pcap(), capture_live(), LiveCaptureSession and AsyncLiveCaptureSession. Diagnostics bypass EventFilter.

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, LiveCaptureSession


def report_decoder_problem(diagnostic):
    print(diagnostic.code, diagnostic.requested_storage_ids)
    print(diagnostic.message)


heidel_deposits = EventFilter(
    event_types={"storage_delta"},
    storage_ids={0x0020},
)

session = LiveCaptureSession(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=heidel_deposits,
    on_diagnostic=report_decoder_problem,
)

storage_ids={0x0020} can’t hide a decoder warning; requested_storage_ids keeps that filter context.

When it runs live

PhaseCalled onIf it raises
StartupThe thread running synchronous startup. Async startup uses the facade’s private worker, not the event-loop threadThe original exception becomes the startup failure, after bounded rollback
Active captureA session-owned decoder or monitor thread; not always the same oneRetained as a background failure. Consumption delivers buffered and shutdown-finalized events first, unless bounded cleanup can’t finish
ShutdownThe thread that owns finalizationSame retained-error, drain and cleanup order

diagnose_capture()

Candidates, not proof

A matching adapter doesn’t show that BDO traffic is visible or decodable. Test the settings with one known action.

See also

diagnose-capture command · no game traffic

function
bdo_toolkit.diagnose_capture(*, timeout: float = 15.0) -> CaptureDiagnosis
ReturnsCaptureDiagnosisconnection candidates, status and messages · nothing applied

Inspects established BDO TCP connections on Windows and matches their local IPv4 to capture adapters, local proxies such as ExitLag included. It captures no packets, needs no profile and applies nothing.

Example

from bdo_toolkit import diagnose_capture

result = diagnose_capture()
print(result.status)
for message in result.messages:
    print(message)
for candidate in result.candidates:
    print(candidate.kind, candidate.interface, candidate.remote_port)
    print(candidate.explanation)

In a GUI, run it on a worker thread.

Parameters

timeoutfloat = 15.0
Positive, finite limit in seconds for Windows connection inspection. Adapter enumeration isn’t covered.

Inspection outcomes

  • Recognizes BlackDesert64 and BlackDesert processes. IPv6 connections are skipped with a message.
  • Unsupported platforms and failed connection inspection return unavailable. If adapter enumeration fails, candidates stay, with interface=None.
  • Each connection–adapter match is one candidate. CaptureDiagnosis.proposals groups compatible ones; none is selected for you.
  • Re-run after reconnecting or changing routes: proxy ports and process IDs are valid only for the observed session.

RaisesShow detailsHide details

ExceptionWhenPhase
ValueErrortimeout is a bool, non-finite or not above zero. Inspection failures are returned in messages insteadcall

CaptureDiagnosis

Private output

Reports include network addresses and process IDs. Review them before sharing.

Local time

format_human() uses the host’s timezone; timestamp_iso is UTC.

from bdo_toolkit import replay_pcap

for event in replay_pcap(

Which optional attributes are set depends on the event type and the profile.

Attributes

Immutable

Toolkit-emitted events are immutable and hashable; supported containers in extra are frozen with them. Arbitrary objects on a hand-built event may not be.

One BDOEvent type; the groups aren’t separate models.

Epoch time of the decoded network message.

Always set live

The | None types belong to the constructible dataclass. Replay and live capture always set opcode, message_length, record_offset and confidence.

to_dict() returns a Python dict. JsonlEventWriter does the JSON encoding.

format_human()→ str
One terminal line in host-local time with the fields this event has. Storage lines read destination='Heidel' storage_id=0x00000020; an unregistered ID may show as UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0xdeadbeef).

valuesbdo_toolkit

Event types & sources

The exact event_type and source strings on BDOEvent, and how unknown values appear.

status
stable
model
BDOEvent
filter
EventFilter

Event types

Unclassified

inventory_record and storage_record failed closed. Count them as neither activity nor state.

Under each name: its kind (live activity, state reported at character load, or unclassified) and the delivery preset that includes it. A filter that names the exact type selects any of them.

loot_previewlive · activity()
Shown in a gathering or loot-preview window before receipt. Not proof it reached inventory.
item_receivedlive · activity()
Inventory receipt or update: a mob drop, gathering reward or storage withdrawal (source="Storage"). quantity is the record amount, not a proven stack total.
storage_deltalive · activity()
Proven positive addition to town storage; quantity is the amount added. source names a confirmed manual or worker origin when known. Withdrawals are item_received.
inventory_snapshotexisting state · snapshot_records()
Inventory amount held at login or a character switch, with source="Character Load". Unsigned 64-bit; zero stays unresolved. Not an acquisition or the whole inventory.
storage_snapshotexisting state · snapshot_records()
Town-storage amount held at character load, with source=None. Not a deposit or the whole town.
inventory_recordunclassified · all()
Decoded, but the profile lacks the context field to prove receipt or existing state.
storage_recordunclassified · all()
Decoded with source=None; evidence proved neither a live addition nor existing state.

Known source labels

See also

How origin is inferred · destination fields · filter by source or storage ID

source is the known origin, producing system or context. Each label below is one exact, case-sensitive string; None means unresolved or not applicable.

Context labelsdecoded from the record’s context bytes

  • Character Load
  • Gathering
  • Mob Drop
  • Storage
  • Central Market
  • Black Spirit Safe
  • Challenges
  • In-Game Mail
  • Box/Bundle
  • NPC Exchange
  • NPC Shop
  • Choose Your Rewards Box
  • NPC Sell
  • Event Adventures
  • Remote Inventory

Inferred originsset on confirmed storage additions; not context-byte labels

  • Player Inventory
  • Worker Production

An unresolved live storage addition has source=None, as do storage hydration and unresolved storage records:

def is_unresolved_deposit(event):
    return event.event_type == "storage_delta" and event.source is None

source="Storage" can still appear on the item_received from a storage withdrawal.

Unknown values

UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0xdeadbeef)display text
Shown for a decoded nonzero storage_id missing from the location registry; no town is guessed or stored. The event keeps the numeric storage_id with storage_name=None, and source stays the separately classified origin, or None. See the unknown-key contract.
UNKNOWN(0x…)source value
An unrecognized generic non-storage context. raw_context keeps the bytes when the profile exposes them.
