dataclassbdo_toolkit

EventFilter

An immutable selector for finished BDOEvent values. Each configured criterion matches exactly, and all of them must pass.

status
stable
values
Event types & sources
guide
Filter item activity
dataclass
bdo_toolkit.EventFilter(*, event_types: Iterable[str] | None = None, sources: Iterable[str] | None = None, storage_ids: Iterable[int] | None = None, item_ids: Iterable[int] | None = None, )

Example

None vs empty filter

EventFilter() is unrestricted. event_filter=None means whatever the API defines: every event for replay, activity() for live capture.

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter, capture_live

heidel_worker_production = EventFilter(
    event_types={"storage_delta"},
    sources={"Worker Production"},
    storage_ids={0x0020},
    item_ids={7003, 4607},
)

for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    event_filter=heidel_worker_production,
):
    print(
        event.source,
        event.storage_name,
        f"0x{event.storage_id:08x}",
        event.item_id,
        event.quantity,
    )
Example outputone matching worker production
Worker Production Heidel 0x00000020 4607 18

All four criteria must match. source names the producing system and storage_id the destination; show storage_name, but persist the numeric ID.

To keep every confirmed live addition to Heidel, drop the source and item criteria:

from bdo_toolkit import EventFilter

heidel_activity = EventFilter(
    event_types={"storage_delta"},
    storage_ids={0x0020},
)

Parameters

event_typesIterable[str] | None = None
Exact event type, read from event.event_type. Stored as frozenset[str].
sourcesIterable[str] | None = None
Exact, case-sensitive source label, read from event.source. Stored as frozenset[str].
storage_idsIterable[int] | None = None
Exact numeric storage destination, read from event.storage_id. Stored as frozenset[int].
item_idsIterable[int] | None = None
Exact raw item ID, read from event.item_id. Stored as frozenset[int].

Matching rules

ConfigurationResult
Several values in one criterionAny of them may match (OR)
Several configured criteriaEvery criterion must match (AND)
NoneThat criterion isn’t tested
An empty iterableThat criterion matches nothing, so every event is rejected

Delivery presets

EventFilter.activity()loot_preview · item_received · storage_delta
Ordinary live item activity; the default when a live API gets no filter.
EventFilter.snapshot_records()inventory_snapshot · storage_snapshot
Proven character-load records, without neutral ones. Not an assembled item-state snapshot.
EventFilter.all()no restriction
Everything, neutral inventory_record and storage_record included.

Methods

EventFilter.activity()→ EventFilter
The live-activity preset.
EventFilter.snapshot_records()→ EventFilter
The proven character-load record preset.
EventFilter.all()→ EventFilter
An unrestricted filter, equal to EventFilter().
EventFilter.from_values(*, event_types=None, sources=None, storage_ids=None, item_ids=None)→ EventFilter
Named constructor with the same inputs and normalization.
allows(event)→ bool
Whether event passes every configured criterion.

RaisesShow detailsHide details

Normalization

Each iterable is copied into a frozenset, so the filter can’t change. Unknown hashable values are kept as given and normally match nothing.

ExceptionWhenPhase
TypeErrorA criterion is a bare str or bytes; wrap a single value in a collectionconstruct
TypeErrorAn element is unhashableconstruct

Stream behavior

  • The stream stays yours: writers never close it or call flush().
  • write() is synchronous and returns None.
  • Stream I/O errors, and formatting or JSON-serialization errors, propagate to the caller.

from bdo_toolkit import JsonlEventWriter, replay_pcap

with open("events.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:

functionbdo_toolkit

fetch_opcode_profile()

Fetches, verifies and atomically installs one remote item profile at a path you own. Capture APIs never call it for you.

status
stable
local
load_opcode_profile()
guide
Install the maintained profile
function
bdo_toolkit.fetch_opcode_profile( url: str, destination: str | Path, *, timeout: float = 10.0, max_bytes: int = 1_048_576, backup: bool = True, ) -> ProfileFetchResult
ReturnsProfileFetchResultfrozen · the installed profile, source URL, revision, ETag and any backup

Example

Replaces the file

An existing destination is backed up by default, then replaced atomically. There’s no inter-process lock: run one writer per path.

Revisions move

The stable channel later points at newer promoted revisions. Read result.revision; don’t hard-code one.

from bdo_toolkit import fetch_opcode_profile

result = fetch_opcode_profile(
    "https://ychwu.github.io/bdo-toolkit-profiles/channels/na-eu/stable.json",
    "opcodes.local",
)

Profile errors

RemoteProfileError reports failed remote acquisition or verification; ProfileError reports invalid stored profile data.

status

Profile troubleshooting

Example

Catch order

RemoteProfileError subclasses ProfileError. When you handle both in one try, catch it first.

from bdo_toolkit import (
    ProfileError,
    RemoteProfileError,
    fetch_opcode_profile,
    load_opcode_profile,
)

try:
    fetch_opcode_profile(
        "https://ychwu.github.io/bdo-toolkit-profiles/channels/na-eu/stable.json",
        "opcodes.local",
    )
except RemoteProfileError as exc:
    print(f"Fetch failed; the installed profile is unchanged: {exc}")

try:
    profile = load_opcode_profile("opcodes.local")
except ProfileError as exc:
    print(f"Invalid profile file: {exc}")

RemoteProfileError

Not this error

Wrong argument types raise TypeError, bad numeric limits ValueError, and local file failures keep their OSError subclasses.

exception
bdo_toolkit.RemoteProfileError(ProfileError)

The remote URL, transport, response size, envelope, digest or embedded-profile validation failed in fetch_opcode_profile(). Verification failures leave the destination untouched.

ProfileError

Structure, not currentness

It reports structural invalidity, not whether a valid profile still matches current traffic.

exception
bdo_toolkit.ProfileError(ValueError)

Profile or origin-candidate JSON couldn’t be parsed, or violates its stored schema. A missing path raises FileNotFoundError instead.

Runs live or recorded calibration and writes eligible promoted specs to a local profile. An empty result returns (result, None) and leaves the file untouched.

Example

Timing

Start the call before the guided in-game sequence and press Ctrl+C after the final action.

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import calibrate_and_update

result, update = calibrate_and_update(
    "path/to/opcodes.local.json",
    item_id=15156,
    quantity=1,
)

print(result.summary())
if update is not None:
    print(update.summary())

To analyze an existing recording instead, pass pcap=.

    input("Perform the controlled calibration actions, then press Enter.")

Methods

start()→ None
Resets retained evidence and error, opens the adapter and returns once capture is ready; processing continues in the background. A finished run can start again; with incomplete cleanup, retry stop() instead.
stop()→ CalibrationResult
Stops capture, verifies shutdown, finalizes TCP reassembly, scores the newest retained frame tail and returns the result. Acquisition or cleanup failures raise before scoring. Repeat stops return the same object.
wait(timeout=None)→ CalibrationResult | None
Waits for automatic finalization. A finite timeout returns None without stopping capture; stored background failures raise. Call it inside the with block to keep ownership.
request_stop()→ None
Requests shutdown and final analysis without waiting; safe inside callbacks. Needs a started session.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Re-raises the first retained acquisition failure in the calling thread. While active, it also raises RuntimeError if capture ended unexpectedly; a no-op before start and after a clean stop.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter starts the session if it isn’t active. Exit stops an active capture as a safety net; it neither scores nor returns a result. Stored background failures surface on exit.

Attributes

runningbool

Live capture is active.

stoppedbool

Finalization or discard ended. False before start and while cleanup is incomplete.

stop_reasonstr | None

complete, requested, manual, discarded or error; None before the end.

resultCalibrationResult | None

The final result only, after successful finalization.

progressCalibrationProgress | None

Latest replaceable assessment, with stop_on_complete or on_update. Candidates can change or disappear.

errorBaseException | None

First retained startup, capture, assessment, callback or finalization failure of this run.

cleanup_incompletebool

Release unverified — keep the session, retry stop(). A completed retry clears it; any acquisition failure stays visible.

frames_observedint

Reassembled frames seen this run, evicted ones included.

frames_collectedint

Alias of frames_observed; kept after stop(), reset by start().

frames_retainedint

Frames in the newest contiguous tail kept for scoring.

frames_discardedint

Older frames evicted by either retention bound.

bytes_observedint

Frame payload bytes seen this run.

bytes_retainedint

Frame payload bytes kept for scoring.

bytes_discardedint

Frame payload bytes evicted this run.

retention_truncatedbool

Older evidence was evicted; stop() scores only the retained tail.

retentionCalibrationRetention

Atomic evidence snapshot with the configured bounds. stop() attaches the final one to its result.

Live progress and automatic completion advanced

Replace, don’t add up

Each update describes the current retained evidence. Replace your previous assessment instead of accumulating candidates.

Callbacks

They run on the assessment worker or the finalizing thread. Keep them light and use request_stop() inside; blocking same-session calls raise RuntimeError.

stop_on_complete=True finishes once sufficient evidence arrives. on_update receives changes in candidate opcodes, inferred layouts, missing requirements and readiness. Either one enables progress.

  • Automatic transfer calibration needs INVENTORY_TRANSFER, STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA and SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT. Storage also needs two distinct validated counts and unique destination and count fields.
  • An explicit deposit needs storage plus a source decrement, an explicit withdrawal needs a receipt, and loot preview needs its own family.
  • Newly inferred runtime layouts must validate. Known packet loss, flow eviction or a truncated tail blocks automatic readiness.

finalizing is provisional: shutdown and TCP finalization can reveal more evidence, and the final batch pass can still reject calibration. The same finalized frames, order, options and retention give the same result; a longer capture can hold more. Manual stopping stays available and can return a partial result.

Callback errors propagate through the lifecycle methods, and incomplete worker cleanup keeps ownership for a later stop() retry. Only one extra bounded frame snapshot is kept; there’s no progress queue.

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import CalibrationSession

with CalibrationSession(
    item_id=15156, quantity=1, stop_on_complete=True,
    on_update=lambda update: print(update.kind, update.detected_opcodes),
) as session:
    # Perform deposit 1, deposit 4, withdraw 5 while capture listens.
    result = session.wait()
    print(result.summary())

Nothing is written. Review the final result before update_profile(). Runnable: live_calibration_progress.py ↗ · asyncio version.

A frozen transfer-frame observation for guiding the user. It can acknowledge a first deposit before storage count authority exists, but never promotes layouts, decides readiness, stops capture or authorizes a write.

Fields and method

to_json_dict()→ dict[str, object]
Every field; opcode becomes a hex string.

Guiding a five-unstackable wizard

Read the latest observations in frame_number order: a deposit with record_count == item_record_count == item_quantity == 1, then a deposit with all three equal to 4, then a withdrawal with all three equal to 5. The toolkit doesn’t hard-code these sizes, and a stack of five is one record, not five unstackables.

  • Deposit guidance needs a uniquely identified destination and a fresh same-flow source decrement linked by exact instance and quantity.
  • Withdrawal guidance needs an unambiguous Storage source, not just any inventory receipt.
  • Missing, ambiguous or recovery-only evidence can yield no observations even when calibration succeeds; loot-preview sessions yield none. Town restrictions don’t change.

When guidance is missing or uncertain, keep the ordinary calibration path available. Base family indicators on specs, and keep the final readiness, error, retention and stopped checks before enabling Save.

Context exit aborts an unfinished capture. Call stop() inside the block to get the result.

Setup

Needs the live-capture prerequisites. Follow the controlled procedure during capture.

import asyncio

from bdo_toolkit import AsyncCalibrationSession


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncCalibrationSession(item_id=15156, quantity=1) as session:
        await asyncio.to_thread(
            input,
            "Deposit 1; deposit 4; withdraw all 5; press Enter...",
        )
        result = await session.stop()

    print(result.summary())


asyncio.run(main())

asyncio.to_thread() keeps the blocking prompt off the event loop. Review the result, then run update_profile() in a worker so file I/O stays off the loop too.

Parameters

item_id*int
Known item ID to find in captured traffic. Range.
quantityint | None = None
Expected positive uint32 in each matching record. None accepts any plausible quantity.
actionstr = "auto"
Calibration mode. "auto" analyzes both transfer directions.
capture_optionsPacketCaptureOptions | None = None
Live capture settings. None uses the defaults.
context_framesint = 5
Positive same-flow evidence lookback.
min_confidencefloat = 0.8
Finite promotion threshold, from 0 to 1.
max_retained_framesint = 50000
Retained-frame limit; must exceed context_frames.
max_retained_bytesint = 67108864
Positive retained-payload limit in bytes.
stop_on_completebool = False
Stop once the selected action has sufficient evidence, then verify the finalized capture.
on_updateCallable[[CalibrationProgress], object] | None = None
Synchronous callback for changed live assessments, run outside the event loop. It reports progress without stopping automatically.

Methods

await start()→ None
Runs startup off the event loop and returns once the adapter is ready. A finished run can start again. Cancellation waits for startup to settle and aborts a late success; incomplete cleanup stays with this facade.
await stop()→ CalibrationResult
Stops capture and scores off the event loop. Concurrent and repeated calls share one terminal task and return the same object. Cancellation waits for that task; a successful result is kept before CancelledError re-raises.
await abort()→ None
Stops and discards without scoring, when it’s the first terminal action. If stop() began first, it waits and keeps that result. Repeat calls return.
await wait(timeout=None)→ CalibrationResult | None
Waits for automatic finalization. A timeout or cancellation leaves capture running and returns or raises; stored background failures raise. Call it inside the context to keep ownership.
request_stop()→ None
Synchronous, callback-safe request for shutdown and final analysis. Needs a started session.
__aenter__ · __aexit__async context protocol
Enter awaits start(). Exit awaits a stop() already chosen, or aborts an unfinished capture; the block’s exception stays primary if cleanup also fails.

The first stop() or abort() picks the manual outcome, though automatic completion can finish first and context exit keeps a completed result. stop() after abort() raises RuntimeError; abort() after stop() waits and keeps the result.

Attributes

runningbool

Live calibration capture is active.

stoppedbool

Finalization or discard ended. False before start and while cleanup is incomplete.

stop_reasonstr | None

complete, requested, manual, discarded or error; None before the end.

resultCalibrationResult | None

The completed result, even if its waiting stop() caller was cancelled. Reset by the next successful start().

progressCalibrationProgress | None

Latest replaceable assessment, with stop_on_complete or on_update. Candidates can change or disappear.

cleanup_incompletebool

Release unverified — keep the facade, retry stop() or abort(); nothing retries in the background.

frames_observedint

Reassembled frames seen this run, evicted ones included.

frames_collectedint

Alias of frames_observed; kept after a terminal action, reset by start().

frames_retainedint

Frames in the newest contiguous tail kept for scoring.

frames_discardedint

Older frames evicted by either retention bound.

bytes_observedint

Frame payload bytes seen this run.

bytes_retainedint

Frame payload bytes kept for scoring.

bytes_discardedint

Frame payload bytes evicted this run.

retention_truncatedbool

Older evidence was evicted; stop() scores only the retained tail.

retentionCalibrationRetention

Atomic evidence snapshot with the configured bounds.

Live progress and automatic completion advanced

Same rules

The evidence and finalization rules of the sync session apply.

Off the loop

on_update is synchronous and runs outside the event loop. Marshal updates with loop.call_soon_threadsafe.

Cancelling await wait() settles its bounded pending wait and leaves capture running; leaving the async context still cleans up.

import asyncio
from bdo_toolkit import AsyncCalibrationSession

async def main():
    async with AsyncCalibrationSession(
        item_id=15156, quantity=1, stop_on_complete=True,
    ) as session:
        # Perform deposit 1, deposit 4, withdraw 5 while this awaits.
        result = await session.wait()
        print(result.summary())

asyncio.run(main())

functionsbdo_toolkit.calibration

Profile updates

Apply reviewed calibration specs to a local opcode profile, or reset that profile to an explicit empty state.

status
stable
one call
calibrate_and_update()
guide
Manual calibration

update_profile()

Replaces families

replace=True clears the represented families and backup=True copies an existing file first. Empty input does no I/O; an incomplete automatic transfer result is refused before the file is touched.

On every write

profile_active is set, updated_at refreshed and calibration-item metadata applied. promote_origin_candidates() has its own activation rules.

function
bdo_toolkit.calibration.update_profile( result: CalibrationResult | Iterable[MessageSpec], path: str | Path, *, action: str = "auto", replace: bool = True, replace_entire_action: bool = False, backup: bool = True, calibration_item_id: int | None = None, ) -> ProfileUpdate
ReturnsProfileUpdatefrozen · destination, added specs, cleared families, backup and whether the file changed

Persists a reviewed CalibrationResult or iterable of MessageSpec values. By default it clears only the families the specs represent, keeping other families, promoted origin evidence and stored metadata.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import calibrate_pcap, update_profile

result = calibrate_pcap(
    "path/to/unstackable-1-in-4-in-5-out.pcapng",
    item_id=15156,
    quantity=1,
)

# Inspect result.specs before persisting them.
update = update_profile(result, "path/to/opcodes.local.json")
print(update.written, update.backup_path)

An automatic transfer result must prove INVENTORY_TRANSFER, STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA and SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT; the calibration guide has the in-game sequence.

Parameters

result*CalibrationResult | Iterable[MessageSpec]
Reviewed specs to persist. Only a nonempty automatic transfer CalibrationResult gets the three-family readiness check.
path*str | Path
Destination profile. An eligible write creates missing parent directories and a new schema-1 file when needed.
actionstr = "auto"
Completeness and action-wide replacement scope. An explicit direction allows a reviewed partial update; you own its match to the specs.
replacebool = True
Clear the represented families before adding replacements. Advanced · False keeps and deduplicates existing specs.
replace_entire_actionbool = False
Advanced · Clear every family action owns; needs replace=True.
backupbool = True
Copy an existing destination into the sibling opcodes_backups folder before writing.
calibration_item_idint | None = None
Positive uint32 metadata override. None inherits it from a result, or keeps the existing value for a raw iterable.

Update outcomes

Input or modeFile behaviorResult
Empty result or iterableNo profile read, creation, backup or write after input and option checksProfileUpdate(written=False)
Default replacementValidates the profile, clears the represented families, adds the specs, then backs up and writes if the data changedA ProfileUpdate with additions, cleared families, backup and write status
Advanced mergeKeeps existing specs and adds only new structural identities. A duplicate-only merge validates but neither backs up nor writeswritten=False for a duplicate-only no-op
Explicit action or raw iterableSkips the automatic three-family readiness check; you own action and spec consistencyThe usual validation and write rules

Replacement scopes

By default only represented families are cleared. With replace_entire_action=True, action clears these families:

"loot-preview"
LOOT_PREVIEW
"storage-to-inventory"
INVENTORY_TRANSFER, SOURCE_CONTAINER_DECREMENT
"inventory-to-storage"
SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT, SOURCE_ITEM_REFERENCE, STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA
"auto"
Every family of both transfer directions; LOOT_PREVIEW stays untouched.

Raises 5 cases · call → validate → writeShow detailsHide details

Validation boundary

The stored profile is schema-validated, and a proposed loot-preview family gets its runtime ambiguity check. Incomplete non-loot evidence can be stored for later completion.

Replaces everything

The new file recognizes no item messages until repopulated. Prior specs and metadata, promoted origin families included, are removed; backup=True copies the old file first.

Write safety

One writer

Neither function locks across processes. Serialize writes to each destination yourself.

Both functions write UTF-8 JSON to a temporary file in the destination folder, sync it and atomically replace the destination. A requested backup is copied first, into the sibling opcodes_backups folder.

Calibration result types

Immutable analysis results and their nested specs, direction evidence and retention accounting. Creating or inspecting them never writes a profile.

How the types fit together

One call: calibrate_and_update() runs both stages and returns (CalibrationResult, ProfileUpdate | None).

CalibrationResult

Live counters

A finished result’s accounting lives on result.retention. Active sync and async sessions expose direct counters for progress.

A new dict of promoted specs by family. Values are tuples: one capture can promote several layouts for a family.

Check the required transfer families before trusting a result:

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import calibrate_pcap

result = calibrate_pcap(
    "path/to/calibration.pcapng",
    item_id=15156,
    quantity=1,
)

required = {
    "INVENTORY_TRANSFER",
    "SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENT",
    "STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA",
}
if required <= result.events_found:
    print(result.detected_directions())
else:
    print(result.summary())

Each family’s role: transfer families and runtime use.

bdo_toolkit.calibration.MessageSpec( event: str, opcode: int, length: int | None, item_id_offset: int | None = None, quantity_offset: int | None = None, item_instance_offset: int | None = None, context_offset: int | None = None, inventory_slot_offset: int | None = None, repeat_stride: int | None = None, source_instance_offset: int | None = None, quantity_removed_offset: int | None = None, quantity_added_offset: int | None = None, destination_instance_offset: int | None = None, confidence: str = "calibrated", source: str = "auto-calibration", observed_at: str | None = None, score: float | None = None, *, record_count_offset: int | None = None, )

exceptionsbdo_toolkit.calibration

Calibration errors

Two exceptions separate a contradicted explicit direction from evidence that can’t produce a safe decoder profile. Neither leaves a profile written.

status
stable
guide
Fix an incomplete calibration

Example

Catch order

Both subclass ValueError. Catch them before any generic ValueError handler.

from bdo_toolkit.calibration import (
    CalibrationAuthorityError,
    calibrate_and_update,
)

try:
    result, update = calibrate_and_update(
        "path/to/opcodes.local.json",
        item_id=15156,
        quantity=1,
    )
except CalibrationAuthorityError as exc:
    print(f"Profile unchanged; repeat the controlled sequence: {exc}")

The default action="auto" never raises DirectionMismatchError.

DirectionMismatchError

exception
bdo_toolkit.calibration.DirectionMismatchError(ValueError)

The captured structure contradicts an explicitly selected single transfer direction. Only single-direction calibration raises it; action="auto" classifies each direction from the evidence instead.

Analysis returns no result. An active live session finalizes before the exception escapes, and nothing is written.

CalibrationAuthorityError

Don’t hand-edit

Repeat the complete controlled workflow in an allowed town instead of editing the ambiguous fields. Retry procedure.

exception
bdo_toolkit.calibration.CalibrationAuthorityError(ValueError)

A calibration target was captured, but the toolkit can’t prove the authority needed to produce or write a safe decoder profile.

WhereReasonEffect
AnalysisA target storage wrapper was seen, but its destination or declared-count geometry wasn’t uniquely provenNo CalibrationResult is returned
Profile updateA nonempty automatic transfer result lacks INVENTORY_TRANSFER, STORAGE_ITEM_DELTA or SOURCE_STACK_DECREMENTRefused before any profile read, backup, creation or replacement

Example

You call stop

No protocol marker ends a load. Call stop() once the world settles; context exit only cleans up.

Setup

Needs an opcode profile and live-capture prerequisites.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import CharacterLoadSession

with CharacterLoadSession(opcode_profile="opcodes.local") as session:
    input(
        "After a fresh game launch, enter the world for the first time; "
        "press Enter after it settles: "
    )
    state = session.stop()

print(f"Hydration detected: {state.hydration_detected}")
print(f"Inventory stacks: {state.inventory.occupied_stacks}")
print(f"Registered storages observed: {state.storages.registered_count}")

Hydration detected: True
Inventory stacks: 243
Registered storages observed: 34

Missing is not empty

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import analyze_item_state_pcap

state = analyze_item_state_pcap(

)

print(f"Hydration detected: {state.hydration_detected}")
print(f"Inventory stacks: {state.inventory.occupied_stacks}")
print(f"Registered storages observed: {state.storages.registered_count}")

dataclassbdo_toolkit.item_state

ItemStateCaptureLimits

Hard bounds on the evidence one item-state snapshot may retain. Exceeding a bound raises ItemStateCaptureLimitError before the extra evidence is stored — never a truncated snapshot.

status
beta
level
advanced
live
CharacterLoadSession
offline
analyze_item_state_pcap()
dataclass
bdo_toolkit.item_state.ItemStateCaptureLimits( max_relevant_frames: int = 10_000, max_snapshot_records: int = 50_000, max_relevant_bytes: int = 64 * 1024 * 1024, )

Example

Keep the defaults

Both acquisition APIs use ItemStateCaptureLimits() when capture_limits=None. Raise only the bound a measured capture needs.

Diagnostics

snapshot.diagnostics reports the applied limits and the evidence retained.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import (
    ItemStateCaptureLimitError,
    ItemStateCaptureLimits,
    analyze_item_state_pcap,
)

limits = ItemStateCaptureLimits(
    max_relevant_frames=20_000,
    max_snapshot_records=75_000,
    max_relevant_bytes=96 * 1024 * 1024,
)

try:
    snapshot = analyze_item_state_pcap(
        "character-load.pcapng",
        opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
        capture_limits=limits,
    )
except ItemStateCaptureLimitError as exc:
    print(f"{exc.limit_name}: attempted {exc.attempted}, limit {exc.limit}")
else:
    assert snapshot.diagnostics is not None
    print(snapshot.diagnostics.capture_limits.to_dict())

Parameters

max_relevant_framesint = 10_000
Distinct framed messages whose opcode matches a selected inventory or storage layout.
max_snapshot_recordsint = 50_000
Retained snapshot observations, neutral storage-record candidates and live storage-delta markers.
max_relevant_bytesint = 67_108_864
Message bytes retained for those frames (64 MiB).

Validation

Every value must be a positive, non-boolean int; otherwise construction raises ValueError.

Methods

to_dict()→ dict[str, int]
Returns the three bounds as a JSON-ready dictionary.

ItemStateCaptureLimitError

Why it fails

Truncating would hide missing state. See current bounds and inference thresholds.

exception
bdo_toolkit.item_state.ItemStateCaptureLimitError( *, limit_name: str, limit: int, attempted: int )

A RuntimeError raised before the observation that would exceed a bound is retained. The failed analysis returns no partial snapshot.

limit_namestr
The exceeded field: max_relevant_frames, max_snapshot_records or max_relevant_bytes.
limitint
The configured maximum.
attemptedint
The total the rejected observation would have produced.

ItemStateSnapshot

The finite, observed inventory and town-storage state from one live or saved capture. inventory and storages hold the contents; the other fields explain the evidence behind them.

status
beta

dataclass
bdo_toolkit.item_state.ItemStateSnapshot( inventory: InventorySnapshotSummary, storages: StorageContents, provenance: ItemStateProvenance, coverage: ItemStateCoverage, decoder_health: DecoderHealth = DecoderHealth(), warnings: tuple[str, ...] = (), diagnostics: ItemStateDiagnostics | None = None, )

Example

Observed only

Queries cover observed, selected state. A zero means no retained stack matched, not that the account has none. Check identity_complete, coverage, decoder_health and warnings first.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import analyze_item_state_pcap

state = analyze_item_state_pcap(
    "path/to/character-load.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
)
inventory = state.inventory
storages = state.storages

print(
    f"Inventory: {inventory.occupied_stacks} item stacks, "
    f"{inventory.currency_balance_records} known balances"
)
silver = inventory.currency("Silver")
if silver is not None:
    print(f"{silver.currency_name}: {silver.quantity:,}")

inventory_item_id = 44391
print(
    f"Item {inventory_item_id} in inventory: "
    f"{inventory.quantity_for(inventory_item_id):,}"
)

heidel = storages.named("Heidel")
if heidel is not None:
    print(f"Heidel: {heidel.occupied_stacks} occupied stacks")

storage_item_id = 1024
print(
    f"Item {storage_item_id} across town storage: "
    f"{storages.total_quantity(storage_item_id):,}"
)
for storage in storages.locations_for(storage_item_id):
    label = storage.name or f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{storage.storage_id:08x})"
    print(f"  {label}: {storage.quantity_for(storage_item_id):,}")

typesbdo_toolkit.item_state

Inventory contents

state.inventory is an InventorySnapshotSummary: observed item stacks, known balances and provisional container views. Queries match exact encoded item IDs.

status
beta
parent
ItemStateSnapshot.inventory
guide
List character inventory

Example

Exact IDs

The toolkit ships no item-name catalog. Ordinary-stack queries leave out known balances; use currency() for those.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import analyze_item_state_pcap

state = analyze_item_state_pcap(
    "path/to/character-load.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
)
inventory = state.inventory
main = inventory.container_named("Main Inventory")
silver = inventory.currency("Silver")
matching_stacks = inventory.records_for(44391)

print(
    f"{inventory.occupied_stacks} item stacks + "
    f"{inventory.currency_balance_records} currency balances"
)
if main is not None:
    print(f"{main.name}: {main.occupied_stacks} stacks")
if silver is not None:
    print(f"{silver.currency_name}: {silver.quantity:,} (slot {silver.inventory_slot})")
if matching_stacks:
    item = matching_stacks[0]
    print(
        f"item {item.item_id}: quantity={item.quantity}, slot={item.inventory_slot}, "
        f"container={item.container_name}"
    )

typesbdo_toolkit.item_state

Storage contents

state.storages is a StorageContents tuple of the town-storage destinations and stacks observed during the captured load. Later receipts and deposits belong to item events.

status
beta
parent
ItemStateSnapshot.storages
guide
Read one town’s storage

Example

Names and IDs

Name lookup is a convenience; persist the numeric storage_id. Keys, names and confidence: storage-location registry.

Reading zero

A zero means no retained stack matched, not that the account has none. Repeated IDs can be separate stacks, and order isn’t slot order.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import analyze_item_state_pcap

state = analyze_item_state_pcap(
    "path/to/character-load.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
)
storages = state.storages
heidel = storages.named("Heidel")
item_id = 1024

if heidel is not None:
    print(f"Heidel: {heidel.occupied_stacks} occupied stacks")
    print(f"Item {item_id} in Heidel: {heidel.quantity_for(item_id):,}")
print(f"Item {item_id} across town storage: {storages.total_quantity(item_id):,}")
for storage in storages.locations_for(item_id):
    label = storage.name or f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{storage.storage_id:08x})"
    print(f"  {label}: {storage.quantity_for(item_id):,}")

print()
print("HEIDEL CONTENTS")
if heidel is None:
    print("  Heidel was not observed in this capture")
else:
    print(f"  {heidel.occupied_stacks} observed occupied stacks")
    for item in heidel.items:
        print(f"  item_id={item.item_id:<6} quantity={item.quantity:,}")

StorageContents

Not synthesized

Only represented destinations are returned; registered towns absent from the capture are not added.

Selected state

Lookups and totals cover selected observed state only. See empty versus not observed before reading a zero.

class
bdo_toolkit.item_state.StorageContents( values: Iterable[StorageSnapshotSummary] = () )

An immutable tuple with one StorageSnapshotSummary per represented destination; len(), iteration, indexing and slicing work as usual. Iterate to enumerate towns; by_id() and named() look up one.

for storage in state.storages:
    label = storage.name or f"UNKNOWN_STORAGE(0x{storage.storage_id:08x})"
    print(f"{label}: {storage.occupied_stacks} occupied stacks")

Empty versus not observed

Internals

How empty envelopes and repeated sweeps become current state: storage internals.

StateEvidenceReads as
NonemptyOne or more validated item recordsItems are queryable on the summary
Explicitly emptyA validated count-zero envelope in the selected sweepcurrent_state_observed=True, current_empty=True
Earlier onlyEarlier evidence, but the selected sweep didn’t revisit itcurrent_state_observed=False, current_empty=None, current_identity_complete=None, items=()
Registered, not observedNo qualifying record or count-zero envelopeListed in coverage.registered_storage_ids_not_observed; not proof of empty
Unregistered, observedThe numeric ID isn’t in the registryKept with name=None; decoder health turns "incompatible" and warns

Dictionary, not JSON

Encode the result with json.dumps() or your serializer. The key is plural "storages"; destinations sit under payload["storages"]["destinations"].

method
bdo_toolkit.item_state.ItemStateSnapshot.to_dict(*, include_diagnostics=False) -> dict[str, object]

import json

    "schema_version": payload["schema_version"],
    "capture_mode": payload["provenance"]["capture_mode"],

    "identity_complete": payload["identity_complete"],
    "inventory_records": payload["inventory"]["serialized_records"],
    "storage_destinations": payload["storages"]["observed_count"],
    "registered_storages": payload["storages"]["registered_count"],
}
print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))

Diagnostics opt-in

Versioned

Branch on schema_version. Item state is experimental; an incompatible revision will increment it.

Example

Join by ID

Match a storage summary to its diagnostics with the numeric storage_id.

Not contents

These counts explain retained evidence and selection. Current contents stay on state.inventory and state.storages.

from bdo_toolkit.item_state import analyze_item_state_pcap

state = analyze_item_state_pcap(
    "path/to/character-load.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="path/to/matching-opcodes.json",
)
diagnostics = state.diagnostics
if diagnostics is None:
    raise RuntimeError("Diagnostics were not populated")

print(
    f"inventory generations={diagnostics.inventory.generations_observed}; "
    f"groups={diagnostics.inventory.groups}"
)
print(
    f"storage sweeps={diagnostics.storage.sweeps_observed}; "
    f"decoded records={diagnostics.storage.records_decoded}"
)
heidel = state.storages.named("Heidel")
if heidel is not None:
    detail = diagnostics.storage.destination(heidel.storage_id)
    if detail is not None:
        print(
            f"Heidel: raw={detail.raw_records}; "
            f"selected={detail.selected_records}; "
            f"superseded={detail.superseded_records}"
        )

classbdo_toolkit

OriginLearner

A thread-safe, bounded in-memory collector that deduplicates structural companion observations into candidates for review and promotion.

status
stable
level
advanced

promote_origin_candidates()
contract

class
bdo_toolkit.OriginLearner( min_observations: int = 2, *, max_candidates: int = 256, max_observations: int = 10000, )
ReturnsOriginCompanionCandidate via observe()the updated immutable snapshot · save() writes all candidates for review

Example

Learning isn’t classification

Runtime worker classification never waits for this learner or its threshold. Only promote_origin_candidates() changes a profile.

Rerun-safe

Observation IDs deduplicate replayed evidence: feeding the same capture twice doesn’t inflate the counts.

from bdo_toolkit import OriginLearner, replay_pcap

learner = OriginLearner.load("opcodes.origin-candidates.json")
for _event in replay_pcap(
    "path/to/worker-session.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    origin_observer=learner.observe,
):
    pass

print(learner.summary())
learner.save("opcodes.origin-candidates.json")
Example outputillustrative values
observed 1 origin companion family/families; 1 confirmed for promotion (threshold: 2 observation(s))
confirmed: delta=0x0D7E companions=0x1234 -> 0x5678 lengths=(72, 96) observations=2 distinct_tokens=2

A missing candidate file loads as an empty learner, so the same script accumulates evidence across runs. capture_live(..., origin_observer=learner.observe) feeds it live instead.

Watch each observation

from bdo_toolkit import OriginLearner, capture_live

learner = OriginLearner()


def report(observation):
    candidate = learner.observe(observation)
    print(candidate.family_key, candidate.observations)


for event in capture_live(
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
    origin_observer=report,
    capture_seconds=60,
):
    print(event.format_human())

Capture calls the observer synchronously and ignores its return value.

referenceorigin learning

Origin evidence

The structural trust rules and forensic evidence behind inferred storage-source labels.

status
stable
level
advanced
labels
Source labels
pipeline
How origin is inferred

How a companion family becomes trusted

Promotion isn’t evidence

It changes when a complete chain becomes trusted, but never creates worker evidence. Runtime confirmation ignores min_observations.

Patch boundary

New opcode, length and token-offset combinations are rediscovered only while the bounded, ordered relationship stays unambiguous. Changed relationships, prefixes or wrappers can need new protocol work.

A worker chain is three correlated frames: the storage message, then two ordered, complete companion messages within the next 32 frames of the same TCP flow. All three carry the same informative 8-byte token before the storage message’s first item record. Other traffic can interleave, but a storage wrapper can’t act as a companion, and one pair can’t own overlapping storage prefixes.

The family key is the storage opcode, both companion opcodes and both companion lengths. The three opcodes must differ, and a token needs at least six distinct byte values.

confirmation values

profileprofile trust · immediate
A complete chain matching a promoted family.
adjacent-structural-chainconfirmed in session
One unique adjacent pair.
repeated-structural-chainconfirmed in session
The same new family at two distinct chain locations.
unambiguous-bounded-windowconfirmed in session
A single candidate remains when the bounded window closes.
Nonecontested or ambiguous
A pair owns overlapping prefixes, or several unconfirmed candidates remain. There’s no companion verdict.

Example

Optional key

companion_chain appears only when the runtime selected a confirmed shared-token chain.

from bdo_toolkit import replay_pcap

events = replay_pcap(
    "path/to/worker-session.pcapng",
    opcode_profile="opcodes.local",
)
storage_event = next(
    event for event in events
    if "deposit_origin_evidence" in event.extra
)
evidence = storage_event.extra["deposit_origin_evidence"]

print(evidence["worker_companions"])
print(evidence["matching_decrement"])

if "companion_chain" in evidence:
    chain = evidence["companion_chain"]
    print(chain["known_family"], chain["confirmed_family"])
    print(chain["confirmation"])

Promoted neutral-record evidence

An illustrative manual deposit, decoded from an unfamiliar wrapper mode and promoted to a live storage_delta by a matching inventory decrement:

{
  "storage_operation_evidence": {
    "wire_operation": "unknown",
    "inferred_operation": "live",
    "signal": "matching_decrement"
  },
  "deposit_origin_evidence": {
    "worker_companions": false,
    "matching_decrement": true,
    "manual_decrement": {
      "opcode": "0x11AD",
      "message_length": 47,
      "quantity_offset": 27,
      "source_instance_offset": 35,
      "match_kind": "instance-and-quantity",
      "confidence": "observed",
      "instance_matches_destination": true,
      "record_index": 1
    },
    "matching_decrement_record_indexes": [1]
  }
}

manual_decrement is the strongest match. A multi-record group can also carry manual_decrement_matches and matching_decrement_record_indexes. A declared but invalid source instance rejects the candidate instead of falling back to a quantity-only match.

instance-and-quantityconfidence observed
Source and destination instances match, and so does the quantity.
anchored-instance-and-quantityconfidence structural
A plausible source instance and matching quantity identify the decrement, but the destination instance is unavailable or differs.
quantity-onlyconfidence heuristic
The profile has no source_instance_offset: message shape and quantity match, with no instance correlation.

storage_operation_evidence is optional forensic evidence for relational classification. event_type stays the live, snapshot or unresolved discriminator, and quantity the item amount.

functionsbdo_toolkit.solare

Solare capture functions

Capture one live Arena of Solare Leaderboard load, or analyze a saved recording. Both return a SolareCaptureResult.

status
beta
session
LiveSolareSession
guide
Capture a leaderboard load

capture_solare_snapshot()

Not an exception

A readable capture that doesn’t prove the whole leaderboard returns a non-complete result. Check result.complete before reading result.snapshot.

Keep the evidence

Pass save_pcap= so the Leaderboard load can be replayed later. Needs the live-capture prerequisites.

function
bdo_toolkit.solare.capture_solare_snapshot(*, capture_options: PacketCaptureOptions | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = 120.0, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, stop_on_complete: bool = True, retain_raw_extensions: bool = False, on_update: Callable[[SolareUpdate], None] | None = None, capture_buffer_bytes: int = 67108864, ) -> SolareCaptureResult
ReturnsSolareCaptureResultterminal status and evidence · a snapshot only after complete confirmation

A blocking call. Start it before the first Leaderboard load after restarting the game, then open the tab once. It stops after the first confirmed snapshot by default, or returns the best classified result when the window ends, on Ctrl+C, or when the capture source ends.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.solare import capture_solare_snapshot

result = capture_solare_snapshot()
if not result.complete:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
assert snapshot is not None
for player in snapshot.overall_top_100[:5]:
    print(player.global_rank, player.name)
Example outputa complete synthetic capture
1 Player0001
2 Player0002
3 Player0003
4 Player0004
5 Player0005

It waits for the leaderboard response, up to the 120-second default.

Parameters

Sensitive

A saved capture holds private traffic. Keep it out of source control and public reports.

capture_optionsPacketCaptureOptions | None = None
Live capture settings. None uses the defaults.
capture_secondsfloat | None = 120.0
Maximum capture window. None removes the deadline.
save_pcapstr | Path | None = None
Optional new PCAP or PCAPNG recording. Existing files are never overwritten.
stop_on_completebool = True
Stop after the first confirmed snapshot.
retain_raw_extensionsbool = False
Keep validated opaque detail sections. Serializing them also needs include_raw=True.
on_updateCallable[[SolareUpdate], None] | None = None
Synchronous progress callback. An exception from it fails the capture.
capture_buffer_bytesint = 67108864
Requested native capture buffer. Why Solare bursts need it.

replay_solare()

Recording

It must have started before the Leaderboard tab’s first load after a game restart.

function
bdo_toolkit.solare.replay_solare( path: str | Path, *, ports: Iterable[int] = (8884, 8885, 8889), retain_raw_extensions: bool = False, ) -> SolareCaptureResult
ReturnsSolareCaptureResultthe recording’s terminal classification · a snapshot only after complete confirmation

Analyzes one PCAP or PCAPNG with the same structural classifier as live capture. Opcode values are kept only as diagnostic evidence, never as classifier inputs; Solare internals explains the rest.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare("path/to/solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

snapshot = result.snapshot
assert snapshot is not None
leader = snapshot.overall_top_100[0]
print(leader.global_rank, leader.name)

The explicit check turns a normal non-complete result into an application error.

Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.
[capture-ready] passive Solare capture is ready ...; open the Leaderboard tab for its first load after restarting the game
[traffic] inbound game-server traffic is flowing
[ranked-progress] 400 unique ranked players recovered; waiting for class balance and the top-100 cross-check

[snapshot-confirmed] opcode-agnostic Arena of Solare leaderboard confirmed
[finished] Solare capture finished with status complete

snapshot-confirmed marks confirmation; finished is terminal and carries the result, ready for the result and snapshot APIs. Breaking the loop early doesn’t stop capture.

Parameters

Live capture settings.

Methods

One consumer

poll() and updates() share one queue, and nothing stops overlapping consumers. Use one.

Coalesced

The queue keeps at most 64 recent updates and always the newest finished one. It isn’t a durable event log.

start()→ None
Opens capture and returns once the adapter is ready. One attempt per session, even a failed one; an explicit session has no hidden deadline.
updates()→ Iterator[SolareUpdate]
Iterator for the one progress consumer. It yields updates through the terminal finished one, then ends or raises the retained failure. Breaking out doesn’t stop capture.
wait(timeout=None)→ SolareCaptureResult | None
Waits quietly for the terminal result when you don’t need progress. With a timeout it returns None while capture runs; a finished run returns its result or raises its failure.
poll(timeout=None)→ SolareUpdate | None
One update, for a custom deadline, heartbeat or loop. 0 checks without waiting; None waits. Returns None on timeout or after a clean terminal drain.
request_stop()→ None
Requests orderly shutdown without waiting; the stop to use inside on_update. The result still arrives through wait(), stop() or the finished update.
stop()→ SolareCaptureResult
Ends capture now, drains every queued packet and returns the best result. For manual shutdown, deadlines or interruption; not the normal way to wait.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Re-raises the first retained failure now.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter calls start() and returns the session. Exit calls stop(), which re-raises a retained failure; a raising block’s exception stays primary.

stoppedbool

resultSolareCaptureResult | None

The terminal result after finalization.

errorBaseException | None

First retained capture, callback, decoder, writer or cleanup failure.

cleanup_incompletebool

Release unverified — keep the session, retry stop(); nothing retries in the background.

endpointSolareCaptureEndpoint | None

Resolved interface, local IPv4 restriction and BPF filter, after startup.

AsyncLiveSolareSession

Awaitable live Arena of Solare capture with an asynchronous progress stream and one terminal SolareCaptureResult.

status
beta

LiveSolareSession
guide
Asyncio integration
class
bdo_toolkit.solare.AsyncLiveSolareSession(*, capture_options: PacketCaptureOptions | None = None, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, stop_on_complete: bool = True, retain_raw_extensions: bool = False, on_update: Callable[[SolareUpdate], None] | None = None, capture_buffer_bytes: int = 67108864, )
YieldsSolareUpdate via updates()one consumer · async for uses updates() · the terminal finished update carries update.result

Example

One consumer

async for, updates() and poll() share one queue; a second concurrent consumer raises RuntimeError. One wait() caller can run alongside.

Setup

Needs the live-capture prerequisites. Start before the Leaderboard tab’s first load after a game restart.

import asyncio

from bdo_toolkit.solare import AsyncLiveSolareSession


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncLiveSolareSession() as session:
        print("Open the Arena of Solare Leaderboard once.")

        async for update in session.updates():
            print(f"[{update.kind.value}] {update.message}")

    result = session.result
    if result is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Solare capture ended without a result")


asyncio.run(main())

The loop waits without blocking the event loop and ends after the terminal finished update, leaving result ready for the result and snapshot APIs. Its output matches the synchronous example.

Parameters

Live capture settings.

Stop after the first confirmed snapshot.
retain_raw_extensionsbool = False
Keep validated opaque detail sections.

Synchronous progress callback, even here.

Requested native capture buffer.

Methods

Inside on_update

Keep it light and call request_stop() without await. Blocking or consuming there raises RuntimeError.

await start()→ None
Opens capture off the event loop and returns once the adapter is ready. One attempt per session, even a failed or cancelled one; if cleanup is incomplete, keep it and retry await stop().
updates()→ AsyncIterator[SolareUpdate]
Async iterator for the one progress consumer; waits without blocking the loop. It yields updates through the terminal finished one, then ends or raises the retained failure. Breaking out doesn’t stop capture.
await wait(timeout=None)→ SolareCaptureResult | None
Awaits the terminal result quietly when you don’t need progress. With a timeout it returns None while capture runs; after stop it returns terminal state at once.
await poll(timeout=None)→ SolareUpdate | None
One update, for a custom deadline, heartbeat or loop; None on timeout or after the terminal drain. A cancelled poll keeps any update it already took for the next call.
request_stop()→ None
Requests orderly shutdown without waiting or await; safe inside on_update.
await stop()→ SolareCaptureResult
Ends capture now, awaits bounded finalization and returns the best result, or re-raises a retained failure. For manual shutdown, deadlines, cancellation handling or app exit; not the normal way to wait.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Re-raises the first retained failure now, synchronously.
__aiter__async iteration
async for update in session uses updates(); it isn’t a second consumer.
__aenter__ · __aexit__async context protocol
Enter awaits start() and returns the session. Exit awaits stop(), which re-raises a retained failure; a raising block’s exception stays primary.

Cancellation stops

Cancelling a pending poll(), wait() or iterator-next stops the session, including through asyncio.wait_for(). For a wait that can time out, pass timeout=.

Result and progress types

SolareCaptureResult is the terminal outcome of capture or replay. During live capture, SolareUpdate reports progress, and the final update carries the result.

Only a complete result has a snapshot, and construction enforces it. A non-complete result is a normal outcome, not an exception.

SolareDetectionStatus

Not complete?

Solare result is incomplete

enum
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareDetectionStatus(str, Enum)

The terminal or best-known classification of one capture window. Each member is also its serialized string; only COMPLETE permits a snapshot.

COMPLETE"complete"
The full class tables and the authoritative overall ranks 1–100 share at least 20 exact rank/name pairs with no contradiction, and acquisition health was clean at confirmation.
DETECTED_INCOMPLETE"detected-incomplete"
Leaderboard identity recognized, but capture integrity or response completeness failed.
RICH_CANDIDATE"rich-candidate"
The supported 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class-table geometry was recovered, but the independent overall top 100 wasn’t fully confirmed. Evidence calls this class-table response rich.
RANKED_PARTIAL"ranked-partial"
Ranked rows recovered, but the 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class tables or the overall top 100 were incomplete.
MENU_CONTEXT"menu-context"
Solare menu or match-history-like traffic, but no full Leaderboard response.
INCONCLUSIVE"inconclusive"
No complete structural signature was found.
NO_TRAFFIC"no-traffic"
No inbound payload arrived from the selected server ports.

SolareUpdateKind

Confirmed isn’t finished

SNAPSHOT_CONFIRMED is a milestone. FINISHED is terminal and always kept; older intermediate updates can be coalesced in the 64-entry queue.

Why it continues

Capability publication

enum
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareUpdateKind(str, Enum)

The machine-readable stage of a live update, for callbacks, polling and iterators. SolareUpdate.message stays display text.

CAPTURE_READY"capture-ready"
The adapter is open; load the Leaderboard tab now. If it was already opened this game session, restart the game first.
TRAFFIC"traffic"
Inbound payload from a selected game-server port is flowing.
MENU_CONTEXT"menu-context"
Menu or history-like Solare traffic; not leaderboard confirmation.
RANKED_PROGRESS"ranked-progress"
Ranked records are accumulating, announced every 100 players.
RICH_CANDIDATE"rich-candidate"
The supported 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class-table geometry was recovered; the overall top 100 isn’t confirmed yet.
CROSS_CHECK"cross-check"
A partial overall table reached at least 20 exact overlaps with no rank/name contradiction.
SNAPSHOT_CONFIRMED"snapshot-confirmed"
Structure and the full overlap check are confirmed; optional finalization may still run.
WARNING"warning"
Bounded retention or acquisition integrity needs attention. Inspect the final status, evidence and health.
FINISHED"finished"
Capture is finalized; update.result carries the outcome.

SolareLeaderboardSnapshot

The frozen, confirmed Arena of Solare leaderboard, read from result.snapshot after a complete result. Capture and replay never return a partial snapshot.

status

from

Player statistics
dataclass
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareLeaderboardSnapshot( snapshot_id: str, observed_at: float, players: tuple[SolarePlayer, ...], *, overall_top_100: tuple[SolareOverallEntry, ...] = (), class_table_capabilities: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"rankings"}), overall_capabilities: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"rankings"}), )

Example

Two leaderboards

overall_top_100 is the in-game overall board, ranks 1–100. players flattens the 31 × 20 historical or 32 × 20 Agent-era class tables; verified short boards can contain fewer entries. It isn’t a global top 620 or 640.

Separate objects

A player in both collections is two independently decoded objects. Optional values are never copied between them.

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare("path/to/solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
if not result.complete:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")
snapshot = result.snapshot
assert snapshot is not None

overall = snapshot.overall_top_100
class_rows = snapshot.players
lahn = snapshot.class_leaderboard(11)  # 11 = Lahn

name = "ExamplePlayer"
overall_entry = snapshot.get_overall_entry(name)
class_entry = snapshot.get_player(name)

print(f"overall rows={len(overall)}")
print(f"class-table rows={len(class_rows)}; Lahn rows={len(lahn)}")
print(
    f"{name}: overall={overall_entry is not None}; "
    f"class-table={class_entry is not None}"
)
Example outputa synthetic complete snapshot
overall rows=100
class-table rows=620; Lahn rows=20
ExamplePlayer: overall=True; class-table=False

Either lookup can return None on its own; this output shows an overall-only player. Next, read their fields in Player statistics.

Check the right set

Snapshot identity

A semantic hash: no observation time, evidence, health, identifier-like source bytes or raw blobs. How it’s built.

SolareOverallEntry

Direct, never copied

Elo, aggregates and class slots come from the overall response itself, never from a class-table row.

Check first

overall_capabilities says which optional fields exist, for all 100 rows or none.

dataclass
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareOverallEntry( name: str, global_rank: int, *, elo: int | None = None, classes_played: tuple[SolareClassPerformance, ...] = (), total_wins: int | None = None, total_draws: int | None = None, total_losses: int | None = None, )

One frozen row of the in-game overall top 100.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.solare import SolareLeaderboardSnapshot


def show_overall(snapshot: SolareLeaderboardSnapshot, name: str) -> None:
    required = {"elo", "aggregate_performance", "performance"}
    if not required <= snapshot.overall_capabilities:
        raise RuntimeError("overall details are unavailable")

    entry = snapshot.get_overall_entry(name)
    if entry is None:
        raise LookupError(f"{name} is not in the overall top 100")

    print(
        f"{entry.global_rank}. {entry.name} — Elo {entry.elo} — "
        f"overall {entry.total_wins}W/{entry.total_draws}D/"
        f"{entry.total_losses}L ({entry.total_matches} matches)"
    )
    for record in entry.classes_played:
        specialization = (
            record.specialization.name if record.specialization else "unknown"
        )
        print(
            f"  {record.player_class.name}/{specialization}: "
            f"{record.wins}W/{record.draws}D/{record.losses}L "
            f"({record.matches} matches)"
        )
Example outputshow_overall(snapshot, "ExamplePlayer") · synthetic data
1. ExamplePlayer — Elo 3045 — overall 70W/1D/49L (120 matches)
  Lahn/Awakening: 40W/1D/29L (70 matches)
  Sorceress/Succession: 30W/0D/20L (50 matches)

Pass the snapshot of a complete result. Name matching is exact and case-sensitive, and an overall-only player needs no class-table row.

Fields

Slots aren’t the total

A record shows at most three class slots, while its aggregate can cover more activity. Don’t sum classes_played; use total_*.

namestr
Exact display name and lookup value, preserving supported Latin, Korean Hangul, Thai, Japanese kana and Han characters; not a stable player identifier.
global_rankint
Authoritative overall rank, 1–100 in a toolkit-built complete snapshot.
eloint | None
From the overall record, when overall_capabilities has elo.
classes_playedtuple[SolareClassPerformance, ...]
One to three occupied slots, primary first, with performance; otherwise empty.
total_winsint | None
Direct aggregate wins, under aggregate_performance.
total_drawsint | None
Direct aggregate draws, under aggregate_performance. All-zero draws can be discovered when independent header boundaries uniquely identify the counter; ambiguous totals remain unavailable.
total_lossesint | None
Direct aggregate losses, under aggregate_performance.

Properties and method

Hand-built rows

Construction doesn’t check slot count or order, and accepts a partial aggregate. Derived totals are then None and serialization omits the aggregate keys.

total_matchesint | None
total_wins + total_draws + total_losses when all three exist. No separate wire field is known.
total_win_ratefloat | None
Aggregate wins as a percentage of total_matches, to two decimals; None when unavailable or not positive.
primary_classSolareClass | None
Class of the first slot marked primary (slot zero on toolkit-built rows); None without performance.
to_dict(*, include_raw=False)→ dict[str, Any]
The available overall fields. include_raw=True adds retained opaque sections inside the slots.

Check first

bdo_toolkit.solare.SolarePlayer( name: str, global_rank: int, primary_class: SolareClass, *, elo: int | None = None, classes_played: tuple[SolareClassPerformance, ...] = (), )

One frozen row of an in-game class top-20 leaderboard.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.solare import SolareLeaderboardSnapshot

LAHN = 11


def show_lahn_leaders(snapshot: SolareLeaderboardSnapshot) -> None:
    required = {"elo", "performance"}
    if not required <= snapshot.class_table_capabilities:
        raise RuntimeError("class-table details are unavailable")

    for player in snapshot.class_leaderboard(LAHN)[:2]:
        record = player.classes_played[0]
        specialization = (
            record.specialization.name if record.specialization else "unknown"
        )
        print(
            f"{player.global_rank}. {player.name} — Elo {player.elo} — "
            f"Lahn/{specialization}: "
            f"{record.wins}W/{record.draws}D/{record.losses}L"
        )

SolareRawSection advanced

Two opt-ins

retain_raw_extensions=True keeps validated sections while decoding; include_raw=True serializes the kept ones. The CLI’s --include-raw does both.

Opaque

Labels mark suspected regions, not decoded gear or addon fields. Boundaries are patch-sensitive, JSON grows substantially, and bytes can hold unidentified or sensitive values.

dataclass
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareRawSection(offset: int, data: bytes)

Exact bytes from one validated region of a class slot, in either response. Nothing is allocated unless the capture, replay or session was given retain_raw_extensions=True.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare(
    "path/to/solare-leaderboard.pcapng",
    retain_raw_extensions=True,
)
snapshot = result.snapshot
if snapshot is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{result.status.value}: {result.message}")

for source, capabilities, rows in (
    ("class", snapshot.class_table_capabilities, snapshot.players),
    ("overall", snapshot.overall_capabilities, snapshot.overall_top_100),
):
    if "raw_extensions" not in capabilities:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{source} raw extensions are unavailable")
    slot = rows[0].classes_played[0]
    gear = slot.gear_loadout_raw
    addons = slot.skill_addons_raw
    assert gear is not None and addons is not None
    print(source, f"gear={gear.length}", f"addons={addons.length}")

# Raw sections are excluded unless explicitly requested.
json_text = snapshot.to_json(include_raw=True)
Example outputraw bytes not printed
class gear=2001 addons=501
overall gear=2001 addons=501

Offsets vary by response, patch geometry and slot; never hard-code them. Serialization can’t recover raw bytes that weren’t kept, so replay the saved PCAP with retention on.

typesbdo_toolkit.solare

Evidence and health

SolareEvidence explains why a result got its status. SolareCaptureHealth tells classifier rejection apart from incomplete packet acquisition.

status
beta
from
result.evidence
guide
Solare result is incomplete

Example

Clean and complete

Publishing needs both. A clean early stop can be incomplete, and valid structure with a gap, drop, queue overflow or flow eviction returns detected-incomplete with no snapshot.

Safe to share

This report separates no traffic, early stop, packet loss, structural drift and missing optional fields, without player data or a raw capture.

from bdo_toolkit.solare import replay_solare

result = replay_solare("path/to/solare-leaderboard.pcapng")
evidence = result.evidence
health = evidence.health

print("status:", result.status.value)
print("ranked:", evidence.ranked_players)
print("overall:", evidence.overall_players)
print("cross-check:", evidence.exact_cross_check)
print("capture clean:", health.capture_is_clean)
print("gaps:", health.tcp_gap_resets)
print("candidate peak:", health.peak_candidate_frames)
print("rollover:", health.candidate_history_rolled_over)
print("queue/flow loss:", health.packet_queue_overflows, health.flow_state_evictions)
if result.snapshot is not None:
    print("class capabilities:", sorted(result.snapshot.class_table_capabilities))
    print("overall capabilities:", sorted(result.snapshot.overall_capabilities))

SolareCaptureHealth

Scope

Replay covers the whole recording. With stop_on_complete=False, live capture keeps the clean health of its first confirmed snapshot. Counters can span more than the winning window, so rejection stays conservative.

Mechanism

Capture integrity and bounded resources

dataclass
bdo_toolkit.solare.SolareCaptureHealth( payload_segments: int = 0, payload_bytes: int = 0, synchronized_messages: int = 0, retained_large_messages: int = 0, tcp_gap_resets: int = 0, pcap_received: int | None = None, pcap_dropped: int | None = None, pcap_interface_dropped: int | None = None, capture_buffer_bytes: int | None = None, saved_packets: int = 0, candidate_messages_observed: int = 0, candidate_frames_retained: int = 0, candidate_bytes_retained: int = 0, peak_candidate_frames: int = 0, peak_candidate_bytes: int = 0, candidate_frames_evicted: int = 0, candidate_bytes_evicted: int = 0, candidate_history_rolled_over: bool = False, packet_queue_peak: int = 0, packet_queue_overflows: int = 0, flow_state_evictions: int = 0, )

Packet, stream and backend counters that decide whether the leaderboard arrived cleanly enough to publish.

Integrity

capture_is_cleanbool · property
True only with no TCP gap reset, reported packet drop, queue overflow or flow eviction. Unavailable offline drop counters and candidate rollover alone don’t make replay unclean.
tcp_gap_resetsint
Times a capture gap forced stream and discovery resynchronization.

Packets dropped by the capture backend.

Interface-level drops reported by the backend.

Packets rejected by a full live worker queue. Any nonzero count makes health unclean and requests a resource-limit stop.
flow_state_evictionsint
Least-recently-active TCP reassembly states evicted past the 64-flow limit. Any nonzero count makes health unclean.

Traffic, backend and retention counters

Candidate rollover

Discovery evaluates the retained window before evicting it, keeps compact best-partial evidence and warns. A non-complete result then suggests retrying while opening the leaderboard promptly.

classbdo_toolkit.grind

GrindSession

Confirmed mob drops plus optional profile-based Agris and solo XP, through one passive capture and one event stream.

status
experimental
standalone
LiveXPSession · LiveAgrisSession
items only
LiveCaptureSession
class
bdo_toolkit.grind.GrindSession(*, profile: OpcodeProfile, track_xp: bool = False, track_agris: bool = False, expected_maximum_points: int | None = None, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = None, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, )
YieldsGrindEvent via events()drops, enabled readings and reader failures · poll() is the timeout-aware alternative

Example

XP is solo-only

Party play can produce wrong XP readings, and the session neither detects groups nor identifies your character. Stop before switching characters.

One capture

Use this instead of the standalone sessions, never alongside them for the same features. It reads saved layouts only; fetching and calibration stay separate.

from bdo_toolkit import BDOEvent, load_opcode_profile
from bdo_toolkit.grind import GrindFeatureError, GrindSession
from bdo_toolkit.xp import XPReading

profile = load_opcode_profile("opcodes.local")
with GrindSession(profile=profile, track_xp=True) as session:
    try:
        for event in session.events():
            if isinstance(event, BDOEvent):
                print(f"DROP item {event.item_id} +{event.quantity}")
            elif isinstance(event, XPReading):
                change = "baseline" if event.delta_xp is None else f"{event.delta_xp:+,}"
                print(f"XP Lv {event.level} {event.percentage:.3f}% ({change})")
            elif isinstance(event, GrindFeatureError):
                print(f"{event.feature} disabled: {event.reason}")
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
print(session.status.status, session.health.capture_is_clean)
Example outputsynthetic · drops and solo XP, stopped with Ctrl+C
XP Lv 61 41.203% (baseline)
DROP item 16001 +1
XP Lv 61 41.210% (+1,240,384)
ready True

The first XP reading is a baseline, not a gain. The live_grind.py ↗ lesson adds Agris with --agris --agris-cap N.

Parameters

Sensitive

A recording holds private traffic and has no disk quota.

profile*OpcodeProfile
Loaded active profile with an inventory receipt layout and source context. Each enabled reader also needs its saved layout.
track_xpbool = False
Enable the saved-layout solo XP reader.
track_agrisbool = False
Enable saved-layout Agris balances, with no discovery fallback.
expected_maximum_pointsint | None = None
Your known Agris cap, a positive uint32. Required with track_agris=True, rejected otherwise.
live_optionsLiveCaptureOptions | None = None
Interface, local address, ports and bounded queues.
capture_secondsfloat | None = None
Optional finite, positive duration after readiness, enforced even while the consumer pauses.
save_pcapstr | Path | None = None
Opt-in new .pcap or .pcapng recording. Parents are created and files never overwritten; a failure can leave partial evidence.

Methods

One consumer

events() and poll() share one queue; a second concurrent consumer raises RuntimeError.

start()→ None
Starts one capture and waits up to 15 seconds for readiness. Single-use: construct a new session after any start attempt.
events()→ Iterator[GrindEvent]
Blocking iterator for the one consumer; ends after a clean stop and drain. Breaking out doesn’t stop capture.
poll(timeout=None)→ GrindEvent | None
One event. 0 checks without waiting; None waits. None back means a timeout or a drained, stopped session: check stopped. Drain regularly from a UI timer.
stop()→ None
Stops capture, drains accepted packets and closes the recording; buffered events stay consumable. Re-raises the first retained failure. Retry while cleanup_incomplete.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Raises the retained whole-session failure. Reader failures arrive as GrindFeatureError events instead.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter starts and returns the session; exit stops it. A raising block’s exception stays primary. There’s no async facade.

Attributes

statusGrindStatus

Current authority, including failed readers.

healthGrindCaptureHealth

Shared acquisition counters; read the final values after stop.

stop_reasonstr | None

requested, duration or error, after shutdown.

runningbool

Ready and running, with no whole-session failure.

stoppedbool

Shutdown and cleanup completed.

errorBaseException | None

First whole-session failure; reader failures don’t count.

cleanup_incompletebool

Release unverified — keep the session, retry stop().

endpointCaptureEndpoint | None

Resolved interface, local address and BPF filter, once available.

Raises 7 cases · construct → start → consume → stopShow detailsHide details

Reader errors are events

A recognized XP or Agris decode error becomes one GrindFeatureError and disables only that reader. Unknown exceptions aren’t swallowed.

Save with totals

Keep final status and health beside any saved application totals. Silence proves neither a current profile nor a live connection.

ExceptionWhenPhase
TypeError · ValueError · ProfileErrorWrong profile, switch or option type; a missing or extra Agris cap; an invalid duration or save_pcap suffix; an inactive profile, or a missing receipt, XP or Agris layoutconstruct
RuntimeError · TimeoutErrorA second start(), or startup not ready within 15 secondsstart
FileExistsError · backend exceptionsave_pcap already exists, or the capture backend failedstart
ValueErrorA poll() timeout isn’t None or a finite, non-negative numberconsume
RuntimeErrorPolling or stopping before start; a second concurrent consumer; stop() from the decoder threadany
CaptureIntegrityErrorA TCP gap, flow eviction, native drops, or a full packet or event queue. Raised ahead of buffered events, and again by stop()consume
retained failureAn unexpected decoder or cleanup failure, re-raised by stop(). If cleanup_incomplete, keep the session and retrystop

Retiring a connection, including the item pipeline’s idle expiry, invalidates a reader bound to it; a clean stop doesn’t. No kill counter, group identity, automatic character rebinding, initial balance hydration or combined replay is included.

GrindEvent

Not per kill

Delivery follows decoder order, not a timestamp sort or per-kill grouping; a frame reading can precede items from the same TCP segment.

type alias
bdo_toolkit.grind.GrindEvent = BDOEvent | XPReading | AgrisBalance | GrindFeatureError

A type alias, not a wrapper: dispatch with isinstance. Every member has to_dict().

BDOEventdrops
Only item_received from Mob Drop; previews and hydration are excluded.
XPReadingwith track_xp
A first-update baseline, then signed changes and single-level rollovers.
AgrisBalancewith track_agris
Remaining and maximum points; no inferred consumption or on/off state.
GrindFeatureErroronce per reader
An optional reader stopped for this session.

Earlier readings stay historical when a reader fails; current and final status take precedence.

GrindFeatureError

Ready isn’t proof

ready means no known failure, not that a drop was seen or the profile fits today’s patch.

Clean isn’t valid

LiveXPSession

Solo character level, XP balances and net XP changes, decoded with an explicit calibrated opcode profile.

status

bdo_toolkit.xp.LiveXPSession(*, profile: OpcodeProfile, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = None, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, )
YieldsXPReading via events()a first baseline, then each changed reading · poll() is the timeout-aware alternative

Example

Solo only

Party play can produce wrong readings. The tracker neither identifies your character nor detects a group: stop before changing characters or joining one.

Profile

Needs an installed profile with an xp section; users don’t calibrate XP. live_xp.py ↗ can fetch one first with --fetch-url.

from bdo_toolkit import load_opcode_profile
from bdo_toolkit.xp import SOLO_WARNING, LiveXPSession

profile = load_opcode_profile("opcodes.local")
print(SOLO_WARNING)
with LiveXPSession(profile=profile) as session:
    try:
        for reading in session.events():
            change = "baseline" if reading.delta_xp is None else f"{reading.delta_xp:+,}"
            print(f"Lv {reading.level} {reading.percentage:.3f}% ({change}) net {reading.net_xp:+,}")
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
print(session.status.status)

Lv 61 41.203% (baseline) net +0

tracking

The first reading is a baseline, not a gain. For a GUI, call poll(timeout=0) from a timer; the decoder keeps running on its own thread.

Parameters

Methods

One consumer

events() and poll() share one queue; a second concurrent consumer raises RuntimeError.

start()→ None
Starts passive capture and waits up to 15 seconds for readiness. Single-use.
events()→ Iterator[XPReading]
Polls until stopped and drained. An unchanged reading refreshes status without a duplicate update.
poll(timeout=None)→ XPReading | None
One ordered reading, or None on timeout or after the final drain. 0 checks without waiting. A stored failure is raised ahead of queued readings.
stop()→ None
Bounded native stop, accepted-packet drain and finalization; re-raises the first retained failure. Repeated stops are safe; retry while cleanup_incomplete.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Raises the first recorded failure. Readings already delivered stay historical; they don’t complete a failed total.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter starts and returns the session; exit stops it. A raising block’s exception stays primary, with cleanup failures added as notes.

Silence proves nothing

No matching XP message means either no XP traffic or an outdated profile. A plausible but wrong layout can pass the numeric checks; compare a new profile with the game UI.

A same-level character change on the same connection can’t be detected reliably. Restart for every character, and never treat this as group-safe. XP never enters the item BDOEvent stream.

The recording’s profile

Pass the layout for the patch the file was recorded on, not necessarily today’s.

Decodes solo XP from a saved PCAP or PCAPNG; nothing is ever sent to the game.

Example

from bdo_toolkit import load_opcode_profile
from bdo_toolkit.xp import replay_xp

profile = load_opcode_profile("opcodes.local")
with replay_xp("path/to/grind.pcapng", profile=profile) as replay:

XPReplay(path, *, profile, ports=…) takes the same arguments. It iterates once, exposes status and health, and supports close() and with; prefer with, especially for an early exit. The end of the file keeps the last observation, while an early close drops pending output without certifying the tail. I/O and decode failures raise and invalidate status. At most 4,096 readings wait unread; no full-file list is kept.

Not your starting balance

Setup

Needs the live-capture prerequisites. Discovery needs repeated decreasing balances, from mobs you kill yourself.

from bdo_toolkit.agris import LiveAgrisSession

with LiveAgrisSession(expected_maximum_points=100_000) as session:

        for balance in session.events():
