    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
print(session.status.status, session.detection_mode)

Example

Cancellation stops

Cancelling a pending poll() stops capture first, and keeps a balance it already took for the next call. Cancellation never makes partial discovery authoritative.

Setup

Needs the live-capture prerequisites. Discovery needs repeated decreasing balances.

import asyncio

from bdo_toolkit.agris import AsyncLiveAgrisSession


async def main() -> None:
    session = AsyncLiveAgrisSession(expected_maximum_points=100_000)
    try:
        async with session:
            async for balance in session:
                print(balance.remaining_points)
    finally:
        print(session.status.status)


try:
    asyncio.run(main())
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    pass

Discovery contract

A clue, not proof

A wrong cap can leave discovery unresolved, and the cap alone can’t rule out a structurally identical field. Inference is provisional; future patches can break its assumptions.

Without a profile, each session starts with no opcode or offset hints. Discovery searches same-connection, same-opcode, same-length families for your constant cap and a separate, non-overlapping uint32 balance column that repeatedly decreases. One qualifying layout must survive the settle interval: five decreasing values and three seconds by default, which doesn’t promise that five mobs are enough.

After qualifying, the latest balance is published, then every later valid value, including equal or higher ones; learning values aren’t backfilled. Competitor checks continue, and ambiguity withholds authority. An ended or changed selected connection invalidates the session, so start a new one to rediscover. Resource exhaustion or detected loss fails closed, and silence never means zero.

No consumption is calculated, because the balance before the first observed update is unknown.

AgrisLayout

Never saved

No discovered layout is saved, loaded or promoted automatically. Calibration writes an AgrisProfileLayout only on request.

calibrate_agris_and_update()

Explicit write

It updates only the Agris section, with a backup. Ctrl+C during capture cancels without saving, and a missing or changed profile is refused.

function
bdo_toolkit.agris.calibrate_agris_and_update( path: str | Path, *, expected_maximum_points: int, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, discovery_options: AgrisDiscoveryOptions | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = None, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, on_update: Callable[[AgrisStatus], None] | None = None, backup: bool = True, ) -> AgrisProfileUpdate
ReturnsAgrisProfileUpdatecalibration and save in one call · written or no-op

Checks the existing profile and snapshots its digest, cold-discovers (ignoring any saved Agris layout), finalizes, then calls the guarded writer. Item calibration is neither needed nor repeated.

Example

from bdo_toolkit import load_opcode_profile
from bdo_toolkit.agris import LiveAgrisSession, calibrate_agris_and_update

update = calibrate_agris_and_update("opcodes.local", expected_maximum_points=100_000)
print("written:", update.written)

profile = load_opcode_profile("opcodes.local")
with LiveAgrisSession(profile=profile, expected_maximum_points=100_000) as session:
    for balance in session.events():
        print(balance.remaining_points)

written: True
99364
99340

Use your confirmed cap. The agris_profile.py ↗ lesson does the same with --calibrate; without it, it tracks strictly from the profile.

modulebdo_toolkit.raw

Raw server messages

Every length-framed server-to-client message, opcode-free and undecoded, for protocol research. No opcode profile, decoding or decryption is involved.

status
experimental
decoded
replay_pcap()
since
1.0.8
contributed
@iSayZes in #10

Example

Nothing is interpreted

Flags and payloads are reported verbatim; the toolkit gives them no meaning. Opcodes can change with any patch.

As private as a PCAP

Every server-to-client payload byte is kept; treat a message dump like the capture itself.

from collections import Counter

from bdo_toolkit.raw import replay_raw

with replay_raw("path/to/session.pcapng") as replay:
    opcodes = Counter(message.opcode for message in replay)
    health = replay.health

for opcode, count in opcodes.most_common():
    print(f"0x{opcode:04X}  {count}")
print(health.messages_observed, health.capture_is_clean)
Example outputa synthetic nine-message capture
0x0A13  4
0x1C02  3
0x0B07  2
9 True

The replay needs no opcode profile and never touches the game. LiveRawSession streams the same messages live.

How messages are framed

Gaps don’t raise

Unlike every other capture API, a TCP gap or flow eviction is counted in health, not raised. Check capture_is_clean before trusting completeness.

Mid-stream

A capture that attaches mid-stream skips the bytes before the first proven boundary.

Every message from the selected server ports, in stream order per connection, is one frame of 5 to 65,535 bytes:

0–1u16 little-endian
length, the whole frame including this five-byte header.
2u8
flag, reported as received.
3–4u16 little-endian
opcode.
5…bytes
payload, possibly empty.

Framing waits for evidence of a boundary: two consecutive complete frames, or one exactly sized standalone frame. After a TCP gap it resynchronizes the same way, and messages accepted while resynchronizing aren’t verified. index keeps counting through a gap, while stream_sequence jumps, so the hole stays visible:

from bdo_toolkit.raw import replay_raw

next_byte = {}
with replay_raw("path/to/session.pcapng") as replay:
    for message in replay:
        key = (message.flow, message.connection_epoch)
        expected = next_byte.get(key)
        if None not in (expected, message.stream_sequence) and message.stream_sequence != expected:
            print(f"gap before message {message.index}: {message.stream_sequence - expected} bytes missing")
        if message.stream_sequence is not None:
            next_byte[key] = message.stream_sequence + message.length
    print("gaps counted:", replay.health.tcp_gap_resets)
Example outputa synthetic capture missing two 11-byte messages
gap before message 3: 22 bytes missing
gaps counted: 1

LiveRawSession

Queue size

Without live_options the event queue holds 16,384 messages. Your own LiveCaptureOptions brings back its 1,024 default unless you set event_queue_size.

Setup

Needs the live-capture prerequisites; no opcode profile.

class
bdo_toolkit.raw.LiveRawSession(*, live_options: LiveCaptureOptions | None = None, capture_seconds: float | None = None, save_pcap: str | Path | None = None, )
YieldsRawMessage via events()one consumer · poll() is the timeout-aware alternative

A single-use, passive live capture of every server-to-client message. It shares the lifecycle of the other observation sessions.

Example

from bdo_toolkit.raw import LiveRawSession

with LiveRawSession(capture_seconds=10) as session:
    for message in session.events():
        print(message.index, f"0x{message.opcode:04X}", message.length)
print(session.health.messages_observed, session.health.capture_is_clean)

Logins and zone loads arrive as thousands of messages per second; keep the consumer fast or write messages out in bulk.

Parameters

live_optionsLiveCaptureOptions | None = None
Interface, local address, ports and queues. None uses the defaults with a 16,384-message event queue.
capture_secondsfloat | None = None
Optional finite, positive duration after readiness.
save_pcapstr | Path | None = None
Opt-in new .pcap or .pcapng recording; never overwrites, no disk quota.

Methods and attributes

start()→ None
Starts capture and waits up to 15 seconds for readiness. Single-use.
events()→ Iterator[RawMessage]
Blocking iterator for the one consumer; ends after a clean stop and drain.
poll(timeout=None)→ RawMessage | None
One message; 0 checks without waiting. A stored failure is raised ahead of queued messages.
stop()→ None
Stops capture and drains accepted packets; re-raises the first retained failure. Retry while cleanup_incomplete.
raise_if_failed()→ None
Raises the retained failure now.
__enter__ · __exit__context protocol
Enter starts the session; exit stops it. A raising block’s exception stays primary.
healthRawCaptureHealth
Packet, message, gap and native-loss counters; read the final values after stop.
statusNone
Always None: raw capture has no reader state.
running · stopped · stop_reason · error · cleanup_incomplete · endpointlifecycle
As on GrindSession.

← Agris models and discoveryNext: Command line →

commandbdo-toolkit

Command line

The bdo-toolkit command installs a profile, decodes item events, and runs the Agris and Arena of Solare capture and replay commands.

status
stable
also
python -m bdo_toolkit.cli

Common workflows

Explicit profiles

replay and live require --profile, and decoding never fetches. Replay uses the recording’s matching-era profile.

Calibration

--qty 1 is the per-record value for the whole capture: deposit 1, deposit 4, then withdraw all 5. Follow the guided sequence.

# Install the latest maintainer-promoted NA/EU profile
bdo-toolkit profile fetch https://ychwu.github.io/bdo-toolkit-profiles/channels/na-eu/stable.json --output opcodes.local

# Watch live item events
bdo-toolkit live --profile opcodes.local

# Watch confirmed live additions to Heidel storage
bdo-toolkit live --profile opcodes.local --event-type storage_delta --storage-id 0x0020

# Decode a recording as JSONL, with its matching-era profile
bdo-toolkit replay path/to/session.pcapng --profile path/to/matching-opcodes.json --jsonl

# Replay worker additions delivered to Yukjo Street
bdo-toolkit replay path/to/session.pcapng --profile path/to/matching-opcodes.json --event-type storage_delta --source "Worker Production" --storage-id 0x058C --jsonl

# Calibrate after a patch, then write the profile
bdo-toolkit calibrate --item-id 15156 --qty 1 --write opcodes.local

# Find candidate capture settings on Windows, without a profile
bdo-toolkit diagnose-capture --json

Replace the capture and profile placeholders. Item ID 15156 is the guided calibration item.

Filter defaults

With no filter flags, replay decodes everything and live uses EventFilter.activity(). Any --event-type, --source, --storage-id or --item-id builds one explicit EventFilter instead: omitted criteria stay unrestricted, and the fields combine with AND. A storage-ID-only filter can also match snapshot records, so add --event-type storage_delta for live additions only. There’s no switch for EventFilter.all(); use Python for exhaustive live delivery.

Command reference

replay and live

Python

replay_pcap() · capture_live()

bdo-toolkit replay PCAP --profile PATH [filters] [--ports PORTS] [--jsonl]
bdo-toolkit live --profile PATH [filters] [--ports PORTS] [--jsonl] [--iface NAME] [--capture-seconds N] [--event-queue-size N]
--profile PATH*both
The local opcode profile to decode with.
--event-type · --source · --storage-id · --item-idboth · repeatable
Filters. Sources are exact labels such as "Worker Production"; storage IDs are decimal or 0x-prefixed.
--jsonlboth
One JSON event per line instead of console text.
--ports PORTSboth = 8884,8885,8889
Comma-separated server source ports.
--iface NAMElive
Capture interface; auto-detected by default.
--capture-seconds Nlive
Stop after N seconds; otherwise Ctrl+C.
--event-queue-size Nlive = 1024
Decoded events buffered for the consumer; not packet buffering.

profile fetch

Python

fetch_opcode_profile()

bdo-toolkit profile fetch URL --output PATH [--timeout SECONDS] [--max-bytes BYTES] [--no-backup]

Verifies and atomically installs one remote profile envelope. It never refreshes automatically, and decode commands never call it. Run one writer per output path.

URL*positional

calibrate

Failure timing

Ambiguous destination or count fields report CalibrationAuthorityError without a traceback. The incomplete-transfer gate runs only with --write, before the profile is read, backed up or created.

Python

calibrate_pcap() · calibrate_live() · update_profile()

bdo-toolkit calibrate --item-id ID [--qty N] [--action ACTION] [--pcap PCAP | --capture-seconds N] [--write PATH] [--merge]
--item-id ID*int
The known item’s decimal ID; use matching unstackables.
--qty Nint
Expected quantity in each record, normally 1. Omit it for a loot preview with a random quantity.
--action ACTIONchoice = auto
auto detects both transfer directions. storage-to-inventory and inventory-to-storage are strict; loot-preview is the separate optional calibration.
--pcap PCAPpath
Calibrate offline from a recording; omit it to listen live and press Ctrl+C after the actions.
--capture-seconds Nlive only
Stop the live window automatically. Combining it with --pcap exits 2.
--write PATHpath
Write the specs, replacing the applicable entries. Without it, the run is a dry run that prints what it found.
--mergeflag
Advanced · Keep and deduplicate existing entries instead of replacing them.
--min-confidence F0–1 = 0.80
Lowest accepted calibration confidence.
--ports · --iface · --verboseoptions
Server ports, the live capture interface, and printing rejected candidates with reasons.

Profile maintenance advanced

reset-profile replaces everything

It writes an empty active profile, dropping all specs. It’s a recovery step, not something to run after a successful calibration.

bdo-toolkit reset-profile PATH [--calibration-item-id ID]
bdo-toolkit origin-learn --profile PATH [--pcap PCAP]... [--candidates PATH] [--min-observations N]
bdo-toolkit origin-promote CANDIDATES --profile PATH [--min-observations N]
reset-profilereset_profile()
Writes an empty active profile. --calibration-item-id (default 15156) is metadata for the next guided calibration, not a claim that one ran.
origin-learnOriginLearner
Adds to the candidate file at --candidates (default opcodes.origin-candidates.json), from each repeatable --pcap or, without one, a live capture (--iface, --capture-seconds).
origin-promotepromote_origin_candidates()
Copies confirmed families from the candidate file into the profile, keeping its active flag. --min-observations overrides the file’s threshold.

diagnose-capture

bdo-toolkit diagnose-capture [--json] [--timeout SECONDS]

Inspects Windows BDO connections and suggests capture settings, without a profile. --json prints CaptureDiagnosis.to_dict(); --timeout (default 15) bounds the inspection. It exits 2 when inspection is unavailable and 0 otherwise, even with no game or connections.

Agris commands experimental

Not a starting balance

--cap is your known maximum. Output holds remaining and maximum observations only, never consumption or on/off state. Empty output means unavailable, not zero.

See also

Discovery limits · LiveAgrisSession

bdo-toolkit agris calibrate --profile opcodes.local --cap 100000
bdo-toolkit agris live --profile opcodes.local --cap 100000
bdo-toolkit agris live --cap 100000 --save-pcap grinding.pcapng --jsonl
bdo-toolkit agris replay grinding.pcapng --cap 100000 --jsonl

Replace 100000 with your confirmed maximum. With --profile, live and replay decode the saved layout strictly; without it, they cold-discover.

--cap POINTS*all · 1–4294967295
Your known Agris maximum; no default.
--profile PATHlive · replay · required for calibrate
Strict saved-layout decoding; a missing layout is an error. For calibrate, the existing profile whose Agris section is updated, with a backup.
--minimum-updates N · --settle-seconds Nall = 5 · 3
Distinct decreasing balances needed (at least 3), and the uniqueness interval.
--jsonllive · replay
One balance per stdout line; status and health stay on stderr.
--ports PORTSall = 8884,8885,8889
Server source ports.
--iface · --local-ip · --no-bpflive · calibrate
LiveCaptureOptions adapter, local IPv4 and Python-filter fallback.
--capture-seconds Nlive · calibrate
Optional positive deadline; otherwise Ctrl+C. Successful tracking doesn’t stop by itself.
--save-pcap PATHlive · calibrate
Opt-in new recording; never overwrites, no disk quota.
PCAP*replay · positional
An existing capture, read offline.

agris calibrate prints one AgrisProfileUpdate JSON object on success, with progress on stderr; item calibration stays separate.

Arena of Solare commands experimental

--quiet hides progress, not data

Without --output, stdout still gets the full result: names, rankings, Elo, outcomes and per-class records. Pipes and redirects keep it.

Data contract

The result is a serialized SolareCaptureResult; stderr progress follows SolareUpdateKind.

# Classify a saved load; JSON goes to stdout
bdo-toolkit solare replay leaderboard.pcapng

# Include opaque gear and addon sections as lowercase hex
bdo-toolkit solare replay leaderboard.pcapng --include-raw --output result.json

# Live: open the Leaderboard once after capture-ready appears
bdo-toolkit solare live --save-pcap patch-check.pcapng

# Keep listening after confirmation, for at most 60 seconds
bdo-toolkit solare live --keep-listening --capture-seconds 60
PCAP*replay · positional
The recording passed to replay_solare().
--output PATHboth
Write the result JSON here instead of stdout, creating parents. It can’t be the replay input or the --save-pcap file.
--include-rawboth
Keep validated opaque sections from both responses and include them as hex. Raw that wasn’t kept can’t be recovered without replaying a saved PCAP.
--ports PORTSboth = 8884,8885,8889
Server source ports.
--iface · --local-ip · --no-bpflive
PacketCaptureOptions adapter, local IPv4 and Python-filter fallback.
--capture-seconds Nlive = 120
Finite, non-negative deadline. Confirmation still stops earlier unless --keep-listening.
--wait-foreverlive
No deadline; completion, Ctrl+C or the backend ending still stop capture. Excludes --capture-seconds.
--keep-listeninglive
stop_on_complete=False: the first snapshot and its health stay latched while recording continues. The deadline still applies.
--save-pcap PATHlive
New .pcap or .pcapng recording; never overwrites, no disk quota.
--quietlive
Suppress non-terminal progress on stderr.

Structural discovery is always on. There’s no --discover flag, Solare opcode profile or trusted Solare opcode.

Output streams and exit status

Pipe-safe

Data goes to stdout and everything else to stderr, so --jsonl and Solare JSON pipe cleanly.

Commandstdoutstderr
replay, liveEvents, as console text or JSONLStatus, decoder diagnostics and errors, even when a filter yields no events
profile fetchNothingInstalled revision and path, any backup, errors
calibrateOne discovered … line per promoted spec; not a readiness verdictProgress, direction summary, diagnostics, write summary, errors
agris live, agris replayBalances, as console text or JSONLDiscovery status, capture health, errors
agris calibrateOne AgrisProfileUpdate JSON objectProgress, errors
solare replay, solare liveOne result JSON object, unless --outputProgress (live, unless --quiet), output confirmation, errors
origin-learnThe final candidate summaryProgress, save status, diagnostics, errors
reset-profile, origin-promoteNothingThe outcome, errors

Exit status

0success
Completed. For Solare, the result is complete; for Agris live and replay, the final status is tracking.
1no result
A valid request found nothing to keep: a non-complete Solare result (its JSON is still written), no calibration specs, no origin candidates, or nothing new to promote. For agris commands, also any I/O, integrity, configuration or runtime failure.
2rejected or failed
Argument parsing or validation, and outside agris, profile, I/O, runtime or direction-mismatch failures. Agris live and replay also exit 2 when discovery stays unresolved.
130interrupted
agris calibrate stopped with Ctrl+C; nothing is saved.
